# Changelog

Releases of TandemLLM. Speed numbers are the benchmark row `serve-single-i256-o256-v1` (one request at a time, 256 prompt tokens, 256 generated, thinking off, greedy), mean tok/s with the lookup store off unless noted. [docs/measurement.md](docs/measurement.md) explains the row. Every release produces the same text as the one before it, except where an entry says otherwise.

## 0.13.0, 2026-10-20

0.13.0 adds Ornith AI's Ornith-1.5-122B, from our EXL3 pack at 4.0 bits a weight. It is a Qwen3.5 mixture-of-experts model that reads images and thinks before it answers, and it drafts with its own MTP layer. On one DGX Spark it decodes 37.2 to 38.4 tok/s plain and 85.3 to 124.8 with the MTP layer and the lookup, and every drafted text is the plain run's. The release also carries the conductor's third round of tool-eval-bench work, room for the caches on Ornith, fixes for long Chat-tab sessions and a test runner that counts what each file ran. The other models write the same text as in 0.12.2 and keep their saved conversations: Flash-Next's, LFM2.5's and NemotronH's fingerprints change, and their first start adopts 0.12.2's files.

### Ornith-1.5-122B

Ornith-1.5-122B has 48 layers, 36 Gated DeltaNet and 12 gated attention (ENG-E15). Each layer has 256 routed experts, of which 8 run a token, and a shared expert. One more layer predicts the next tokens (MTP), a Qwen3.5 vision tower reads images, and the context is 262,144 tokens. About 10B of its 122B parameters run for each token.

- The Qwen3.5 MoE trunk, `engine/models/qwen3_5_moe` (ENG-383, ENG-391). It reads the config strictly and the EXL3 pack with its per-expert projections and mixed rates. The row step and the prefill run on Flash-Next's EXL3 kernels with one residual stream, and the row attention is dense at any context length. The router kernel now takes up to 512 experts. The reference forward matches transformers on tiny configs of both Qwen3.5 MoE shapes, and a cache restore on this trunk builds no sparse-indexer pool (the second call of every tool turn failed without it).
- One profile, `ornith-1.5-122b-exl3-4.0`. Our pack has every projection at 4 bits, the head at 6, the MTP layer at 4 and the vision tower at 6, 64.6 GB. exllamav3 1.6.2 converted it from the BF16 checkpoint at revision e09bc0dfbe, with a patch for 13 experts whose weights are all zero in fp16. The repository `0xBakeer/TandemLLM-Ornith-1.5-122B-EXL3-4.0` is public, pinned at 92f7483c, and sits in [one collection](https://huggingface.co/collections/0xBakeer/ornith-15-122b-exl3-for-tandemllm-6ad7ccf04f93a379ba434c4c) with the base model and the DFlash2 drafter. A download needs no token.
- Drafting: the MTP layer as a chain of 3 and the lookup in one tree, cut by StairCut from the pack's price file. After a round that StairCut cut to the anchor alone, the next 1, 2, 4, then 8 rounds take the plain step (`QWEN38_Q35M_ANCHOR_BACKOFF`). `QSE_ORN_HEAD=dflash2` drafts with incoai's DFlash2 drafter for Ornith instead, with its projections in NVFP4 and its head over the 32,768 most used tokens; the profile then fetches it (1.86 GB). The lookup keeps a suffix store of its own, since the tokenizer is not the Qwen3.8 one.
- Serving: one slot, a window up to 262,144 tokens, vision on with the pack's own tower (0.35 GB). The model thinks in a `<think>` block and calls tools in the XML form. Temperature 0.6, `top_k` 20 and `top_p` 0.95 come from its generation config. A start needs 93 GiB of free memory.
- Against the BF16 checkpoint's logits (`tools/q35m_quality.py`, 8 wikitext rows of 1,024 tokens): KL 0.139, top-1 86.2 %, perplexity 7.27 against BF16's 7.09. exllamav3's own forward of the pack gives KL 0.136 on the same rows.
- Against exllamav3 1.6.0's forward on the same pack, fed the engine's greedy tokens, the top token agrees at 498 of 512 positions (97.3 %, KL 0.027). Agreement is not exact. Of the 14 differences, 9 have a margin under 0.5 logits and one a margin over 4. The cause is not tested.
- Measured on one DGX Spark on 2026-10-20: one fresh server a row, greedy, thinking off, 512 new tokens on prompts of 3,146 to 4,165 tokens, one run a cell. The last column is a 2,048-token code answer (a game in one HTML file) through the raw path. Every drafted text is the plain run's.

| tok/s | prose | code | chat | edit | copy | 2,048-token code |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| plain | 37.6 | 38.4 | 37.8 | 38.0 | 38.1 | 37.2 |
| MTP layer + lookup (the profile) | 85.3 | 114.2 | 110.0 | 115.9 | 124.8 | 103.3 |
| DFlash2 + lookup | 67.3 | 91.7 | 92.2 | 106.9 | 122.8 | 96.8 |

- A start loads the pack in 65 s: the weights take 59.95 GiB, 61.16 with the MTP layer. [models/ornith-1.5-122b/measurements/0.13.0-summary.json](models/ornith-1.5-122b/measurements/0.13.0-summary.json) has the runs. Not measured: requests at once (a joint verify for side slots on this trunk is SRV-653), prompt reading speed, images, sampled decoding and repeat runs.
- tool-eval-bench on the 0.13.0 code, one run a row: 93 and 94 on the raw path at every thinking setting, 96 for the conductor's `tools` profile, 94 to 97 for the other conductor profiles, and 80 raw against 84 for the conductor in hard mode. [docs/tool-eval-bench.md](docs/tool-eval-bench.md#ornith-15-122b-on-0130-2026-10-21) has the rows.

### Caches

- Flash-Next, LFM2.5 and NemotronH adopt their 0.12.2 conversations (OPS-215). ENG-383's router change moved their fingerprints, since `tools/fn_kernels.py` is in their manifests. At 512 experts the router launches the same kernel with the same arguments as before, so a `SAME_ROWS` entry maps the new bytes to the old. Without it their first start on 0.13.0 would have swept every saved chat. The 27B's fingerprint does not change.
- The response cache keys on the effort level a request resolved to, the client's word and the router's level (SRV-645). `high` and `xhigh` render the same prompt and, at a 16,384-token limit, the same thinking cap after the answer reserve, so a raw `xhigh` tool-eval-bench run replayed 190 answers of the `high` run before it. The same request at the same level still replays.
- Ornith's caches have room (SRV-655). At the profile's first ceiling of 74 GiB every end anchor, stash, park and store snapshot was refused, and so was a 55k-token turn: 65.5 GiB was allocated against 74 less the KV pool's 6.5 and 2 of slack. The limits are now 86 and 90 GiB with a 2 GiB pin, and a long prefill gives caches back first. The trunk's prefill workspace is priced as its own, 2.75 GiB plus 32 KiB a token; Flash-Next's line had refused a 148k-token turn by 60 MB. A store decline names its reason: the entry cap, the budget, or the memory policy with its figures.
- A refused end alignment serves the part it aligned (SRV-657). When no pass aligns the whole copy, as when the parser rewrote a tool call, the rows up to the highest resident anchor in the part that matches token for token are served, and the turn resumes there. On Ornith such a turn had read 132,635 of 144,923 tokens again, from an early answer's whitespace. An image turn the end replay did not serve logs why.

### Tools

- `tools/teb_batch.sh` runs tool-eval-bench rows one at a time against one server and keeps what each ran under: the bench's and the server's versions, the pack, the slots, the cache settings, `/health` before and after, the response cache's hits during the row; `tools/teb_summary.py` prints the table and each miss with the grader's reason (OPS-209). The conductor rows send no profile header, so each request is resolved by what it offers, as a client meets it. [docs/benchmarks.md](docs/benchmarks.md#a-batch) has the commands.
- `tools/chat_trace.py` replays a recorded conversation through a `chatd` of this tree over the fake engine in seconds and checks that no write shows as a stub, requests only append, the bash status follows the exit code and a capped run ends idle; `tools/prefix_check.py` sends the requests it built to the live engine and reads what each one read again (SRV-667).

### Conductor

- A package whose result an offered tool delivers can stay out of the turn (SRV-615); shipped in shadow, it journals what it would keep out and changes no prompt. A package names its result in `deliverable`: write-message and formal-letter `send`; event-plan, weekly-schedule and checklist-builder `schedule`; social-post `post`. When one is about to go in on a request that offers a client tool whose declaration makes the deliverable (C5's reading of the tools), the class question's stages get one more question, done with one of these tools or the text itself; `tool` would keep it out, `text` puts it in ("draft an email to Sarah, I will send it myself" keeps write-message), and with no answer it would stay out. Without such a tool (Open WebUI's search tools, opencode's) nothing is asked; a forced function keeps it out unasked; the tool turns of the same message keep the decision; a pin wins. The journal row has `package_choice.kept_out` (or `shadow.tools.kept_out`), the counter `qse_conductor_package_kept_out_total`; the router's `tool_fit.deliverable` is `shadow` (shipped), `on` or `off`, and a stored packages document gets the field once (migration `2026-10-20-packages-deliverable`). On the DGX Spark with it on (2026-10-20, the chat profile, n = 1) tool-eval-bench's TC-03 passed, where the model had drafted the message with a placeholder for Sarah, and the score stayed 91: TC-47 and TC-51 failed, which passed on 0.12.0; the cause is not tested, so it ships in shadow. In shadow the side question still runs on the turns it would decide (one decision-model question, about 0.9 s on the Spark). The Packages screen shows the field.

### Tests

- New CPU tests for the Qwen3.5 MoE trunk: the config and the pack's layout, the reference against transformers, the row attention (Triton on a GPU, or the interpreter), the DFlash2 selector and its hot ids, and a cache restore on a tiny engine (`tests/test_q35m_*.py`). `test_the_ornith_card_is_the_raw_data` holds the card and the profile's pin to the summary (OPS-215).
- Every test file runs its tests as a script (SRV-661). Sixteen pytest-style files had no script entry, so on the box they ran nothing and counted as passed. `tests/scriptmode.py` runs a module's test functions with their fixtures, `tests/script_suite.py` fails a file that ran no test and lists a file that skips on purpose apart, and `ops/gate.sh` uses it.
- The fake backend and a test of SRV-639 describe the strict window as a strict OpenAI-compatible backend's and the relayed model as a `proxy` backend, not by another engine's name (OPS-211).
- `tests/test_grammar.py` passes run after run (SRV-647): it failed in most runs on 0.12.1 and 0.12.2 because the constraint's mask cache was keyed by `id()` of the grammar, and a grammar built after another was freed read that one's masks (a mask for a 97-token vocabulary on a 99-token one). Each grammar now keys its masks by a serial of its own, and a grammar replaced for another vocabulary drops its masks. On a box the same reuse could serve a wrong mask after the grammar cache replaced a grammar; no case was seen.

### Chat tab

- `grep` given one file's path searches that file line by line, where it answered "is not a directory"; a folder's files over 2 MiB are named as not searched instead of being counted as no match (SRV-649). The tool's description is unchanged, so no chat reads its prompt again.
- `read_file` reaches every line of a file over 4 MiB (SRV-651). It decoded the first 4 MiB of any file and paged inside them as if the file ended there: the window's last page promised nothing more and an offset past it came back empty. A large file is now read 4 MiB at a time from the line `offset` names, whole lines numbered as in the file, and the marker names the bytes after the page and the offset to read on from; a line longer than 4 MiB says so. Files up to 4 MiB read as before, and the schema is unchanged.
- A `write_file`'s content and an `edit_file`'s long texts stay whole in the requests after them until a fold point (SRV-659). Past 160k characters of whole texts, or at a compaction, the oldest leave the call down to 48k; the path stays, and the tool result says what left and how to read the file. A heredoc that writes a file folds the same way, with its output and exit code kept. Requests between fold points only append, so the engine's cache keeps them.
- Plan mode keeps the request's head (SRV-663). The tool list and the system block changed with it, so the turn into plan mode and the turn after Approve read the whole conversation again (84,423 tokens on Ornith). The request now keeps every tool, the run refuses all but the read tools and the todo list, and the plan rule goes into the plan turn's message. A library or sandbox tool check that times out keeps the last tool list.
- A run stopped at its 100-call cap leaves the chat idle with its Continue card, where the header and the rail said error (SRV-665). `render_page` keeps a shader error's compiler lines, which the 240-character clip cut after the first one.

Upgrade: run the 0.13.0 installer again (`--setup --force-setup` on a box installed with `--setup`, then `ops/use-profile.sh` with your profile; the same `--dir` otherwise), then `tandem restart` and `tandem chat restart`. For Ornith run `ops/use-profile.sh ornith-1.5-122b-exl3-4.0`; it downloads 64.6 GB.

## 0.12.2, 2026-10-20

0.12.2 fixes two Chat-tab bugs that users reported and the adoption of LFM2.5's older saved conversations. A run that reads a large file now ends with an answer instead of a request over the window (#18), and the port preview shows an app's Server-Sent Events and long-polls as they arrive (#86). No model, card or profile changed, and every profile writes the same text as in 0.12.1. `read_file`'s schema changes, so each chat's first request after the update reads its prompt again. A box that comes from 0.9.x to 0.11.1 adopts its LFM2.5 conversations again; a box that ran 0.11.2 to 0.12.1 already lost them.

### Chat tab

- A run that reads a large file no longer dies over the window (SRV-639, #18). One step's tool results share the room the model has left: half of what is left under the compaction line, 2,000 tokens at least, never past the window less twice the answer's room. `read_file` stops at whole lines and names the offset to read on from (a line longer than one read goes on with a new `column` argument); a 700 KB paragraph-per-line file came back as its first and last 16,000 characters and "[117 more lines]", with about 400 KB in between left out unsaid. Eleven 64,000-character results in one step were about 68 % of a 262,144 window. A request's estimate now carries a margin for the text the engine has not counted (#18's was 4,612 tokens low, with 256 left for it): at the edge our engine counts the request exactly (`POST /v1/tokenize`), a request counted over the window fails before it is sent, and a relayed model's `max_tokens` leaves the margin free. On the DGX Spark (Qwen3.8-27B, 262,144 tokens) the #18 repro with read-only tools, a 700 KB `.md` and "read it and summarize", ends with a summary; asked to read the whole file in one step, the model made 49 reads in 5 steps at 26,185, then 21,264, then 14,336 characters each, filled the gaps at the offsets the markers named, and peaked at 190,671 prompt tokens. read_file's schema changes, so each chat's first request after the update reads its prompt again. Reported by AgentSparko (issue #18).
- The port preview streams (SRV-633, #86). chatd held an app's whole answer until the app closed the connection, so a preview with Server-Sent Events or a long-poll never showed an event, the request's thread waited forever with a growing buffer, a client that left went unnoticed, and the sandbox counted as busy, out of reach of the idle stop. The answer now goes on once its head is read: an event stream, a chunked or until-close answer as it arrives, with no read limit; a sized one with a 60 s limit between reads. A page, script or style sheet up to 8 MiB is still read whole and rewritten; a bigger one passes unrewritten with `X-Tandem-Rewrite: skipped`. The app has 300 s to start its answer (else 504). A client that closes its connection, or takes no bytes for 60 s, ends the relay inside the sandbox and frees the sandbox; the engine's forward now closes its side to chatd when the browser leaves, also while chatd has nothing to send yet (a held long-poll ended in the sandbox within 0.2 s on the DGX Spark, where it ran until the app answered). Port lookups and probes end after 60 s or 4 MiB. Reported by joeynyc (issue #86).

### Caches

- LFM2.5 adopts the saved conversations of 0.9.x to 0.11.1 again (ENG-381). 0.11.2 changed two of its modules without changing a stored row (ENG-363: which joint decode graphs stay, and how the split attention sizes its partials) and gave them no equivalence entry, so 0.11.2 to 0.12.1 adopted none of the older files. The entries are in. On the DGX Spark the split attention at 1 to 32 rows, alone and with shared buffers, equalled 0.11.1's byte for byte (`tools/lfm_attn_rows_check.py`).

### Dashboard

- The dashboard's build uses source-map-js 1.2.2 (OPS-205, GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q). It is a build-time dependency under Vite; the served bundle is unchanged.

### Tests

- Three CPU tests that failed on 0.12.0 and 0.12.1 pass. `test_decider_api` expects the raw path's answer split as SRV-617 splits it (SRV-635), `test_proxy_http1_tls_fd` imports pytest only where it is installed (SRV-637), and `test_fp_same_rows` passes with ENG-381's entries. `tests/test_security_docs.py` checks SECURITY.md and docs/threat-model.md against the tree (OPS-202).

Upgrade: run the 0.12.2 installer again (`--setup --force-setup` on a box installed with `--setup`, then `ops/use-profile.sh` with your profile; the same `--dir` otherwise), then `tandem restart` and `tandem chat restart`.

## 0.12.1, 2026-10-20

0.12.1 serves the first community pack on Nemotron 3.5 Super VL: styles01's EXL3 pack at 3.5 bits a weight, text only, with LiLiCorr and the lookup from our 4.0 profile. A request with images now takes a side slot, the Chat tab's port preview keeps an app's redirects, and eleven pull requests from three contributors fix chatd, the Setup Guide, the GGUF reader and the image path. Every profile writes the same text as in 0.12.0; a request with images can run on a side slot, where it writes the tokens slot 0 writes. The NemotronH profiles' fingerprint changes (ENG-327, ENG-365, ENG-377), so the saved conversations of Bolt, Lightning and Super VL from 0.12.0 are not reused: their first request reads the prompt again. The 27B's and the other models' carry over.

### Nemotron 3.5 Super VL: a community pack

- Super VL is a community base (ENG-377). A pack on it is served as `community/<id>` with our EXL3 profile nearest in size, `nemotron-super-vl-exl3-4.0` for 3.5 bits: its limits, its sampler, NVIDIA's LiLiCorr drafter and the lookup, with the pack in place of the weights. `python -m server.setup.community check-pack community/<id>` checks a pack's files: a NemotronH config with 88 layers, EXL3, every shard, and the image tower when the entry lists images. [docs/community-weights.md](docs/community-weights.md#bases) has the rules.
- The first pack is `aitamedia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-EXL3-3.5bpw` at 358667cf (57.8 GB) by styles01 (pull request #63): routed experts at 3.5 bits, every other projection at 5, an fp16 head. It holds no image tower, so it serves text. `ops/use-profile.sh community/nemotron-super-vl-exl3-3.5bpw` downloads and starts it.
- NemotronH reads a stored head under a tied config. The pack's config, remapped from the Omni wrapper, says `tie_word_embeddings: true` and the pack stores `lm_head`; the loader now reads that head and notes it in the audit, where it refused the pack before. Without a stored head the embedding stays the head.
- Measured on the DGX Spark, 2026-10-20, one request at a time, 512 greedy tokens, thinking off, one run each: plain 25.9 tok/s; with LiLiCorr and the lookup, prose 33.2, code 53.9, chat 37.4, edit 99.0 and copy 112.3 tok/s (2.97, 5.38, 3.41, 15.5 and 16.0 tokens a block). Every drafted text is the plain run's. A cold 7,507-token prompt reads at 529 tok/s. The weights take 53.58 GiB at load, and the served profile (262,144 tokens, 3 slots) starts and answers in 110 s.
- Against exllamav3 1.6.0's own forward on the same pack, 8 prompts of 64 tokens: the top token agrees at 510 of 512 positions (99.6 %), both differences near ties, KL 0.0019. Images, requests at once and repeat runs were not measured.
- Plain decoding runs at 25.9 tok/s here and at 31.1 on our 4.0 pack (0.11.0). From the headers, a decode token reads 7.95 GB of this pack and 6.74 GB of ours. `models/nemotron-3.5-super-vl-120b-a12b/measurements/0.12.1-summary.json` has the runs and the card's numbers, and [docs/nemotron-h.md](docs/nemotron-h.md) the layout and the profile of a decode step.

### Parallel requests

- A request with images takes a side slot (SRV-629). On 2026-10-19 two Chat-tab agent runs carried 3 to 8 screenshots a request, and the router sent all 31 of their requests to slot 0: 56.6 min of wall time for 18.9 min of decoding, with slot 1 idle. Nothing but the routing kept them there. Each side slot is its own engine over the same weights, with its own image context and rotary offset. The router now expands each image to its rows on the host and keys them by the image's digest, as the caches do. Window, output cut and memory admission count those rows: a screenshot of 1,280 by 800 pixels is 1,000 rows. Slot 0's admission counts them too. Every continuation test reads the keys, from the resident rows to the NVMe. When the next turn moves to slot 0, slot 0 takes over a side slot's end kept after images with its rotary offset and image mark. A request with images is never a guest of slot 0. `QWEN38_SIDE_IMAGES=off` keeps images on slot 0, as 0.12.0. Super VL's tower stays on slot 0.
- Checked on the DGX Spark (the 27B, EXL3 6.0, `--parallel 2`, side window 262,144, side graphs off, KV pool on). One image request wrote the same 300 tokens twice on slot 0 and once on slot 1 beside a 6,000-token text run on slot 0, with no response-cache hit. Two image requests (2 and 3 screenshots, 2,000 tokens each, streamed) decoded together on slots 0 and 1 in 373 joint rounds. `/health` showed `decoding` [0, 1] in 118 of 140 samples. A text request alone took 105 to 109 ms a verify block in three restarts with the flag off and 108 ms in three with it on. Its tok/s moved between 69 and 129 in both arms with the tokens each block accepted; that spread was not traced.

### Chat tab

- The Chat view starts nothing when it closes during a sign-in (VIS-235). A sign-in that finished after the view was gone started the 10 s list poll, the global stream and the route's chat, and nothing stopped them. Its sign-in handler now takes the view's mount token before its first wait and checks it after each one, as the view's own start does since #85 (VIS-217). When the chat server stops answering as the view closes, no reprobe starts either.
- The port preview keeps an app's redirects inside the preview (SRV-631). An app on port 3000 that answered `Location: /login`, or `Location: http://127.0.0.1:3000/login`, sent the browser out of `/sandbox/ports/3000/`. chatd now puts the preview's prefix in front of a `Location` or `Content-Location` that is an absolute path or names the app's own address and port. External URLs, other ports and relative values pass as the app sent them.

### Setup Guide

- The dashboard keeps track of an install that Finish started when the user left the guide before the answer arrived (#34). Since #34 such an answer opens no install page, and the dashboard lost the job too: its engine restart showed as the engine being offline. The dashboard now keeps the job's id, as the install page does, so the restart shows as one and the dashboard moves to the guide while the engine is away. Nothing opens when the answer arrives.

### Contributions

- joeynyc, pull requests #78 to #85. chatd sends a text attachment it could not save instead of failing the send (SEC-1, #78), and measures the inline budget on the branch a message goes on, so an edit of an earlier turn gets its own room (SRV-487, #79). The port preview forwards the path as the client sent it, with its trailing slash and its escapes, and refuses one with a space or a line break (SRV-511, #80). The Setup Guide's remove checks for a running job under the job lock (SRV-560, #81). NemotronH's fingerprint counts `engine/vision.py` (ENG-365, #82), and an image 16 by 40,000 pixels gets a patch grid of at least one cell a side instead of a 400 (ENG-365, #83). The GGUF reader refuses tensor sizes that overflow 64 bits and an alignment that is not a power of 2 (ENG-327, #84). The Chat view opens no stream after it is gone (VIS-217, #85); the dashboard bundle was rebuilt for it (VIS-233).
- AgentSparko, pull requests #34 and #43. The Setup Guide clears its timers when it closes, drops a model's answer that arrives after a newer pick, and a Finish answer that lands after the user left opens no install page (#34, issues #4 and #5). chatd's sandbox reader closes its stream on every exit, an MCP server's body is capped at 4 MiB and each SSE line at 1 MiB, `read_file` reads 1 to 2,000 lines and promises no more lines past the end, and a negative limit on the conductor's journal routes reads 1 row instead of all (#43).
- James Aita (styles01), pull request #63: the Super VL community pack above.

### Engine

- NemotronH's manifest names each `engine/` module its files import: a listed one counts in the fingerprint, and `LEFT_OUT` gives the reason for each of the others (kvpool, capture_lock, config, the lfm2_moe package). `tests/test_tier_identity.py` fails on an import in neither list. The fingerprint does not change for it (ENG-379).

### Docs

- [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) says how to report a vulnerability in private and what is in scope. [docs/threat-model.md](docs/threat-model.md) says where untrusted input enters a running install and which parts matter most.

Upgrade: run the 0.12.1 installer again (`--setup --force-setup` on a box installed with `--setup`, then `ops/use-profile.sh` with your profile; the same `--dir` otherwise), then restart chatd: `tandem chat restart`.

## 0.12.0, 2026-10-19

0.12.0 serves API clients that offer tools through a profile of their own. An SDK, curl or an unnamed client that sends tools and names no profile gets `tools` (SRV-621): the prompt as the client sent it, token for token the raw path's, with the loop guards and the tool-call checks acting. A request with tools can ask for a JSON answer: the model's first answer token picks a tool call or the document (SRV-619). An answer that makes two or more changes outside the conversation in one turn is written again one call at a time (C5, SRV-623), and a key the model read in a tool result is masked where the answer repeats it (SRV-625). On the raw path a plain API client now gets the thinking in `reasoning_content` (SRV-617). On [tool-eval-bench](https://github.com/SeraphimSerapis/tool-eval-bench)'s 69 scenarios the raw path scores 92 with thinking off and 95 to 97 with it on, and the `tools` profile 95; in the bench's hard mode the conductor scores 91 against 84 for raw ([docs/tool-eval-bench.md](docs/tool-eval-bench.md)). No change touches the decoding of a request without tools and without a JSON format; the served text against 0.11.4 was not measured.

### Conductor and tool calls

- The `tools` profile (SRV-621, SRV-622). A request resolves to the `X-Tandem-Profile` header, else the profile mapped to its client kind, else, for a client kind no profile maps whose request offers function tools (`tool_choice` not `none`), `settings.tools_profile` (shipped `tools`, `""` turns the rule off), else the default profile. The journal says which rule picked it (`extra.profile_source`). `tools` asks no class question and adds no note, package, memory or effort change (`prompt: client`, `transcripts: off`); D1, D1b, D2, E1, C3, C4 and C5 act. A side class call cost 1.23 times the raw path's time on tool-eval-bench, so the profile asks none.
- Structured outputs with tools (SRV-619, SRV-620). `response_format` (`json_schema`, `json_object`) or `structured_outputs` beside tools under `tool_choice: auto` was a 400. The answer is now constrained to the product of the tool-call automaton and the document automaton. Where both are alive the mask follows the row's argmax before the mask: a call's first token commits to the calls, whitespace keeps both open, any other token commits to the document. The token taken fixes the side, so speculation changes no token. `tool_choice: none` is the document alone, `required` and a named function the calls alone. The log line `[structured] <id> branch=calls|document` and `extra.structured_branch` say which side won. `<tool_call>` and `</tool_call>` keep their own ids under this constraint. `--tool-format pythonic` keeps the 400.
- C5, one mutation per turn (SRV-623, SRV-624). An answer with two or more calls to tools that change something outside the conversation (send, schedule, create, write, delete, read off each tool's declaration, never its messages) is written again through C4's regeneration turn: the first call, its result, then the next. Cap 1; past it the calls go out as they are, journaled. Policy 8 adds the task: `tools` acts, `coding`, `chat-app`, `hermes` and `chat` journal in shadow, `general` and `overnight` have it off. A stored monitor document gets it with `tools/monitor_migrate.py --put http://127.0.0.1:8000 --tasks C5`.
- The secret echo mask (SRV-625, SRV-626). A secret that a tool result showed the model (an API key, a bearer value, a password assignment, a PIN) is masked where the answer repeats it verbatim as a whole word: `sk-abc123` becomes `sk-[redacted]`. The answer is never read for shapes, so a span no tool result held is never masked, and call arguments are untouched. Profile key `secret_mask` (`off`, `shadow`, `on`): on in `tools`, `coding`, `chat-app` and `chat`, never in `raw` and `bench`. `extra.secret_mask` counts each kind, never a value.
- The raw path gives a plain API client the thinking in `reasoning_content` (SRV-617, SRV-618). An SDK, curl or unnamed client on `X-Tandem: raw` got the thinking inline as `<think>...</think>` in `content`, and tool-eval-bench's exact-answer scenarios read it as the answer (TC-22, TC-24). Stop strings are matched on the answer. Every other client kind on the raw path keeps the server's format, and a request that names `reasoning_format` keeps it.

### Server, proxy and chatd

- `/v1/models/{id}` asks for the key `/v1/models` asks for, before any lookup (SRV-603).
- The standalone proxy times out a request phase after 60 s with nothing sent (`--idle-timeout`, `TANDEM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_S`); no answer has a timeout (SRV-605).
- chatd compacts and retries once on a 400 that says the request is over the window, when the compaction cut something (SRV-607, #18).
- An operator sets a relayed model's output limit under Backends (VIS-227, #21).
- CI fails when the committed dashboard bundle differs from its source (OPS-185); the chatd tests pin the sandbox environment before any module imports chatd (OPS-183).
- Fixes by AgentSparko in pull requests #36, #46, #47, #49, #50, #51, #53 to #61, #64, #67, #70, #71 and #73 to #76: the conductor's journal writer, session pages and number params; the collectors' baselines, joins, tokens and stale cards; the proxy's TLS sockets and model cards; the sandbox relay's sockets; chatd's `finish_guard` and MCP draft tests; stale responses in the dashboard's params, chat and setup pages; one long-task budget in the e2e suite.

### Docs

- [docs/benchmarks.md](docs/benchmarks.md) says how to run tool-eval-bench against TandemLLM and which settings a score must name (OPS-189). [docs/tool-eval-bench.md](docs/tool-eval-bench.md) has the 2026-10-19 results: the raw path at five thinking settings, four conductor profiles and hard mode.

## 0.11.4, 2026-10-18

0.11.4 adds Agents mode to the Chat tab (VIS-E15): with the chat setting `agents` on, the main agent talks with the user and plans, and gives every file write and every multi-step build or fix to a worker with the `task` tool, so the file texts live in the worker's context and go with it. A Task card shows each worker's run and report, and the Context panel shows each running worker apart, with its live figures. The engine keeps a worker's rows and its parent's while they take turns (ENG-371): in the live checks of 2026-10-18 no worker call after the first started from 0, and both parents came back from the NVMe. File texts stay out of a chat's requests, a compaction cuts to under half its trigger, a memory refusal compacts the chat instead of failing the run, and a run on a cloud model takes no run slot. Agents mode is off by default; with it off, chatd's requests are those of chatd-fold byte for byte (`tests/chatd_replay.py`). The engine's new restores copy rows it computed before, from the park or the NVMe, and compute none; a request with images can now resume at the end anchor, as a text request already did. The tests hold every such resume's logits to a cold prefill's within 1e-4 (`tests/test_worker_cache.py`, `tests/test_mm_end_anchor.py`); the served text against 0.11.3 was not measured.

### Chat tab

- Agents mode (VIS-E15, SRV-579): a chat setting, `agents`, off by default; the composer's agents chip and the settings switch (this chat, and the default for new chats) set it, and in a chat with messages they first say how many tokens the next message reads again (`reread_tokens`). With it on the main agent gets a `task` tool {title, brief, expect}. Each call starts a worker: a full run on a conversation of kind `task` under the chat, whose first request holds the worker's instructions (`packages/system/workers/PACKAGE.md`), the worker tools, the task, its brief, expect, the chat's todo list and the user's message that started the run, and nothing else of the chat. The worker runs in its parent's run slot, with the chat's sandbox, workspace, settings and rules, its own session `chat-<chat>-task-<n>`, `X-Tandem-Worker: 1`, `X-Tandem-Parent-Session` and `X-Tandem-Memory: off`. One task a step, 8 a run, depth 1, 40 calls a worker. Task conversations stay out of the list, search and titles, and go with the chat on delete. The chat-app store moves to v8 (`conversations.kind`, `parent_id`, a `tasks` table); `GET .../tasks` and `.../tasks/{id}`.
- The main agent in Agents mode reads and delegates (SRV-583): read_file, glob, grep, web_search, web_fetch, render_page, present, the library, todo_write, task and the chat's MCP tools; bash, write_file and edit_file answer "not available in Agents mode: give this to a worker with task". Its read_file returns at most 200 lines or 12,000 characters and says where it stopped, every result is cut at 12,000 characters, and a read, grep or glob that repeats one the request still carries, with no worker run and an unchanged workspace since, answers "unchanged since call <id> (step <k>)".
- A brief and a report are contracts chatd checks (SRV-581). A brief needs its Goal, Files, Constraints and Check lines, a title of at most 80 characters and an expect, and carries no code (a fence, more than 4 tags, more than 8 lines that look like code, minified code or a "CODE:" block); otherwise the call is refused with the template and no worker starts. The brief has no length cap: a cap of 3,000 characters made the main agent cut requirements. The worker's last answer is parsed into a report; a report that misses a field goes back once, and chatd builds it from the record when it misses it twice. At its call cap a worker makes one report-only call and the task ends partial. Below each report chatd's check lists the files the task changed with line counts, changed files the report left out, the render_page and bash calls that ran, claims with no call behind them, and the screenshots. The main agent reads at most 8,000 characters of it; the whole report is in `/workspace/.tandem/tasks/<n>/report.md`.
- Stop, a steer, Continue and failures reach the worker (SRV-585). Stop ends the task cancelled with chatd's check. A message queued while a worker runs is the main agent's steer, and the worker reads it as a note on its next tool result. A worker cut off (the engine away, the sandbox failing, a chatd restart) leaves the task and its parent interrupted, and Continue goes on in the worker first, then in the parent; a call that was running at the stop is never run again, and the model reads that its effect is unknown. A 4xx fails the task with a report that says why.
- A `task` call is a Task card (VIS-217): the task's number and title, a status chip in words, call k of max, tokens in and out, the time, the Now line while it runs and the summary once it ended. Opened, it shows the brief, the parsed report, chatd's check, the screenshots and the worker's transcript; on a phone the transcript is a sheet. Stop on the card stops the run, and an interrupted task offers Continue. A reload or a second device loads the tasks, then a running task's transcript.
- The Context panel shows each running worker in a section of its own (VIS-219, SRV-579): its context bar and split, its call of max, its cache tier and its Now, the prefill's bar with done/total, tok/s, the time left and the cached rows, or tok/s, the first token, tokens per round, acceptance and thinking. The main window is titled "Main agent" and reads "waiting for Task 1" while it waits; "Last worker: Task 2, 51,204 tokens, done" stays until the next task, and a turn with workers reads "main 31,204 · workers 2 (96,410) · total 127,614 prompt tokens". The Now dock lists a row a worker. chatd takes each worker's figures from the engine's live row of its session, once a second (`task.metrics`, `context.workers`).
- File texts stay out of a chat's requests. A finished write_file's content, and an edit_file's old or new text over 2,000 characters, go to the model as a stub (path, lines, bytes, sha256, the read_file call that shows it) from the next request on; a read_file or bash result over 4,000 characters stays whole until a compaction and is a stub after it. The store keeps every text. A write of a stub is refused, and edit_file's not-found error says to read the file again. One run on 2026-10-17 grew from 25k to 162k tokens in 50 minutes of write_file, edit_file and read_file steps.
- A worker's write_file and edit_file arguments go back whole until a compaction stubs them, as long read_file and bash results do; the chat's own writes are stubs from the next request on (SRV-593). A stub inside a worker's last answer parted its request from the engine's rows, and the next call read that answer again (681 to 8,690 tokens).
- A compaction tries its cuts from shallow to deep and takes the first whose request lands under half the limit that set it off; before, a compaction at 162k tokens kept three steps of whole shader and JS texts, landed at 138,673 and read 131,505 tokens again. The log line and the compactions row give the request size before and after: `[compact] <conv> <before> -> <after> (summary call <n> tokens) in <ms> ms`.
- A memory refusal compacts the chat and the run goes on. The refusal is retried once after its Retry-After, then the conversation is compacted and the smaller request sent, and the guard compacts the chat at 80 % of the refused request from then on. A run at 215,247 tokens, under 80 % of its 262,144 window, was refused for memory on every call while another chat ran, and ended interrupted after 10 minutes of retries. The Context panel counts a run compacted mid-way and continued from its own last call.
- A run on a cloud model takes no run slot: its calls run at the provider. A chat on DeepSeek waited "for a free run slot" while two chats on the engine held both.
- Tool screenshots are append-only: a chat keeps all up to 8, then the first 7 and the newest, so the prompt no longer changes where an earlier screenshot sat (SRV-546). The Now line names a long re-read with the engine's reason.
- `render_page` says which graphics APIs the check browser has: "WebGPU: not available in the check browser (WebGL2 only): a page with a WebGPU path was not checked on it". Chromium in the sandbox gets a WebGPU adapter in software but presents no canvas with it, so a WebGPU page was only ever checked on its WebGL2 fallback.
- A `finish_run` that raises can no longer wedge a conversation: chatd forces the run's terminal state, frees the conversation and drains its queue (pull request #41 by NotMainstream).
- chatd's store releases its lock when `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` fails; a second writer past the busy timeout leaked the lock and every later transaction deadlocked (pull request #14 by NotMainstream).

### Caches and parallel requests

- A request with images resumes at the end anchor (SRV-546). The end anchor's replay and alignment ran on text only, so a chat's first screenshot parted from the rows at the first trimmed tool parameter and resumed at a grid anchor far below. Replay and alignment now run on the expanded key ids, an end or NVMe entry kept after the same images is offered, and the router's in-context stage of a turn with images resumes the same way. `QWEN38_MM_END=off` serves such a request from the grid, as in 0.11.3. A re-read of 8,192 tokens or more logs where it resumed and why.
- An agent's worker is never a guest (ENG-371). A request with `X-Tandem-Worker: 1` or `X-Tandem-Parent-Session` becomes its slot's conversation on slot 0 or a side slot, never waits for a side slot, and a new worker takes a free side slot first when slot 0 holds its parent. Live on 2026-10-17 a worker's first three calls (2,532, 5,764 and 7,925 tokens) each read their prompt from 0 beside a 24,200-token chat, and one wrote over the parent's rows.
- A parent is kept while its worker runs. For 600 s after a worker's last request (`PARENT_KEEP_S`) its parent's rows go to the NVMe rather than away, from a side slot before another session's prefill cuts them and from slot 0's park before the memory policy takes it; a worker's own rows on a side slot do the same. A returning parent, and a worker's call that continues slot 0's rows, try slot 0 first and wait for it up to the time a re-read would take, 60 s at most.
- A conversation that ran on a side slot is carried into slot 0 at its first screenshot instead of reading its prompt again, and a parked end kept after images serves the next request whose key ids hold every row up to it.
- A park swap parks the longer conversation whole: the park's buffers grow to it within `--resident-park-gb`, else it goes to the NVMe first. A conversation the park refuses, an NVMe restore's victim and a park a safe shed or a side slot's gate cannot write go to the NVMe, not away. The NVMe keeps one entry a session, and a park's write never replaces the entry a restore reads next or a newer one.
- The sandbox's memory release (`POST /v1/cache/release`) frees a kept park, written to the NVMe when the engine is idle; the KV pool's last reclaim level, `kept_park`, frees it unwritten, so neither a release nor a page gate is refused for it. A swap commits every view's pages before a row moves, and the memory gate does not give back the end anchor its own request resumes at (`end_hold`).
- A side slot's NVMe write holds the capture lock: one ran while slot 0 captured a verify graph, and slot 0's request ended in an error (`cudaErrorStreamCaptureInvalidated`).
- A prefill has a rate on the live row from its first progress mark, and a layer-major window has one while it runs (SRV-591): a worker's re-read of 5,057 tokens showed 2,048 / 7,105 without a rate for six seconds. The window's layer marks are CUDA events the prefill's thread records between layers; `engine/model.py` is unchanged, so no stored row's fingerprint moves.

### Proxy, setup and tools

- The proxy closes a socket whose TLS handshake failed; each failed request to such a backend leaked one fd (pull request #38 by NotMainstream).
- The Setup Guide's reset holds the job lock across its re-check and its deletes, so a reset and an apply cannot run at once (pull request #40 by NotMainstream).
- `tools/prefill_reuse_e2e.py` runs a long chat with screenshots and a parallel chat against the engine and counts each turn's new tokens as the engine read them (SRV-547).

Upgrade: run the installer again, then `tandem restart` and `tandem chat restart`. chatd's store moves to v8 in place at its first start. Agents mode stays off until a chat or the new-chat default turns it on.

## 0.11.3, 2026-10-17

0.11.3 hardens the Setup Guide: `tandem doctor` checks an install and repairs what is safe, a check before the restart stops nothing when the new setup cannot start, the scripts call each other through `bash`, and a failed step says what broke, with Retry and Copy diagnostics. A restart is one card with the load's phases, a finished install has its own screen, and the Setup Guide removes a model's weights. Super VL reads images, a cloud model's turns in the Chat tab have their speed, cache and cost, and Performance and Usage keep the engine's requests apart from relayed ones. A conversation stays on the slot that holds its rows, the decider Laya fits beside Super VL, the narrator is off by default, and a chat sandbox has 4 GiB of memory. Requests on the raw path write the same text as in 0.11.2; under the conductor a turn can get packages it did not get before (SRV-534, SRV-536, SRV-552), and its text changes with them.

### Install and the Setup Guide

- Our scripts call each other through `bash`, never through the execute bit: `ops/use-profile.sh` (start.sh, stop.sh), `ops/watchdog.sh`, install.sh's calls of `bin/tandem` and its systemd unit (`ExecStart=/bin/bash DIR/bin/tandem start`), and the documented cron lines. A Setup Guide install failed at "Restart the engine" after 1.4 s with `ops/start.sh: Permission denied`: a deploy had written start.sh with mode 644. `tests/test_no_exec_bit.py` fails on a new direct call in the scripts, the Python code's subprocess calls, the units and the documented command lines (OPS-167).
- The install page shows a job's true end within seconds of the engine's return (VIS-211). The job stream's catch-up gave the job snapshot the id of the log line before it, and the page, which had counted that id, dropped the snapshot as a repeat: with no job in hand it dropped every later step and the done event too, and a finished install showed "Step 8 of 8, Installing" and the spinner "Starting the install" for good. The snapshot carries no log line's id now, the page dedupes log lines only, and a page with no job, a stream that ends or an engine that answers again reads the job by id. After 30 s without the job the page says it cannot read it, with Try again and Refresh. A finished install has its own screen: "<model> is ready", the weights, the tools, the parallel chats and their windows, how long it took, Start chatting and Back to the Setup Guide; the log and the steps fold under it. A tool that waits for memory reads "loads later, when memory frees up; nothing to do" (the planner's reason stays in the log). The dashboard's update banner no longer shows while a setup job runs or the engine is away, reads "The dashboard on the box was updated", and a waiting update loads at the finished screen's Start chatting. The install step no longer waits for the model's card, which cannot load during the restart.
- The status responder (`ops/engine_status.py`) belongs to its tree: `GET /_tandem/status` names its tree, status file, release and address, and `ensure` replaces a responder of another tree or an older release (found by its socket when it has no such route) and leaves any other program alone. During a Setup Guide restart on 2026-10-17 the page got a responder of another checkout, started the day before, which read that tree's status of 2026-10-15 ("TandemLLM is stopped: switching to Nemotron 3.5 Bolt") and answered the job's route with 404 ("This install and its log are no longer on the box"). A reason older than 6 h is no longer shown, and a start or stop that should long be over reads "not answering" (OPS-173).
- The responder carries a Setup Guide restart (OPS-175): the setup job as the server streams it (SSE or JSON, from the tree's `run/setup-jobs`), and `GET /v1/setup/status` with the engine's facts, the job's step n of N and the load's phase read from the engine log (weights, drafters, warm-up, verify graphs, the port). The server answers the same route while it runs, `/health` carries `status_port`, the read-only routes answer any origin, and the responder listens where the engine does. install.sh sets `QSE_STATUS_PORT` (the API port + 9), so every installed box has one. The fake engine's `--fake-load-s N` writes the load's phases over N seconds before it listens.
- A restart under a Setup Guide install is one card (VIS-209): "Restarting the engine with <model>", the job's step n of N, the load's phases (weights, drafters, warm-up, verify graphs, the port, with the weights' last progress line), the time taken and about how long is left, and a bar. The card asks `/v1/setup/status` every 2 s, of the engine, else of the status responder through the reverse proxy or on its own port (`status_port`, remembered from `/health`); with nothing to ask it counts the time against a typical start, and far past it says so with a refresh. The job this browser follows is kept in localStorage, so a refresh, a page the service worker served while the engine was away, or a view that went offline goes back to the Setup Guide's job and its card; the pill reads "restarting" instead of "offline", and the restart and offline banners, the update banner and the setup page's route errors stay away. When the engine answers, the card goes and the job's end shows (VIS-211).
- `tandem doctor` checks an install and repairs what is safe (OPS-171): file modes against `ops/executables.txt` (the release's executable files, kept equal to git's), the `run/ops` copies and `bin/tandem`, stale pid files of the engine and chatd, a hold's pause left behind, the setup marker's address, and the secrets file's mode (600). It reports what it does not change: a `run/ops` copy that differs from the checkout, a `serve.env` that does not load and its line, an interpreter that does not run, a secrets file where the engine does not read it, too little disk for a download. It runs before every `tandem start` and in every Setup Guide install's check step (the job keeps its report as `doctor`), and as `tandem doctor [--check] [--json]` or `python -m server.setup.doctor`; each run is logged in `logs/doctor.log`.
- A Setup Guide install checks what the restart needs before anything stops (OPS-169): a step of its own, "Check the new setup before the restart", between the download and the configuration. The scripts the switch runs are there and parse, `serve.env` with the new profile and the overlay the job will write sources under `set -u` as `start.sh` sources it, the weights are complete (the hub manifest's sizes too), MemAvailable and what the running engine gives back cover the profile's need (`MEM_NEED_GB`, as `use-profile.sh`), the new port is free, no box lock or hold, and the engine's and chatd's interpreters run. A failure ends the job there, says what is wrong in plain words and "Nothing was stopped or changed"; the running setup keeps running. Before, a start script without its execute bit was found only after the engine had stopped.
- A failed Setup Guide step says what broke in plain words (VIS-213): "the script start.sh could not be run (Permission denied: it lost its execute bit). tandem doctor has repaired its file mode; press Retry." instead of "the new setup did not start (ops/use-profile.sh exit 1)"; a hold, too little memory, an engine that did not answer in time (with its log's last line), a download that stopped and a time-out have their own sentences. The failed and rolled-back screens show the step it stopped at, what tandem doctor repaired, Retry from that step and Copy diagnostics. `POST /v1/setup/jobs/{id}/retry` starts a new job from the failed one's selection (`retry_of`; the check runs again, a finished download is not repeated); `GET /v1/setup/jobs/{id}/diagnostics` gives the job as text (versions, steps, tandem doctor, the selection, the last 200 log lines, no secret), which the page copies, or shows to select where the browser does not let it copy. The check step's change count shows once.
- The Setup Guide removes a model's weights (SRV-560, VIS-215). The weights step lists the weights on the box with their sizes (`GET /v1/setup/weights`; the running one marked, the shared drafters and base listed apart), and Remove asks first with the GB it frees and the line that downloads them again. `POST /v1/setup/remove` never removes the running profile, a folder a kept profile shares, or a folder outside the home folder and the Hugging Face cache, holding the installation or what something else reads; the review step can remove the old weights once the new setup answers (`remove_after`). Each removal is a line in `run/weights-removed.txt` with the repository at its revision and the fetch command. A download that does not fit names the GB too few and the weights that could be removed.
- A release gate for the Setup Guide (OPS-177), mandatory before every release (docs/operations.md, "Release checklist"): `tools/release_gate_setup.sh` installs the candidate twice on the box with `install.sh --setup` into scratch folders, beside the live engine and without touching it (spare ports, no chatd, the CPU fake engine with a load of 20 s, a few KB of stand-in weights, a HOME of its own, an interpreter copy the live box's `ops/engines.sh` does not count). Run A applies a profile through the Setup Guide's API while WebKit at 390 px follows the job in the Playwright container: the restart card during the restart, the finished screen with Start chatting within 10 s of the engine answering, screenshots; then the job, `/health`, a chat and a remove. Run B strips the execute bit from `start.sh`, `stop.sh` and `use-profile.sh` first and must still install. Its report and screenshots go to `results/gate-setup/<utc>/`.
- `ops/start.sh` asks `/health` every 2 s instead of every 10 s (600 s in all, as before), so a start, and an install's job with it, goes on within 2 s of the engine answering; a setup-mode start no longer counts as a model start in the status file's typical start, which made the next restart promise "any moment now". The dashboard's CSP admits the status responder's port (`connect-src ... http://*:<QSE_STATUS_PORT>`) and the responder answers a browser's preflight on its read-only routes, so a page with no reverse proxy in front reaches it (VIS-209, VIS-211).
- A Retry follows the new job from its first state: the page kept the failed job, final, over every event of the retry. A page that re-reads a finished job by id still reads its log to the end, and a job's last event before done carries its steps, the ones that did not run skipped (VIS-213). The release gate's browser part now fails the first try at the preflight, checks the failed screen and Copy diagnostics, presses Retry (no download), and removes a profile through the weights step's Remove button and its confirmation (OPS-177).

### Chat tab

- Super VL's card says vision, so the Chat tab sends it the chat's images: uploads in the user message, the newest tool screenshot in its tool message (VIS-205).
- The Context panel lists the prompt's images as a part of their own, the engine's count, out of the conversation's share (VIS-205).
- A run that builds or changes a web page or app checks it in a browser before it ends. When the model's answer would end the run and web files changed since its start (the run's snapshot, so files written by bash count), chatd loads the page it presented, the project's running dev server or the changed page in the sandbox's headless Chromium at 1280 and 390 px with the laya kit's page check, as a call of its own (a `verify` card with a `harness` badge, the Now line "Verifying the app ..."). The model reads the console errors, failed loads, visible text, controls, the page's state hook, overflow and the screenshot's brightness and colours, and the 1280 px screenshot when it reads images, then fixes what is wrong or answers. A page that needs its dev server with none running gets the command instead. At most two checks a run, a second only after more changes; a sandbox failure counts in the run's failure streak (SRV-526). The answer ends with a "Checked / Not checked" block from the run's evidence: the checks, whether the model saw the screenshot, its own render_page, preview and kit calls, and files changed after the last check; with no sandbox, the step limit reached or a check that could not run, it says not verified and why. The chat setting `verify` (on by default, a switch in the composer's tools menu) turns it off. Before, a run that built a Three.js scene said it was done from a count of colours in a screenshot, and tested it only when asked (SRV-532).
- A cloud model's turn has its figures (VIS-207). chatd measures the stream itself: tok/s, the first token's wait and the thinking tokens live (a text chunk is a token on DeepSeek: 320 chunks for 321 tokens; a tool call's arguments count 3.5 characters a token), then after each call the provider's usage over the stream's span, DeepSeek's `prompt_cache_hit_tokens` as the cached tokens, and the proxy's price as `cost_usd`, shown in the line under the answer and the Context panel's usage. The proxy's live row of a relayed call counts no tokens, and chatd took its zeros over its own counts: a DeepSeek turn read 0 thinking through a minute of thinking and "not tracked for this model" for its speed. The Context panel says what is true for a cloud model: "no drafting (cloud)" for tokens per round and acceptance, "the provider decides" for the thinking budget, "cached by the provider" for the cache, the system prompt, tool schemas and skill index as chatd's estimate ("est."), the window from the model card (1,048,576 for DeepSeek V4) and the answer's room as a request asks for it (393,216, or what the window has left). The Now section shows the first token's wait for every model.
- A library text that downloads the laya kit (laya-playtest) gets the kit copied into the chat's files (`/workspace/.tandem/`) and a line that says so: the sandbox cannot reach TandemLLM's address, so the download failed. Its `page` check runs in the sandbox; the modes that ask Laya for each move do not (SRV-532).
- `render_page` reports the page's console only: Chromium's own pages (chrome://, "Slow network is detected"), its service errors (GCM registration) and its GL driver lines are dropped, the line keeps the message and its source without Chromium's process and clock, and WebGL runs through SwiftShader by name (`--use-angle=swiftshader --enable-unsafe-swiftshader`) instead of the deprecated automatic fallback and its notice. Every render of the 2026-10-16 pagoda chat said `console:` over eight lines of which none was the page's (SRV-538).
- A new chat's run may make 100 model calls before it stops for Continue (`max_steps`, 50 before); a chat's own value stays. The pagoda replay of 2026-10-17 wrote its 15 files in 22 calls and stopped at 50 while it fixed its first errors, before any check (SRV-544).
- The verify phase loads a page that loads module scripts from its own folder (`<script type="module" src="js/main.js">`) through the HTTP server that runs from that folder in the sandbox, not as `file://`, where Chromium refuses the modules (CORS) and the page stays blank; with no such server the check says so and how to serve the folder. Inline pages load as files as before (SRV-548).
- `render_page` on a port takes a workspace path below the server's folder as the path it serves (`/workspace/_test.html` on a server run from `/workspace` is `/_test.html`), and says when the server answered with an error ("the server answered HTTP 404 ...: the screenshot is its error page"); a 404 page read "no console errors" before (SRV-550).
- `render_page` runs the laya kit's page check (Chrome under DevTools, after the page has loaded) and reports console errors, uncaught exceptions and failed loads, and the visible text; Chromium's screenshot mode, which logs no failed load, stays as the fallback without the kit. A pagoda replay's module answered 404 and render_page said "no console errors" six times over the app's loading screen. An error that names a script of the page and a line (the kit now says where an exception was thrown) comes with that line from the chat's files, in render_page and in the verify phase's check: the same replay read "reading 'set'" at pond.js (62) thirteen times and edited main.js (SRV-554).
- A model call the engine ends with finish reason `error` is retried once as a new step, without the empty-turn nudge; a second fails the run saying the engine failed twice. A pagoda replay failed as "The model answered with nothing, twice" after two engine failures (SRV-556).
- A chat sandbox has 4 GiB of memory by default (`QSE_SANDBOX_MEM_GB`, 1 before; the running cap follows, 16 GiB for 4 sandboxes); a container made under another limit takes the current one at its next start. render_page and the laya kit start Chromium with `--disable-dev-shm-usage` and one renderer. Headless Chromium drawing a Three.js app in software went past 1 GiB and render_page was killed for memory on the app it checked (SRV-558).

### Proxy and dashboard

- A streamed request with `X-Tandem-Cost: 1` gets its cost as one SSE comment before `data: [DONE]` (`: tandem-cost {"cost_micros": N, "backend": id}`), the figure of its ledger row, the harness's second requests included; chatd sends the header. Without it the stream is the backend's, byte for byte (VIS-207).
- The card of a backend's model carries what the provider's model list says (VIS-207): DeepSeek's `GET /models` names the model, its window, its output limit, its input kinds and its effort levels, and the discovery every 10 minutes stores them. The picker shows "DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (cloud)" instead of the adapter's "DeepSeek V4 Flash"; the effort chip offers low, high and max for a DeepSeek model, auto being the provider's default (high), and the request carries `reasoning_effort` with that level (thinking off: `none`; the engine's medium and extra high go as high, a max picked on DeepSeek goes to the engine as extra high); deepseek-flash, whose input kinds name `image`, gets the chat's images (uploads, `render_page` screenshots) as `image_url` parts, deepseek-v4-pro none.
- A model id a later discovery finds for the first time is stored disabled, logged, and pushed once to the ntfy topic of the monitor's stall watchdog: nothing reaches the picker until it is turned on under Backends (VIS-207). `deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` was in DeepSeek's list for a while on 2026-10-17.
- The usage ledger records each relayed answer's `system_fingerprint` (schema 10, migrated in place), and Performance shows it in the request detail: `deepseek-flash` keeps its id while DeepSeek swaps the snapshot behind it (VIS-207).
- Performance and Usage keep the engine's requests and the relayed ones apart (VIS-207). Relayed requests were in the ledger with tokens, TTFT, tok/s and cost, but the views pooled them: an hour of a DeepSeek chat put the engine's decode p50 at 300 tok/s, its dots sat above the scatter's axis as "cold", the cache sources put the provider's cache hits under "cold", and the Live panel showed the request in flight as "warming up (0 of 50 tokens)". Recent requests now draws relayed requests as dots of their own on a log axis, the timing panel names the backend and the cost, the cache sources and the history count the engine's own requests with each relayed backend as a line of its own beside them in decode speed and TTFT, and Usage has a table of the engine against each relayed backend (requests, tokens, decode and TTFT p50, cost). The Live panel names a relayed request's backend and says its tokens are counted at its end; the Last 20 rows carry `backend` and show the backend's cache.

### Models and engine

- Super VL reads images (ENG-365). The checkpoint's C-RADIO ViT-H/16 tower and projector (BF16 in the EXL3 packs and in NVIDIA's NVFP4 checkpoint, 1.57 GB of tensors) load beside the trunk: 1.60 GiB allocated on EXL3 4.0. An image is one tile at a dynamic resolution, 1,024 to 13,312 16-pixel patches, 256 to 3,328 prompt rows between `<img>` and `</img>` (1,000 for a 1,280 x 800 screenshot); the trunk has no positional encoding, so an image row is only an embedding over its placeholder. The processor is the checkpoint's, without remote code. Against the checkpoint's own processor and modeling code on three pictures (DGX Spark, 2026-10-17): pixel values and prompt ids identical, the tower's rows bit-identical to the reference's bf16 run (cosine 0.99973 to 0.99990 against its fp32 run, as the reference's own), greedy answers with our rows and with the reference's identical. The caches key image rows on the image's content. The NemotronH tier fingerprint counts `vision.py`, and `engine.py` changed: Bolt's, Lightning's and Super VL's saved conversations from 0.11.2 are not reused, their first request reads the prompt again.
- Rows forwarded after a prompt with images (a forced reasoning close, a hidden note) are plain rows: the serving forward handed them the image context and the request failed with "forward past the prompt ... with images attached" when the conductor closed a looping reasoning on a request with a screenshot (ENG-367).
- The three Super VL profiles set `VISION=on`; their memory need, ceiling and peak grow by 2 GiB (the tower and the 512 MB image cache). The setup guide has a Vision switch for Super VL with that figure. Bolt and Lightning stay text only.
- A turn that ends inside a verified block commits the block's rows through its end token only (SRV-530). The lookup drafts what followed the same tool call earlier in the prompt (`</tool_call>`, `<|im_end|>`, `\n`) and the walk accepted it; the loop committed those rows and returned at the end token, so the engine stood one or two rows past the committed tokens. A NemotronH state cannot take a committed row back: on Super VL 31 of 54 turns of a chat run kept no end anchor (`end anchor not kept (ahead)`), every one a tool call, and their next turn resumed at the last anchor line or read the conversation again. The commit now stops at the end token's row (or the budget's), where Qwen's cut back of the pending commit stopped: Qwen keeps the same state and end anchor bit for bit, NemotronH and LFM2.5 keep theirs, and the text is the same. `end_cut` counts these blocks in the resident prefix's report.

### Parallel requests

- A conversation's next turn goes to the side slot that holds the longest share of its prompt, with or without an end anchor, and before slot 0 when slot 0 holds less of it (SRV-528). A side slot was its home only when it had kept an end anchor; without one a turn took the lowest free side slot, and once the 600 s carry guard of a slot below expired, a 45,683-token Super VL conversation moved from slot 2 to slot 1 and read 45,778 tokens again (80.9 s). The carry guard now orders new conversations only. A slot-0 conversation whose last request was cancelled inside its prompt, or that no request continued for `QWEN38_SLOT0_KEEP_S` (1,800 s), no longer sends new conversations to the side slots: a cancelled 1,000,000-token test prompt had kept the 1,048,576-token slot 0 idle all evening. A turn whose slot stays busy past `QWEN38_SIDE_HOME_WAIT_S` says it moved, in the log and the Lanes view; `/health` `parallel` counts `hops` and `hop_tokens`.

### Conductor

- A turn whose class nobody decided keeps its class's packages under a model fit with `fallback: lean` (Super VL, Bolt, Lightning, LFM2.5): the profile's default class on a new session, the session's class after it, filtered by the fit's `packages` and `rules` as for a decided class. The lean fallback dropped every package, rule and core, so with Laya refused every Chat-tab turn on Super VL went out with no package at all; the Chat tab now gets code_edit's core. The effort stays the profile's default and no effort sentence goes in. A tool turn keeps the note of its user message, so a run's prompt prefix does not change between its steps (SRV-534).
- A router stored before FX6 gets the `coding` core on code_edit and debug by a one-time migration, unless a stored version gave them a core: under `packages: core` such a router gave a coding turn no package, decided or fallen back (SRV-534).
- design_ui and drawing have a core package, `ui-design` and `creative-coding`; a stored router gets them by a one-time migration where the class lists the package and no stored version gave it a core. Under `packages: core` (Super VL) a turn Laya decided as one of them got no package: "make a three.js page with a red cube" (design_ui, 0.43) went out with the reading note only (SRV-536).
- three_d's core is threejs-scene and coding; a stored router gets coding by a one-time migration unless a stored version had it there. Three pagoda replays on Super VL thought 6 to 11 minutes on their first step and drafted the files in the thinking; coding's "a plan of 3 to 8 lines, code in files only" reached code_edit and debug turns only (SRV-552).
- The narrator is off by default: the roles document's `narrator.mode` is `off`, and no shipped profile sets `ui.narrator` (coding and chat had `live`). The model does not load, the keeper leaves it, `POST /v1/conductor/narrator/load` answers 409 `role_off`, and the residency plan leaves out a role the roles document switches off, so the narrator's 6 GiB claim is gone. No model card turns the narrator on in the Setup Guide. A stored coding or chat profile with `live`, the role `on` in a stored roles document: `off` by a one-time migration, unless a stored version had another value. The narrator stays switchable: the role `on` and a profile's `ui.narrator` (SRV-534).
- The decider's residency claim is 3.0 GiB, measured with Laya in the engine (OPS-69), instead of the arbiter sidecar's 8.2. With 8.2 a new box refused Laya on Super VL at 3 slots of 262,144 (43.75 GiB available, 17.46 still to come to the engine's peak: 18.09 left, under the 21 of floor and margin); with 3.0, 23.29 are left. A stored residency document with 8.2 gets 3.0 by a one-time migration, unless a stored version had another value. While no Laya model is loaded because the planner refused it, the log says so once (`[deciders] WARNING`) and `/health` `roles.laya.refused` has the model, the reason and the numbers (SRV-534).

### Packages

- threejs-scene: tone mapping and colour space, a day scene by default (a sky background with matching fog beyond the subject, hemisphere light about 1.5, a sun about 3 with shadows), a day/night switch that changes background, fog, lights and exposure together, saturated non-metal materials, foliage as clustered shapes, and a check of the screenshot against the request. Its skeleton had a near-black background and light strengths from before three.js r155, which render dim. The creative-coding Three.js skeleton gets the same light strengths and tone mapping (SRV-532).
- threejs-scene names the calls the model reached for that three.js does not have (`Matrix4.makeRotationXYZ`, `Matrix4.rotateY`, `renderer.shadowMap.size`, BufferGeometryUtils as a namespace) and what to use, the bloom chain with `OutputPass` last (without it the frame has no tone mapping), golden-hour and night light numbers, framing, and how to read a class's methods from the readable source of the same version. A pagoda replay spent 28 of its 50 calls on those four calls, grepping the minified build (SRV-542).
- The laya kit's page check reports each screenshot's look in numbers: brightness, the share of its most common colour, the colours over 1 % and saturation (SRV-532).

Upgrade: run the installer again, as for 0.11.2, then `tandem restart` and `tandem chat restart`. The conductor's migrations run at the engine's first start (`migrations.json` in the conductor's directory lists them), and the usage ledger moves to schema 10 in place. A chat sandbox made under the old 1 GiB limit takes 4 GiB at its next start.

## 0.11.2, 2026-10-16

0.11.2 starts chatd, the Chat tab's service, with the engine, and the Chat tab says when chatd is down instead of switching to the in-browser mock; update every box that runs the Chat tab. It fixes the install's scripts and secrets file, keeps a second chatd on the same Docker from taking another's sandboxes, makes the port preview open the app the model built, and reads the Context panel's live figures. The model picker lists models, one row each, and DeepSeek can be picked. The Setup Guide sets the number of chats and both windows with steppers, and Nemotron 3.5 Super VL takes a window up to 1,048,576 tokens, its checkpoint's own. Every model writes the same text as in 0.11.1.

### Chat tab and install

- chatd starts with the engine (`tandem start`, `ops/start.sh`, the systemd unit, the Setup Guide) and stops with `tandem stop`; an engine restart leaves it running. The watchdog starts a chatd that died. `tandem chat start|stop|restart|status|logs`, a chatd line in `tandem status`, `QSE_CHATD=off` to opt out; the install's last message names the Chat tab (OPS-155).
- `ops/chatd.sh` runs under the install's venv and reads the same secrets file as the engine; a start that fails exits 1 with the log. `ops/make-secrets.sh` writes the file the engine reads, so the Setup Guide's generated admin password takes effect on an installed box. `ops/chatd.service` runs from `~/TandemLLM` (OPS-153).
- The Chat tab says when chatd is not running, with the command, instead of switching to the in-browser mock, which now loads only for `?chat=mock`; a key chatd refuses, an engine without chat routes and no answer are named too, and the tab checks again by itself (VIS-179). Reported by Aron (issue #3).
- `bin/tandem` loads its config on an install with no `ops/active-profile`, which is every plain and `--setup` install: under `set -e` the failed read ended `tandem start`, `status` and the rest with status 1 and no message, so the installer's own start failed. A Flash-Next profile with a cold table failed the same way. A config command that fails now names its file and line, and setup mode's `tandem start` no longer drops the page cache of every file under the working directory (OPS-159).
- The installer copies `roles.sh`, `watchdog.sh` and `hold.sh` into `run/ops`: every start on an installed box printed `roles.sh: No such file or directory`, and the documented watchdog line read the checkout's template `serve.env`. On an install the line is `* * * * * ~/TandemLLM/run/ops/watchdog.sh` (docs/operations.md); `hold.sh` there pauses the tree the watchdog and `start.sh` watch (OPS-161).
- The Setup Guide's reset never removes the secrets file the engine reads: it guarded `~/.qwen38-spark-engine/secrets.env` only, and an install keeps it in `DIR/state/secrets.env` (`QSE_SECRETS`). The install's ledger in `DIR/state/usage` is kept below level 5 as well; the setup apply job reads `$QSE_STATE_DIR/secrets.env` in `start.sh`'s order (OPS-163).
- `render_page` and the port preview dial `::1` and `127.0.0.1` by address, not through `/etc/hosts`: a dev server that listens on one of them and that `curl` reached answered "Connection refused", with no address and no port in the message (SRV-507). A Vite app's absolute module imports (`/src/...`, `/@vite/client`) and a style sheet's `url(/...)` are rewritten to the port's prefix, as the HTML was.
- The Context panel gives a live run's figures: the Now row keeps its tok/s between ticks, and a gap says why (between model calls, warming up, prefilling, queued, no drafter) where it read "not tracked for this model" for every one (VIS-181). The row of the call in flight wins over a finished one, a side slot's request has its own block counts, and a turn of several calls takes its first call's time to first token and the run's wall time, so "thinking, this turn" no longer reads 0 after a turn (SRV-509).
- The chat header's More menu opens downward from its button and fits the screen, so Pin, Rename, Export, Sandbox and Delete can be reached; it opened under the top bar (VIS-183).
- The preview pane opens the running app on its own: a port that starts listening opens in a Preview tab once, the plus menu's Preview opens the newest running server first, and a waiting pane names why, with the command and a Start button. `port:N` resolves to the server that listens when N does not, and a bundler project's source `index.html` resolves to its dev server. The pane serves module scripts and style sheets of the Vite dev server and of `vite preview`, and lets a page's `fetch` and hot-reload socket through. `present` reports the target, the server's answer for the page and its assets, and what the pane itself shows, and fails when the pane shows nothing (SRV-511).
- Chat tab design pass: no horizontal overflow from 320 px to 1440 px (a phone included), a quieter thread, cards, a figures line, and a tidier composer and panes (VIS-185).
- chatd adopts, reaps, stops, kills and removes only its own sandbox containers. Each chatd labels its containers with an instance id kept in its data dir (`tandem.chat.instance`); a container from before the label counts as its own only when the chat's workspace folder is in that data dir, and is created again with the label at its next start. Before, a second chatd on the same Docker (a test install with its own `--data`) adopted the first one's containers and removed them as containers of chats it did not know (SRV-524).
- A sandbox container removed or stopped outside chatd starts again at the next tool call, which says once that the sandbox restarted (files kept, processes gone). Before, chatd kept the box as running and every bash and render_page call answered `exec failed (404)`. The same sandbox failure three calls in a row ends the run as interrupted with a notice, whatever the calls were; Continue goes on once the sandbox is back (SRV-526).
- The Continue card of an interrupted answer says why it stopped: its limit of model calls or the sandbox failing (the notice, in the card's place), the engine not answering, or chatd restarting. It said "The engine restarted" for every one, a run at its limit included. chatd records the reason in the answer's `stats.interrupted`; an answer from before has neutral words. The card hides while a Continue run writes into the same answer (VIS-197).
- The composer's model picker lists models, one row each: DeepSeek V4 Flash and V4 Pro through the proxy can be picked. It listed the conductor's profiles (each client's harness: opencode, Open WebUI, Hermes, A/B tests, header-only ones) as the only buttons, so a model without profiles was a heading, and both DeepSeek models were named by their backend, `DeepSeek (cloud)`. A backend's model is named by its provider name (`name` in the proxy's `/v1/models` card, with `cloud`), else its id; the line under it leaves out what the backend does not report. The Chat tab runs under its own profile, chat-app, by its client kind: chatd sends no `X-Tandem-Profile`, a settings patch stores no profile, and chatd's store v7 clears the profile stored in a chat or preset.
