A preset picks a model instead of a profile. A chat with a DeepSeek model failed at its first call: chatd sent the window minus the prompt as `max_tokens`, and DeepSeek refuses more than 393,216. A backend's model now gets a `max_tokens` only from its output limit (`max_output` in the proxy's card, 393,216 for DeepSeek), none when the limit is unknown (VIS-203).

### Setup Guide

- Parallel chats is a stepper: minus, a number field and plus (VIS-199). A model card's range is how far the model was measured, not a cap. Above it the step says the count is untested, and the memory estimate decides, up to the engine's 16: a joint verify pass holds 32 rows and each chat keeps 2. The memory bar and a line with one extra chat's cost follow every change. The step names a count that does not fit, or one the engine does not take, next to the field; Next stays on the step and `POST /v1/setup/apply` refuses it (`over_budget`, `out_of_range`). The extra chats' window names chats 2 to N.
- Both windows, the longest conversation and the one of the extra chats, are steppers too (VIS-199). Minus and plus walk 8,192, 16,384, 32,768 and on, doubling up to the model's own maximum (1,048,576 on Super VL, whose card now says so); the field takes any number, `131,072`, `128k` or `1m`, and shows the short form beside it. A value above the model, below its shortest window or off its step stays as typed with the limit named ("This model holds at most 1,048,576 tokens."), and Next stays on the step. The extra chats hold at most the first chat's window, as the engine cuts a side slot to slot 0's, and the step says so.

### Models and engine

- Nemotron 3.5 Super VL takes a window up to 1,048,576 tokens, its checkpoint's own, for slot 0 and the side slots (default 262,144). Checked to 249,983 prompt tokens (five needles of five at 131,054 and 249,983 on EXL3 4.0, slot 0 at 1,048,576, 4 slots); a 1,000,000-token prompt is not measured. The setup guide reads every model's largest window from its checkpoint's config when the weights are on the box, the card's otherwise, and every card now names its checkpoint's maximum: Super VL 1,048,576; Qwen3.8-27B, Flash-Next, Bolt and Lightning 262,144; LFM2.5 131,072. Super VL's memory estimate counts LiLiCorr (3.9 GiB), the measured prefill workspace (3.4 GiB) and a side slot's part beyond its KV (1.1 GiB); `slots.max` 3 is what was measured (ENG-363).
- NemotronH's prefill workspace is flat (3.34 GiB at 131,054 tokens, 3.18 at 249,983): the memory policy no longer refuses a long prefill by the 27B's line of 30 kB a token, which put 29 GiB on a 1,000,000-token prompt. A slot 0 window above 262,144 adds its KV above it to the policy's ceiling and peak, as the side slots' bytes are added (ENG-363).
- NemotronH keeps attention's partials once per power-of-two bucket of verify widths and slot instead of once per width: at a 1,048,576-token window a set is 32 MiB a row, and the 33 widths could hold 17 GiB. NemotronH and LFM2.5 keep at most 32 joint decode graphs (one per set of slots decoding together and their attention classes), the least recently used dropped and captured again on demand; the count had no bound with more slots and longer windows. `/health` reports them under `parallel.joint_graphs`. The bound is a safe pick, not a measurement (ENG-363).

Upgrade: run the installer again; chatd then starts with the engine, and `bin/tandem`, `run/ops/serve.env` and the scripts in `run/ops` are rewritten. A chatd started earlier keeps the old code until `tandem chat restart`.

## 0.11.1, 2026-10-16

0.11.1 fixes how chatd, the Chat tab's server, reaches the folders a chat's sandbox can write; update every box that runs the Chat tab. It gives Bolt's EXL3 packs 2.5 to 6.0 their StairCut price files, so drafting no longer runs slower than plain decoding on them, takes two contributions, names each weight pack's maker in the setup guide, and describes the install through the setup guide. Every model writes the same text as in 0.11.0.

### Security

- Chat tab: chatd saves an attachment under `/workspace/uploads/` without following a symlink. The sandbox can write that folder, so it could make `uploads/` a symlink, or leave one at the file's name, and chatd then wrote the user's file wherever the link pointed on the host. Now `uploads/` must be a real folder and the file a new one; when chatd cannot save it there, it sends the message all the same and the prompt says why. chatd cuts a name over 255 bytes, keeping its extension; on Linux such a name failed the send (SEC-1). Reported by Joey.
- Chat tab: chatd's other reads and writes in the folders the sandbox writes into do not follow a symlink either: the file tools and files pane, snapshots with their undo, and the Open WebUI runner's files in the sandbox's home. Before, a symlink at the runner's `run.py`, the toolkit file or the request file made chatd overwrite the link's target, and a snapshot copied a file the sandbox swapped for a symlink into the chat. Each access walks from the folder's root by directory fds opened with O_NOFOLLOW, a write goes to a new file renamed into place, and a read takes a regular file only (a FIFO blocked chatd). chatd replaces a tool call id from the backend that is not a plain name before the id names a file (SEC-1).

### Contributions

- Asset fetches download a pinned asset at its revision (SPD-121). `ops/fetch_weights.py` planned an asset at its `revision` but fetched the repository's default branch and checked it against that branch's manifest. Contributed by joeynyc (pull request #1).
- NemotronH's tier fingerprint counts its GGUF reader and loader (`gguf.py`, `gguf_load.py`) and the GGUF file itself (`QSE_NH_GGUF`, a `.gguf` in the model folder): another GGUF restored the first one's saved states (ENG-327). The NemotronH profiles' fingerprint changes, so Bolt's and Super VL's saved conversations from 0.10.0 and 0.11.0 are not reused: their first request reads the prompt again. Contributed by joeynyc (pull request #2).

### Nemotron 3.5 Bolt: StairCut price files

- Bolt's EXL3 profiles 2.5, 3.0, 3.5, 4.0, 5.0 and 6.0 ship StairCut price files (`ops/prices/nemotron-3.5-bolt-74b-a9b/`, SPD-127), measured on the Spark: the verify chain of 1 to 16 rows at 1,024 and 8,192 tokens, the plain step, and a `spec` prior for a drafted round, (8-row chain + draft) / (0.75 x LiLiCorr's accepted length), 13.9 to 20.2 ms a token. `tools/nh_check.py prices --lilicorr` writes it.
- Without a file the cut priced a one-row block at 1 ms and took the anchor alone after the draft had run, wherever the draft was unsure; on 0.11.0, 3.0 to 4.0 wrote prose at 31 to 33 tok/s and chat at 39 to 40, below their plain 40.5 to 41.7.
- Setup Guide rows on 0.11.1, one request, 512 greedy tokens, thinking off, 3 runs of the profile's drafting beside 3 plain runs; plain / drafted prose / chat / code, tok/s: 2.0 43.2 / 65.6 / 71.1 / 102.1; 2.5 41.9 / 65.8 / 68.9 / 114.7; 3.0 41.6 / 58.1 / 69.3 / 100.8; 3.5 40.6 / 59.5 / 65.9 / 101.0; 4.0 40.4 / 52.0 / 62.0 / 97.9; 5.0 33.9 / 51.7 / 55.5 / 81.7; 6.0 29.1 / 40.1 / 50.1 / 76.3; the IQ2 GGUF with the lookup 27.7 / 27.7 / 27.8 / 31.9. Every drafted text is the plain run's. DGX Spark, 2026-10-16.
- Super VL keeps its 0.11.0 price files. On 0.11.1 NVIDIA's NVFP4 drafts above plain on every ask (prose 23.7, chat 28.5, code 39.5 against 19.6). The EXL3 2.0 pack's prose varies from run to run: two runs at 37.3 tok/s, one at 33.5 with the cut on plain steps, against 36.5 plain; chat and code drafted 45.4 to 63.7, one code run 44.6 (cause not isolated).

### Setup guide and install

- Each weight card names its source: a TandemLLM quant, a vendor release or a community quant, the maker and the Hugging Face repository as owner/name (VIS-175). Every profile in `models/*/model.yaml` carries `made_by`. Flash-Next's community section lists turboderp's five packs from `models/community-builtin.json`, which ships with the release and is never fetched; Use selects the matching `flashnext-<bpw>` profile.
- The install is two commands, then the setup guide in the browser: `bash install.sh --setup --yes` and `http://127.0.0.1:8000/dashboard/#/setup` (OPS-149). README, docs/setup.md, the manual and install.sh's last message say so; `use-profile.sh` moved to "Advanced: from the command line".

Upgrade: run the 0.11.1 installer again (`--setup --force-setup` on a box installed with `--setup`, the same `--dir` otherwise). chatd is its own process and keeps the old code until it restarts: `bash ~/TandemLLM/src/ops/chatd.sh stop`, then `bash ~/TandemLLM/src/ops/chatd.sh start`.

## 0.11.0, 2026-10-16

0.11.0 adds a fifth model, NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Super VL 120B-A12B, from our EXL3 packs at 4.0 and 2.0 bpw or NVIDIA's NVFP4 release, with NVIDIA's LiLiCorr drafter for Super VL. The other models' text and speed do not change, and their saved conversations carry over.

### Nemotron 3.5 Super VL 120B-A12B

Super VL is a NemotronH hybrid (ENG-E13): 40 Mamba2, 40 mixture-of-experts (512 experts, 22 a token, one shared) and 8 attention layers, an MTP head, 1,048,576 tokens of context (TandemLLM serves up to 262,144). Text only: the vision tower is not served yet. Reference: [docs/nemotron-h.md](docs/nemotron-h.md).

- ModelOpt checkpoints read as stored (ENG-351): NVFP4 projections (uint8 codes, e4m3 group scales, an fp32 tensor scale) and FP8 projections (e4m3 codes, an fp32 tensor scale), audited against the layer table. The routed experts of a layer run as one `NVFP4Bank` (`tools/nvfp4_relu2.py`: one program a row-expert pair, fp32 products, row-invariant), FP8 projections as `FP8Linear` (a 16-row tensor-core product, the scale on the fp32 sum). Static activation and KV scales are read past: activations and the KV cache stay in BF16.
- LiLiCorr with its own head (ENG-353): Super VL's drafter carries an NVFP4 LM head over the target's vocabulary and reads five taps with a window of 8,192. Accepted length 4.82 on NVIDIA's NVFP4, 4.65 on the EXL3 4.0 pack (4 prompts of 192 tokens, thinking on).
- Profiles `nemotron-super-vl-exl3-4.0` (default for Super VL), `nemotron-super-vl-exl3-2.0` and `nemotron-super-vl-nvfp4`, each with LiLiCorr and the lookup cut by StairCut, and the model's Setup Guide card (ENG-355). The price files carry a `spec` prior, so the cut drafts from the first request.
- EXL3 packs converted from NVIDIA's BF16 checkpoint (revision 97e00975) by exllamav3 1.6.2 with a patch for Super VL's layer layout (ENG-347, ENG-349): 4.0 has every projection at 4 bits, head 6, MTP head 4 (65.0 GB); 2.0 has routed experts at 2 bits and every other projection at 4 (36.84 GB). Each is in a public Hugging Face repository pinned by commit, with its model card, NVIDIA's OpenMDW-1.1 license text, a NOTICE and the converter patch (ENG-359).
- Against the BF16 checkpoint's logits (`tools/nh_quality.py`, 8 wikitext-2 rows of 1,024 tokens): EXL3 4.0 KL 0.049, top-1 92.9 %; EXL3 2.0 KL 0.325, top-1 82.1 %; NVIDIA's NVFP4 KL 0.041, top-1 93.4 %.
- Through the server, one request, 512 greedy tokens, thinking off, mean of 3 runs: plain 31.1 (4.0), 36.5 (2.0) and 19.6 tok/s (NVFP4); with LiLiCorr and the lookup on prose / chat / code / edit / copy 33.1 / 43.9 / 53.6 / 101.0 / 108.3 (4.0), 35.6 / 46.2 / 46.3 / 125.1 / 139.2 (2.0), 23.9 / 28.7 / 39.9 / 73.5 / 81.7 (NVFP4). Every drafted text is the plain run's. vLLM on NVIDIA's NVFP4: 19.4 plain, 29.9 / 34.8 / 52.7 / 72.4 / 72.7 with LiLiCorr. DGX Spark, 2026-10-16.
- Not yet (ENG-357): prompts read at 476 to 589 tok/s, 4 to 5 times slower than vLLM; with a drafter, requests at once take turns instead of sharing a pass. The vision tower and the MTP head are not served.

## 0.10.0, 2026-10-15

0.10.0 adds a fourth model, NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B, from our EXL3 packs at 2.0 to 6.0 bpw or NVIDIA's IQ2 GGUF, with NVIDIA's LiLiCorr drafter, and limits each Chat tab sandbox to 1 GiB. The other models' text and speed do not change, and their saved conversations carry over.

- Chat tab: each chat's sandbox has 1 GiB of memory (`QSE_SANDBOX_MEM_GB`; was 4 GiB), and four of them take what one took (`QSE_SANDBOX_TOTAL_GB` follows the limit). A process the kernel kills at the limit fails its call with "out of memory (1 GiB sandbox limit)", read from the container's cgroup, also when a pipe's writer exits 1 after its reader was killed; the call card shows it (SRV-485, VIS-167). What fits in 1 GiB, measured: [docs/chat.md](docs/chat.md#the-sandbox-phase-2).
- Chat tab: an attachment is never inlined past the window. Every attachment is saved under the chat's `/workspace/uploads/` when its message is sent; one message's text files share a budget of a quarter of the free window, at most 32,000 tokens, and a file past it is one line with its name, size, tokens and path. The chip shows size and tokens on upload and marks a file that goes as a file. A request that does not fit names the attachment or the largest part instead of advising a new chat (SRV-487, VIS-169).
- Engine: `POST /v1/cache/release {bytes}` (as `/v1/cache/clear`: the admin token or trusted-local) gives back what the engine holds idle, cheapest first: free allocator blocks and caches while slot 0 is idle, the small models, idle side conversations, slot 0's idle conversation (to the NVMe first). chatd asks it before a sandbox waits and before the memory guard stops one (SRV-483).

### NemotronH (Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, Bolt)

A fourth model family: NVIDIA's NemotronH hybrid (ENG-E12), Mamba2, NoPE attention and mixture-of-experts blocks with an MTP head, built on Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B BF16 for Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B, served from NVIDIA's IQ2 GGUF or EXL3 packs at 2.0 to 6.0 bpw, all with NVIDIA's LiLiCorr drafter. The other models' text and speed do not change. Reference: [docs/nemotron-h.md](docs/nemotron-h.md).

- Correctness: reference within 2e-5 of transformers' NemotronH (three tiny models, fp32). Lightning BF16 against transformers BF16: top token 98.63 % of 1,024 chat positions, all 14 differences near ties.
- Exactness: a verify row equals the decode step's row bit for bit; a commit walks each SSM state along the kept path with the decode kernel, so the committed state equals the decode steps'; load-time self-check over 24 rows and the states.
- GGUF: `nemotron_h_moe` files, IQ2_XXS weights and expert banks decoded on the fly (`tools/iq2_linear.py`, twin equal to gguf-py bit for bit), Q8_0 dequantised at load; other types refused by name.

- The checkpoint's MTP head as a draft head (`QSE_NH_HEAD=mtp`, off in the profile): its draft is the trunk's greedy token at depth 1, 2, 3 in 91.9, 80.6, 69.5 % of 1,000 chat positions.

Decode step 44.2 tok/s; with LiLiCorr and the lookup, 512 greedy tokens, thinking off: prose 65.8, code 99.0, chat 69.3, edit 152.8, copy 256.0 tok/s, every text the plain run's; 3 requests at once 72.1 tok/s in total. DGX Spark, 2026-10-15. On this release through the server, 3 runs each (ENG-345): plain 43.3 tok/s; with LiLiCorr and the lookup prose 65.7, code 102.8, chat 69.4, edit 180.5, copy 244.7.
- Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B as EXL3 packs at 2.5, 3.0, 3.5, 4.0, 5.0 and 6.0 bpw (ENG-337): profiles `nemotron-bolt-exl3-<bpw>` with LiLiCorr and the lookup, no StairCut price file yet. ### Fixed

- Chat tab (SRV-481): a tool call waited for its sandbox without end. On the Spark every `bash` call of a chat waited 21 minutes on a 30 GiB start line (`QSE_SANDBOX_MIN_START_GB`, a leftover from the Flash-Next memory fits) and a 19 GiB reserve, with MemAvailable at 20 GiB. The start line is gone. A sandbox starts when MemAvailable less its limit stays at 4 GiB or more (`QSE_SANDBOX_FLOOR_GB`): the engine keeps itself at its own floors, and a prefill's workspace measured 2.7 GiB at 203,052 tokens. The guard stops an idle sandbox under 3 GiB and kills them all under 2 GiB. A wait ends after 60 s (`QSE_SANDBOX_WAIT_S`) with the reason and the numbers, as the tool result the model reads and on the call card; the terminal and stdio MCP servers no longer wait forever either.

Upgrade: run the 0.10.0 installer again (`--setup --force-setup` on a box installed with `--setup`, the same `--dir` otherwise), then `ops/use-profile.sh nemotron-bolt-exl3-2.0` for Bolt.

## 0.9.2, 2026-10-15

0.9.2 fixes two install bugs an early tester hit on a new DGX Spark with 0.9.1. The engine, the conductor and the dashboard do not change.

### Fixed

- `ops/fetch_weights.py` (OPS-143): `verify()` compared a fetch entry's globs to file names literally. A download whose list is all globs (Qwen3.5-0.8B for the shadow reader, Qwen3.5-2B for the narrator) checked no file and failed with "0 files checked: FAILED"; Laya's files under `multilingual/` and `typed-decisions/` were not checked. The globs now select the files, as in the plan.
- `install.sh --setup` (OPS-143): the installer wrote `QWEN38_MODEL`, the Hugging Face cache's base folder, after the weight profile. On a new box that folder is empty, the 27B's EXL3 profiles did not switch to `base-plain`, and `use-profile.sh exl3-*` refused with base-plain on disk. The keys the installer adds now come before the profile, and an EXL3 profile takes `base-plain` when that folder holds no snapshot. A standalone community pack reads its own folder on an install.sh box for the same reason.
- `install.sh` with `HF_HOME` or `HF_HUB_CACHE` set (OPS-143): `serve.env` names that cache, and `use-profile.sh` passes it to the fetch, so a later shell without the variable fetches and finds the base in the same cache.

Upgrade: run the 0.9.2 installer again (`--setup --force-setup` on a box installed with `--setup`, the same `--dir` otherwise). It rewrites `run/ops/serve.env` and the scripts in `run/ops`; a `git checkout` of the tag alone keeps the old ones.

## 0.9.1, 2026-10-14

0.9.1 adds web search and media playback to the Chat tab, turns on the loop guard, the loop escape and memory notes in the shipped conductor profiles, and fixes the Setup Guide's install page and the EXL3 base download. The decode path does not change: under `engine/` only the small models' slot changed (VIS-153).

- Chat tab: a built-in `web_search` tool with DuckDuckGo and SearXNG providers, set in the chat settings (SRV-469, VIS-157). Reference: [docs/chat.md](docs/chat.md#web-search).
- Chat tab: video, audio, PDF and other binary files open in a player, the browser's PDF viewer or a size line with Download, in the Files pane and the `present` card; chatd's view route streams a file with byte ranges (206, 416, ETag) and no 2 MiB cap (VIS-159).
- Conductor: the same-call guard (C3) is on in the shipped `coding`, `chat-app`, `hermes`, `overnight` and `chat` profiles (`toolgate.same_call: true`; chat's C3 acts). C3 counts only the current user turn, a run whose result took the client 10 s or more is a wait (`wait_s`), and calls are held only on a request whose turn already ends with the repeat; every other turn streams its calls as before. A one-time migration turns it on in each stored profile whose versions never had it on (SRV-473).
- Conductor: the loop escape. After a repeated or near-repeated tool call the session decodes with the model card's sampling (the checkpoint's `generation_config.json`, fresh seed) and C3's escape note until it makes progress, then greedy again; the client's own sampling wins. Profile section `sampling` (`loop_escape`, `agentic_default: greedy | card`; shipped greedy, escape on in the agent profiles). Ledger `sampling` `loop_escape` / `card`, usage `tandem.sampling`, `/health` `sampling.card` and `sampling.loop_escape` (SRV-475). Output changes on those turns only.
- `--reasoning-effort none` and `off`: thinking off for every request that says nothing about thinking (SRV-477).
- Conductor: the shipped `chat`, `coding`, `hermes` and `chat-app` profiles have `memory: on`, and a one-time migration adds it to each stored one without the switch (an explicit value stays; `general` keeps none); the memory card says the notes are the model's memory between chats, and a profile with `memory: off` tells the model so; the Context panel shows a turn's memory notes (SRV-471). Memory-on prompts change by the card's new sentence.

### Fixed

- Setup Guide, install page (VIS-149): a reload no longer shows a finished job as running. The job stream sends the log on disk, the job as it is now, then its events; the page keeps a final job final and handles no event after it closes the stream.
- Setup Guide, install page (VIS-151): a finished job keeps its whole log after a reload (the stream ends at the job's `done` event); past 300 lines the log box says how many it dropped from the top; a job whose folder is gone says so instead of an empty log.
- Setup Guide, review and install page (VIS-155): the change list compares every key the current `run/setup.env` sets too, so a model switch lists the keys it drops (LFM2.5's TEMPERATURE, TOP_K and REP_PENALTY: 16 changes, not 13) as removed, with what the engine runs with then; the install page lists the changes under the check step.
- Setup Guide, fetch and smoke steps (VIS-153): the fetch step downloads the models of the tools the selection turns on (Qwen3.5-0.8B for the shadow reader, Qwen3.5-2B for the narrator, Laya), and the review lists every download with its size; a tool model nothing downloads is a `missing_assets` error. After the start the smoke step reads the tools' states: a failed one is a warning on the job with its reason. A failed shadow reader load is tried again after 300 s in an idle window; `/health` `roles` carry the load error.
- EXL3 profiles of Qwen3.8-27B (OPS-133): their base is `base-plain`, the Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 tensors an EXL3 load reads (embedding, norms, GDN gates and convolutions, vision tower, config, tokenizer), fetched by HTTP range requests into `~/.qwen38-spark-engine/weights/base-plain`: 3.54 GB instead of 30.41 (the F8_E4M3 projections, their scales and `lm_head.weight` stay out). A fresh `exl3-6.0` downloads 36.48 GB, not 63.34. A box with the full FP8 snapshot uses it and downloads nothing; NVFP4 still needs the full base.
- Dashboard service worker (OPS-131): a page load that the reverse proxy answers 502, 503 or 504 gets the cached shell, as a network error did; the page says the engine is restarting and reloads once `/health` answers.

## 0.9.0, 2026-10-14

A third model: LiquidAI's LFM2.5-24B-A2B (ENG-E10), 24B parameters, 4 of 64 experts a token, 30 short-convolution and 10 attention layers. The Qwen models' text and speed do not change. The shared EXL3 kernels' bytes changed (half-integer rates); `SAME_ROWS` maps them to the old bytes, so the first Qwen start adopts its saved conversations once. Reference: [docs/lfm2.5-24b-a2b.md](docs/lfm2.5-24b-a2b.md).

### LFM2.5-24B-A2B

- `engine/models/lfm2_moe/`: configuration, reference forward, pack reader, Triton row kernels, board engine. Decode step, verify block (up to 32 rows) and commit run as CUDA graphs; a verify row has the decode step's bits, checked by a self-check at load.
- Correctness: reference forward within 2.1e-5 of transformers' `Lfm2MoeForCausalLM` (tiny model, fp32). BF16 engine against transformers: top token 98.05 % of 1,024 chat positions, 19 of 20 differences near ties, KL 0.0064. 4.0 pack against exllamav3: 97.85 %, all 22 differences near ties. Trellis decode equals exllamav3 `LinearEXL3` bit for bit.

DGX Spark, 2026-10-14. Decode step: one request, 256 tokens, from its graph. Chat: one greedy request through the server, 512 tokens, thinking off, plain / lookup. Quality: exllamav3 `model_diff` against BF16 on oasst1 chat. Not the benchmark row. Raw runs: `models/lfm2.5-24b-a2b/measurements/0.8.3-summary.json`.

| profile | download | decode step, tok/s | chat, tok/s | chat KL | chat top-1 |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| `lfm25-exl3-2.5` | 8.20 GB | 188.2 | 185.4 / 175.6 | 0.313 | 78.9 % |

- Default `lfm25-exl3-3.5`. Rule: the fastest profile in chat as served (lookup on) with chat top-1 against BF16 of at least 85 %. 3.0 is faster (168.5 tok/s) at 83.6 %.
- No `-hq` profile: an exllamav3 `-hq` 4.0 served chat 9 % slower than 4.0 at a worse KL than 4.5 (0.082 against 0.063).

- Server: the checkpoint's chat template. Thinking off, from a client or the conductor, closes the `<think>` block the template always opens. Pythonic tool calls (`<|tool_call_start|>[f(a=1)]<|tool_call_end|>`) become OpenAI `tool_calls`; values are parsed as Python literals, never run. Default sampling when a request names none: temperature 0.1, top_k 50, repetition penalty 1.05.
- Conductor, Laya and the narrator on by default, with the model's fit to the router (SRV-441, [docs](docs/lfm2.5-24b-a2b.md#conductor)): Laya alone answers the class question, a turn nobody classified stays lean, and a class sets the level and budget with only its core skill in the note. On 2.5, raw / router as written / fit: four short chat asks 2,155 / 9,098 / 2,234 reasoning tokens; seven Chat-tab tasks run twice 14/14 / 12/14 / 14/14, 0 / 9 / 0 tool errors in the last two.
- The Chat tab's `present` tool: asked to open a page it wrote, the model calls it again. The router's testing packages had it check pages through the shell (6 follow-ups: 145 tool calls, 15 shell calls in the follow-ups, 113,211 reasoning tokens); with the fit 20 calls, `present` in all 6 follow-ups, 7,228 tokens.
- Three slots: 1, 2 and 3 requests at once decode 139.9, 169.1 and 177.8 tok/s in total on 4.0; each text equals its request alone. When every slot takes a plain step, one joint graph reads the weights once.

- Not on LFM2.5 yet: a draft head (none published), the shadow reader (it reads Qwen's token ids), the KV pool (off in the profiles, not verified on this model).

### The lookup without a draft head

LFM2.5 drafts with the lookup alone (`NoHead` in the shared tree drafter), cut by StairCut.

- A round with no lookup match is the plain step and is priced as one. Each round's own match decides; StairCut's class-wide skip is not consulted.
- The lookup's confidence carries its match length, so a long copy match scores above a short phrase match. BF16, store off: edit and copy 153.7 and 157.8 tok/s against 44.3 plain.
- One StairCut price file per profile (`ops/prices/lfm2.5-24b-a2b/`). Without one, the lookup cost the 2.5 pack 26 % on prose.

Effect: prose, chat and code within 5 % of plain; edit and copy asks 1.8 to 3.6 times faster; every text equal to plain decoding.

### Fixed

- A pack stored as one `model.safetensors` without an index counts as complete in `ops/use-profile.sh` and the Setup Guide. Before, a switch to the 2.5 pack downloaded it again and refused it.
- Reading a slot's `kv.length` commits nothing. Before, the health report's read committed a joint plain step twice with three slots ("LFM2 forward at 53, the state holds 54 rows").
- Attention split buffers are kept per attention class. Before, a verify graph captured at a new class freed buffers an older graph replays into (illegal memory access past 2,048 keys).
- A suffix store written by another tokenizer turns the store off instead of stopping the start.
- The dashboard's disk tier default is 16 GB, as the server's since 0.4.3 (it showed 50).
- `/v1/completions` with a text prompt and two or more slots answers. Before, the slot choice read the prompt as a tensor and the request failed with 500 (SRV-443).
- Chat tab: the plus menu draws outside the tab strip, which clipped it (VIS-133). A page a `write_file` or `edit_file` call left opens from its tool card, the plus menu's Preview and the Files viewer (VIS-135).
- Chat tab, Context panel: it counts every tool call on the branch, the files the file tools carried, the routed packages' tokens, the chat's KV rows, the resident prefix and the sandbox's memory (SRV-445, SRV-447, SRV-449, SRV-451, SRV-453). A figure it cannot show names the reason instead of a dash (VIS-137). The packages and the prompt split survive a chatd restart (SRV-455).

### Shared EXL3 kernels

- Half-integer rates (1.5, 2.5 and 3.5 bits a weight, tiles 16 K + 8 int16 wide), as exllamav3 1.6.0 writes them below 4 bpw, in the decode GEMV, the MoE bank, the prefill grouped GEMM and the slab decode. 7-bit experts in the MoE kernels.
- Whole rates unchanged: 51 of 51 kernel outputs equal the previous tree's bit for bit.

### Setup Guide

- Wren runs beside LFM2.5: on 3.5 it loads its own Qwen3.5-2B in 20 s (3.62 GiB), as the model has no narrator copy to share.
- The Tools step no longer offers turning vision off on a text-only model.

Repository hygiene for the public release: no private hostnames, home paths or personal notes in the files; no code change. The engine's modules are the bytes of 0.8.2, and the text does not change.
