## 0.8.2, 2026-10-13

0.8.2 fixes two bugs found on v0.8.0 in Open WebUI on a phone: a chat that waited minutes for slot 0 while the side slots were free (SRV-409), and Flash-Next calling itself Fable or Claude, made by Anthropic (SRV-411). The engine's modules are the same bytes as in 0.8.1; the disk tier's fingerprint does not change (the new knob is the server's).

- A request whose conversation slot 0 holds waits for slot 0 at most 3 s (`QWEN38_SIDE_SLOT0_WAIT_S`), then takes a free side slot it fits in. Live on v0.8.0 a new Open WebUI chat waited 437 s behind another chat's 496 s `write_file` generation while both side slots were free. It had matched another chat's NVMe entry at 8,192 tokens, which is only Open WebUI's system prompt and tool list, and the wait for slot 0 had no limit. The spill wait now needs an entry that reaches past the request's first user message, as the view and resident rules have since SRV-223; the log says `spill_head=` for a match at the client's head. On the side slot the prefill reads what the disk tier holds and the rest again. A request too long for every side slot still waits for slot 0.
- `/health` `parallel.max_running` is now the most requests that may run at once: every slot built, fewer only while the admission holds requests for memory, with `max_running_reason`. It used to be the high-water mark of busy slots (`max_running: 2` on three slots read as a cap); that number is `peak_running` now. New: `requested`, `spill_waits`, `slot0_gave_up`; `slot0_grants` counts again.
- The Lanes view's queued line says why a request waits: "Queued: all 3 slots are busy", "Queued: slot 0 holds its conversation; a free side slot takes it after 3 s", "Queued: too long for a side slot (65,536 tokens); waits for slot 0". While the router's questions run it says "Queued: TandemLLM decides how to handle the request first". The live feed's `queue` object carries the same `reason`.
- Asked who it is, the model now says it is TandemLLM running the served model on the user's own machine. On v0.8.0 Flash-Next answered "I'm Fable, an AI made by Anthropic" and "I'm Claude": the reference box served it with the conductor off (box values carried over from the first Flash-Next test launcher), so the identity note never went in, and Open WebUI's system prompt names only tools and skills, one of them named after another assistant. The note names the model from the served pack's model card (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next or Qwen3.8-27B; before, the note called Flash-Next Qwen3.8-27B), says it is no other assistant and not made by Anthropic or OpenAI, and goes in for every client the conductor serves: Open WebUI, opencode, the Chat tab, Hermes and any other. It stays at the end of the asking message, where the prefix cache keeps it.
- The reference box runs Flash-Next with the conductor on, with the same store and profiles as the 27B.
- Standalone EXL3 checkpoints of the 27B family load directly (#1, 0xWhiteMage): a complete BF16-origin `mul1` EXL3 pack is passed as `--model`, with no separate BF16 or FP8 base, its FP16 plain tensors re-encoded as BF16 only where every value survives the round trip (docs/quantisation.md). Vision and quantised MTP are not qualified on that path; it is text only, and speculative parallel serving still needs the `lenrouter` drafters. The 27B's own profiles (an EXL3 overlay over the base, or NVFP4) take the path they took before, so their saved conversations stay: `engine/loader.py`'s new bytes count as the old ones in the disk tier's fingerprint (`SAME_ROWS` in engine/methods/manifest.py), the first 27B start adopts the files of v0.8.0's fingerprint once, and the 27B's code fingerprint stays 0.7.2's (`9ac3d8a94c8a9199`). Flash-Next's fingerprint does not read the loader.
- Live on the reference box (Flash-Next 3.05, three slots): while one Open WebUI chat generated 2,600 tokens on slot 0 for 80 s, a new chat started on slot 1 and the next turn of the chat slot 0 had held moved to slot 2 after its 3.0 s wait; both answered while the long run went on. Asked "Who are you?" and "WHO are you?" with Open WebUI's own system prompt and 49 tools, 5 times each greedy and 5 times each sampled (temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95, top_k 20), 20 of 20 answers said "I'm TandemLLM, running the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next model on your own machine"; v0.8.0 gave 0 of 20 (Fable, Claude, Kiro, Kimi). opencode, the Chat tab and an OpenAI SDK client gave the same answer. Single-request decode, greedy, thinking off, the second of two runs: 54.5 tok/s on v0.8.0 without the conductor, 59.5 tok/s on 0.8.2 with it (the conductor's notes change the prompt, so the texts differ: no slowdown, not an A/B). Before its prefill, a new Open WebUI chat waits for the router's two questions on the served model: the class (440 tokens, about 0.55 s) and the package (2,355 tokens, about 2.0 s).
- The Flash-Next profiles load Laya (laya-english at the start, the other two on demand), as the 27B's box does, because the memory features ask only a decision model: the remember/forget/recall intent on a new user message (about 20 ms) and the background writer's gate. Without it they answered nothing on Flash-Next, so memory did not work there. Live on 3.05 with Laya loaded: "remember that my favourite colour is green" got the intent yes in 20.6 ms and the memory skill attached; the writer's gate answered yes in 20.9 ms. On 3.05 with three slots and the 262,144-token window the residency planner leaves 36.8 GiB after Laya's claim and the engine's growth to its peak (floor 15 plus margin 4). It does not shorten the router's questions: the router document's decider stage has been off on both models since 2026-10-02 (Qwen 0.949 against Laya 0.782 on 216 labelled requests), so the class question goes to the served model. Decode speed with Laya loaded: 46.8 tok/s on a fresh prompt, against 47.6 and 47.9 on the first runs before (different texts).
- The Chat tab has permission modes per chat, with a default in the chat settings (SRV-387, SRV-391). Auto is the new default: a call that stays inside the chat's sandbox runs without asking (bash, files in `/workspace`, `render_page`), and a call that leaves it still asks (`web_fetch` to a domain the chat has not fetched, an MCP tool not marked read-only, an Open WebUI tool that imports a network or process module, and `rm` aimed at `/`, `/workspace` or a home directory). Ask keeps the old prompts. YOLO asks nothing. Deny rules and plan mode's read-only list hold in every mode, and the sandbox is as locked down as before. Each call a mode allowed is logged as `tool.auto_approved` in the chat's event log, and the run shows its mode. In a test run on a phone, six bash prompts took 20 s of tapping; replayed through the new rules in Auto, all six run without asking. The chat store moves to schema 5 (`runs.permission_mode`). docs/chat.md, "Permission modes".
- "Always allow" on a chained bash command saves a rule for every part that no rule allows yet, and the prompt names them ("Always allow cd, node, echo, cat"). Before, it offered only the first part's word, which never covered the command, so the prompt came back: one chat saved "cd" 11 times for `cd /workspace && node ... > run.log 2>&1; echo "exit:$?"; cat run.log`. A second word counts as a subcommand only for programs that have them (`git push`, `npm install`), so "grep tilt" saves "grep". The chat store moves to schema 6, which keeps one copy of each duplicate rule. A command with `$(...)` or backticks still matches no rule and offers no "Always". This matters in Ask mode; Auto runs sandbox bash without asking.
- Community weight packs: one JSON file per pack under `models/<model>/community/`, checked by the registry (a pinned commit, EXL3 only, text only on the standalone path) and listed in the setup guide after our profiles as `community/<id>`. The guide fetches the index from the public repository when its weights step opens or on Refresh, never on a timer, and falls back to its last copy, then to the one in the release. `ops/use-profile.sh community/<id>` downloads a pack at its commit, checks the hub's sha256 and runs it with our drafters. The first entry is ThinkingCap Qwen3.8-27B Kearuga by 0xWhiteMage (EXL3 4.0 bpw, standalone, measured on 0.8.2: 39.6 tok/s prose, 95.9 code, 51.3 chat). docs/community-weights.md says how to add one.

## 0.8.1, 2026-10-13

0.8.1 lets a new DGX Spark run every 27B EXL3 profile and Flash-Next with public files only and no Hugging Face token (OPS-95). The engine's modules are the same bytes as in 0.8.0, so the text, the speed and the disk tier's fingerprint stay as they were. The changes are in `ops/`, `server/setup/`, the registry, `install.sh` and the docs.

- `ops/use-profile.sh` fetches the files a 27B profile reads besides its weights before it switches, and with `--fetch-only`: the K3 drafters and the K4 draft head (`0xBakeer/TandemLLM-Qwen3.8-27B-EXL3-drafters`), the BF16 drafters (`...-DFlash2-b8` and `-b16`, into `train/ft-b8-v2` and `train/ft-b16`) and the base checkpoint `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8` (into the Hugging Face cache, without `mtp.safetensors`). Before 0.8.1 these four had no download, so an `exl3-<size>` profile could not start on a new box. Each asset in `models/qwen3.8-27b/model.yaml` now says where its files come from and where they go.
- The fetcher pins every download to the hub's commit, checks each weight file against the hub's sha256, and moves a folder into place only when it is complete. The disk check runs first and counts the assets, the weights after them and the 60 GB margin. A run that stops continues where it stopped. `--dry-run` prints every file's URL and size, for the weights and for the assets.
- The EXL3 profiles read the BF16 drafters from the repository's `train/` folder. An install.sh box pointed `CKPT8` and `CKPT16` into the Hugging Face cache, whose folder names are commit hashes, so the drafter arms did not find their K3 files. With `--setup` they were empty.
- A switch from the command line on a box in setup mode removes `run/setup-pending` first, so the engine starts with the profile. A failed start puts it back and starts setup mode again.
- The setup guide's plan downloads the missing assets in its fetch step and counts them in `download_gb`. It refuses only a file with no download (`missing_assets`). Every published profile is public, so no profile asks for a token.
- `install.sh` installs v0.8.1 by default (it still named v0.4.8, which has no setup mode). With `--setup` it points `QWEN38_MODEL` at the base checkpoint's folder in its own Hugging Face cache. Its messages no longer call the repositories private.
- The switch's smoke turn goes to the engine on `127.0.0.1` unless `serve.env` or the environment sets `SMOKE_URL`. Before, it went to the reference box's own address. The smoke's model name follows the conductor, as the setup guide's does.
- New box path for testers: docs/setup.md, "A new box from the command line".

## 0.8.0, 2026-10-13

0.8.0 adds a second model, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, the Chat tab with chatd, its own chat service, and the cache peek and prewarm the Chat tab's Context panel reads. Flash-Next 3.05 is served with a 262,144-token window and three slots. The 27B's text does not change: its v2 disk-tier fingerprint is the same as 0.7.2's (`9ac3d8a94c8a9199`).

### The Chat tab

- A Chat tab in the dashboard (`#/chat`) and chatd, the service behind it (`python -m chatd` on 127.0.0.1:8016, reached through the engine's `/v1/chat-app/*`). A run belongs to the server: it goes on when the browser closes, and another device attaches mid-run and catches up from the last event it saw (docs/chat.md).
- Tools in a sandbox per chat (a locked-down container, no LAN, a memory guard that gives way to the engine), permission prompts on every device, the terminal, preview, files and diff panes, MCP servers, Open WebUI tool imports, pinned and blocked skills, plan mode with a todo list and Rewind, the PWA and local notifications.
- The Chat tab is in beta: a Beta pill beside it in the rail, in the phone's bottom bar and in the chat's header. Its known limitations are listed below.
- On a phone the bottom bar has four slots, with the other views behind More, and the composer shows every control.
- The model card in `/v1/models` (SRV-347): what a model can do, read from `models/<id>/card.json`, and what the process serves (its window, its pack, the vision tower). `POST /v1/tokenize` counts a chat body's tokens by part.

### The cache peek and prewarm (SRV-349)

- `POST /v1/cache/peek` says where a chat's rows are before it is sent (resident, the RAM park, a snapshot, the NVMe spill, the disk tier, none), how many tokens are warm and the re-read's estimate; `POST /v1/cache/prewarm` reads a chat back from the NVMe while the engine is idle. Live on the RC the peek named the tier and line of the next request in every case tried (resident, none, nvme_spill), and a prewarmed chat's next turn resumed at its end anchor.
- The usage frame carries `tandem`: the prompt by part (system, tools, history, the router's notes, images), the router's choices for the turn (`harness`), and the cache tier the prompt came from.

### Found by the RC's live checks

- A restart could leave the engine unusable on Flash-Next: the spill's restore at startup told the MTP drafter its cache was valid before reading any row back, the drafter read pages the KV pool had released, and the GPU faulted (`illegal memory access`). Every request after it failed. The rows are now committed before a drafter resumes, and it resumes again over the restored rows (the spill, the disk tier and a side slot's carry).
- Every short request the side lane took on Flash-Next failed (`'FlashNextCacheState' object has no attribute 'primed'`): the lane lends the engine with the 27B's pending commit in mind. The lane is off for an engine whose capabilities say it cannot be lent; such a request waits or takes an idle side slot.
- Flash-Next had no model card, so the Chat tab saw no thinking and no images on it, and sent an attached image as a file. It has its card now.
- A chat that last ran on a side slot came back cold after a restart. The drain now writes each side slot's conversation to the NVMe too, and its next turn reads it back through slot 0.
- The System view said PREFIX_CHUNK 1,024 needed a restart on Flash-Next, whose caches keep their own grid. It shows the grid the engine runs (4,096), locked.
- A request that arrived during a prewarm waited for the whole save and restore (1,246 ms). The prewarm now stops between blocks when a request waits and answers `yielded`; the request still waits 0.5 to 1 s.
- Right after a turn, a peek found the engine lock held by the turn's end and the idle graph captures, and answered 409. The peek and the prewarm now wait up to 3 s for the lock unless a request waits for it. A parked chat's next turn reports the park, as its peek does.
- A chat waiting for a permission prompt held one of chatd's two run slots, and two other chats ran one after the other. A run gives its slot back while it waits for the answer.
- An iPhone test (2026-10-13): a 21-step run building a clock stopped with "This conversation is about 319,136 tokens" while the engine held 16,980. chatd counted five 300 KB screenshots by their base64 text, sent each screenshot as a new user message (the model then thought the user kept repeating the request), and could not compact a run with a single user message. chatd now counts an image by its pixels, puts a tool's image inside the tool's result, keeps only the newest screenshot, and compacts a long run's earlier steps between two steps. render_page says each screenshot is a fresh render, and the sandbox runs Chromium for any command. The same prompt now finishes in 6 to 9 steps with at most 8,144 tokens of context.
- The disk tier now knows its files by content (the `fp4` fingerprint). Before, the 27B moved to a new folder threw away all 29 of its saved files (2.97 GB) because the fingerprint held folder paths. 0.7.2's files carry over in place, or from the old folder named in `QSE_DISK_ADOPT_FROM`. On the box, Flash-Next kept its 34 saved chats through the switch.
- Under the 27B's conductor the cache peek counted fewer tokens than the turn would send: it left out the memory notes a turn replays. It now replays them, and the peek's prompt matches the sent one from the second turn on.

### Chat tab (beta): known limitations

The Chat tab is in beta in this release, and a Beta pill beside it says so. We know of these limits and have not fixed them yet:

- The agent loop does not yet work the way Claude Code does (epic VIS-E10). Its prompts are not kept prefix-stable from step to step (SRV-375). Old tool results and old thinking stay in the context until a compaction (SRV-365). A compaction writes a general summary, not the task's state (SRV-373). Every sandbox command asks for permission; there is no mode that runs them without asking (SRV-387). Nothing notices when the model repeats the same failing approach with different calls (SRV-367). render_page passes on Chromium's console noise (SRV-369). Long tool output has no "see more" paging (SRV-371). Searches run in the main context, with no sub-agents (SRV-381).
- The engine reads a short Flash-Next chat again on its next turn when the answer ended inside a verified block (ENG-235).
- A request that arrives during a prewarm still waits 0.5 to 1 s (SRV-349).
- When memory reaches its ceiling, the engine drops the parked chat without writing it to the NVMe, so its next turn starts cold.
- Images only: there is no video input (VIS-97).
- The 5.05 Flash-Next pack does not load yet.
- Parallel decoding does not raise throughput over one request at a time: three requests together took 27.18 s against 27.03 s one after another, though the later ones start sooner.
- The phone layout's keyboard behaviour is not verified in Safari on an iPhone.

### Qwen3.8-Flash-Next

A second model, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, served from turboderp's EXL3 packs through the same server, caches, ops scripts and setup guide as the 27B. The 27B's text does not change: its modules, flags and disk-tier fingerprint are as in 0.7.2, and every switch added here is off for it. On Flash-Next, greedy and seeded answers with speculation equal plain decoding token for token.

- Five weight profiles, `flashnext-2.05` to `flashnext-6.05`, and a second tile in the setup guide (`models/qwen3.8-flash-next/model.yaml`). `ops/use-profile.sh` switches between the 27B and Flash-Next one engine at a time, and rolls back across models. The fetcher takes a branch of the repo, checks the hub's sha256, and links the n-gram table that the 4.05, 5.05 and 6.05 packs share.
- Each pack has its largest window in the registry: 262,144 tokens for 2.05 and 3.05, 208,896 for 4.05 with the vision tower on (212,992 without). The guide's window buttons and the estimate follow it, and a start with a longer `--max-len` is refused. 3.05 reads its n-gram table cold. Warm, the whole table resident took MemAvailable less the table to 8.4 GiB in a 146,400-token request at a 147,456-token window, under the 15 GiB floor. 6.05 fits no window on one DGX Spark.
- 5.05 does not load yet: its experts use 5 and 7 bits a weight, and the MoE kernels take 2 to 6 and 8. Its card in the guide says so.
- Speculation drafts with the pack's own MTP layer, cut by the shared StairCut. The lookup (the request's text, the corpus, the suffix store) joins the same round as one tree. Sampled requests walk the tree with the 27B's sampler.
- StairCut keeps its prices, the plain step's cost and a drafted round's cost per context class, by wall time. A class whose drafts cost more a token than plain steps takes the plain step, and a turn drafts only when the saving pays for the draft head's backlog. While idle, the server captures the graphs a context class lacks, so the first drafted request at a new length no longer pays 3.4 to 5.1 s of captures.
- All cache tiers hold Flash-Next's state (grid 4,096). A reset keeps the KV rows in place: a short request run between two turns of a long conversation used to zero rows the next turn resumed over. The resident guest stash is on again.
- The KV pool, side slots and a joint verify pass work on Flash-Next, each answer equal to its single-stream answer, and its profiles turn them on (`QSE_PARALLEL=3`, `QSE_KV_POOL=on`). Three requests arriving together took 27.18 s against 27.03 s one after the other on fresh servers, with first tokens at 2.2 to 6.1 s instead of up to about 20 s. One request alone decodes at 45.78 tok/s against 45.79 with one slot. The limits are in docs/parallel-requests.md.
- Flash-Next reads images: the pack's vision tower on the EXL3 kernels, image rows with three-axis rotary positions, on in its profiles (VIS-97). Image chats answer the same with the MTP drafter and without, and the text after an image keeps the text's own agreement with transformers (KL 0.019 after 140 image rows, 0.0025 after 2,184).
- The mixers are int8 with one fp32 scale for each group of 128 weights (`QWEN38_FN_MIX=int8`; `int8rows` is the old one scale a row). Against the pack's fp16 mixers at 8,192 tokens: KL 0.0031 on code and 0.0188 on prose, inside the kernels' own noise, where one scale a row gave 0.267 on code.
- On Flash-Next the shadow reader stays off, because its outputs were validated on the 27B's reasoning only. The conductor, the narrator and the residency planner run as on the 27B.
- `/health` and the dashboard no longer issue CUDA work when they count the engine's state. On Flash-Next, a `/health` poll during a graph capture invalidated the capture and failed the request (seen at the first decode after a 260,800-token prefill).
- Measured on 3.05 (DGX Spark, one request each): MTP alone, one greedy request of up to 512 tokens a class: prose 49, code 85, chat 62, edit 106, copy 102 tok/s. With the lookup: edit 132 and copy 133. The prefill made 571 tok/s at 260,800 tokens, with a workspace of 10.5 GiB there.
- Measured on 3.05 by context, one greedy request a length and its repeat on one fresh server, the second round, against plain decoding: 1k 56.6 and 57.3 against 41.0 and 45.4 tok/s; 32k 34.9 and 55.6 against 33.0 and 42.5; 140k 42.1 and 52.4 against 33.9 and 41.4; at 260,800 tokens the class takes plain turns, 41.0 and 41.0 against 39.6 and 40.5. All 16 texts equal plain decoding.
- Measured at 260,800 tokens, one request a pack: lowest MemAvailable (less a warm table) 25.5 GiB on 2.05 with its table warm, 31.9 on 3.05 and 17.8 on 4.05 with their tables cold; prefill 585, 571 and 581 tok/s.

## 0.7.2, 2026-10-11

Wren, the setup guide's assistant, answers a question in words again (VIS-91). The text the engine writes does not change: only `server/setup/`, `dashboard/` and the docs changed, and the engine's modules are the same bytes as in 0.7.0, so the disk caches keep their fingerprint.

- On a phone with 0.7.1, Wren answered on the Model step and then called `explain("overview")`, the name of the step. The server took a step's name as valid, the page refused it, and the page asked again, four times. "Which one is for coding tasks?" got eight lines of "Wren tried something that does not exist", the 4-round stop and no answer. The sheet dropped to a peek and rose again once per call.
- `explain` now takes only what the page can highlight: a tool, a method or advanced field, a weight profile or a parallelism field. The server and `tools.ts` check the same set.
- The prompt has the current step: the ids a tool call may name there, and on the Models, Model and Weights steps the measured table with the fastest profile for each task. It also says which profile the box runs. The question about coding tasks found the conductor's "coding" profile before; it now gets `exl3-2.5` at 124.17 tokens a second.
- An invalid change gets one repair. If the repair fails, Wren answers in words with no tools in the prompt, and the page shows one notice that nothing changed. The server drops a highlight the page cannot make, with no repair. The page's last round sends `"tools": false`, so every turn ends in words.
- A turn shows one notice at most, and none when the repair worked or only a highlight failed.
- On a phone the sheet stays open while Wren works. A change shows inside the sheet as a toast with Show me, which closes the sheet and scrolls to the field. A refused call leaves the sheet and the figure alone. The desktop panel is as before.
- On a phone the mini box's landing (0.7.1) started 60 px right of the field and widened the page by 27 px, and the fixed sheet with it, so its close button went off the screen. The setup page now clips that overflow.
- On the narrator's 4,096 rows, a long chat could cut the page's second round down to the tool's result alone, and the chat template threw "No user query found". The trim now keeps the whole turn Wren answers.
- Measured on the box (`tests/gpu/setup_wren_gpu.py cases`, Qwen3.5-2B at 4,096 rows): 15 of 15 right on ten requests for a change and five questions, the two from the report among them. No call was invalid, and a turn took 0.7 to 1.6 s. The reported conversation replayed on the same 2B: the status answer, then the coding answer in one round, then "Use two slots" in two.

## 0.7.1, 2026-10-11

Wren, the setup guide's assistant, is drawn as the gold DGX Spark box from the video "7 weeks with one DGX Spark" instead of a bird. The text does not change: only `dashboard/` changed, and the engine's modules are the same bytes as in 0.7.0, so the disk caches keep their fingerprint.

- The box has the eight states the bird had, each with its own face. Idle, it smiles and blinks. It leans toward the message box as the user types, and question marks float above it as it thinks. Loading, it half closes its eyes inside the progress ring. Its mouth opens with the streamed text of an answer. To change a field it hops toward the page, and a small copy of the box lands on that field. An error brings a sweat drop and "?!", and asleep it closes its eyes under a drifting z.
- With reduced motion each state is a still face, and no two states look the same.
- This release swaps the dashboard's `dist` on a running engine, so `/health` reports 0.7.0 until the engine's next restart.

## 0.7.0, 2026-10-11

The dashboard has a setup guide at `#/setup`, with a small assistant called Wren beside it. The text does not change: the guide is not on the serving path, a chat request never reaches it, and the engine imports it only when a `/v1/setup` route is called. [docs/setup.md](docs/setup.md) describes all of it.

- The guide walks through an install in eight steps: the model, its overview with the measured table, the weights, the tools beside the model, the parallel requests, the methods, a review and the install. Next and Previous move between them, each step has its own link, and the progress stays in the browser's storage across a reload.
- A model the browser has no progress for starts from what the box runs now: the active profile and every knob as `ops/serve.env` resolves it. Review lists only what the user changed.
- A memory bar stays at the top. It shows the box's live free memory beside the selection's estimate, part by part, and the floor, and it turns red with a sentence when the selection does not fit. One formula in `server/setup/estimate.py` gives the numbers, and the page's copy must pass the same 47 cases in `models/estimate-cases.json`. `exl3-4.5` with the recommended tools at 4 slots of 262,144 tokens comes to 67.35 GiB of a 106.63 GiB budget.
- The models the guide offers come from `models/<id>/model.yaml`. Qwen3.8-27B's file has the 7 weight profiles, the 0.6.2 table of 2026-10-10 (a test holds it equal to the run's summary file) and every tool with its memory, its `serve.env` keys and its default.
- Wren is Qwen3.5-2B on the engine's own forward with no caches, one sequence and thinking off. It answers from the docs, the manual, the registry and the packages that describe TandemLLM, and it reads the page and the box's free memory each turn. It can fill fields, tick tools, pick a profile and move between steps; the page runs each call after the server has checked it. It cannot finish, apply, reset, load or unload anything. On a serving box it loads only when asked, and it borrows the narrator's copy when that is loaded, which costs 0.03 GiB. Its own copy loads in 22 s and holds 3.62 GiB, it gives way to any request within one 150 ms slice, and it is the first thing given back when the KV pool needs memory.
- Finish starts an install job of fixed steps from `server/setup/apply.py`: wait until no request runs, write `run/setup.env`, switch the profile, and check that one chat answers. A failed switch or check brings back the old overlay and the old profile. Nothing a client sends becomes a command. The job's steps stream to the page, and the status responder keeps them coming while the engine restarts. `ops/serve.env` is never edited; it reads `run/setup.env` after the weight profile. The overlay leaves out a key serve.env leaves unset when its value is what the engine runs with anyway, so an install that changes nothing keeps the disk caches' fingerprint and the parked chats.
- Reset has five levels, in the System view and on the setup page: (1) the page's progress and Wren's chat, (2) the applied setup, (3) the caches and parked chats, (4) the weights of the profiles not in use, (5) the usage history and the conductor's data. Each lists what goes and its size, the destructive ones need a typed word, and the server refuses all of them while a request runs.
- Setup mode: `install.sh --setup` and `ops/start.sh --setup` start the dashboard and Wren alone, with no weights of Qwen's, for a box that has no configured engine yet. `/health` says `"mode": "setup"`, `/v1/models` is an empty list, and every other route answers 503 `setup_mode`.
- Every POST under `/v1/setup` must be same-origin JSON. A `text/plain` body gets 415, and a cross-site `Sec-Fetch-Site` or an `Origin` that names another host gets 403. A page on another site cannot run apply or reset through a visitor's browser, even on a box with no admin password.
- `VISION` and `RESPONSE_CACHE` in `serve.env` now reach the engine (`--vision off`, `--response-cache`). Unset, they keep the old behaviour: vision on, the response cache off.
- The KV takes 104.25 KiB a token (106,752 bytes), not 106.5 KiB. The old figure was the kB value with the KiB unit. The memory and operations docs and the manual say so; `engine/kvpool.py` keeps the old wording, because its bytes are part of the disk tier's fingerprint, and changing them would sweep the saved chats.
- `tools/exl3_fastrun.py --env-file` reads `serve.env` without `run/setup.env`, so a benchmark row has the file's knobs, not the box's last setup.
- Measured on :8000 (EXL3 6.0, 2026-10-11 night):
  - With Wren loaded on the narrator's copy, three greedy 512-token prose requests gave the same 411 tokens as three without it, and the first token's logprobs matched bit for bit. Decode ran at 148.6 tok/s with Wren and 147.5 without, and MemAvailable moved by 0.08 GiB.
  - In setup mode, Wren's own copy loaded in 30 s and held 3.62 GiB.
  - An install from `exl3-6.0` to `exl3-4.5` and back through the page took 243 s and 255 s. Both profiles kept their disk cache and their parked chats.
  - The same prompt decoded at 32.17 tok/s against 0.6.2's 32.45 (one run each).

## 0.6.2, 2026-10-10

Decoding no longer stops while another slot prefills, and the dashboard's Perf tab reads the 0.6.x live feed correctly again. The text does not change: with another engine's 8- and 512-row forwards run at all 63 layer boundaries of a 24,576-row window, the prefill's logits, KV rows, recurrent state and convolution tails, and every logit of the other engine, matched running each alone bit for bit.

- An EXL3 prefill works through its prompt in 8,192-row windows, and each window was one GPU pass of about 10 s. Other slots got the GPU only between windows, so every decoding slot stopped for the whole pass (SRV-321). A window now offers the GPU turn between its layers, only when another slot is waiting. `QSE_PARALLEL_LAYER_YIELD=off` restores the old behaviour.
- Measured on :8000 (EXL3 4.5, one run each): three streamed chats with a 37k-token uncached prompt arriving 25 s later. Seconds with no decoded token during the prefill went from 42 of 147 (the longest 10 s) to 0 of 145. The prefill beside the decoders ran at 252 → 254 tok/s, a single request decoded at 42.5 → 42.1 tok/s, and the prompt alone prefilled at 809 → 792 tok/s (within single-run noise).
- Dashboard (VIS-76):
  - The Now card's prefill bar fills again. A global tone rule in `parallel.css` had cleared the Live panel's colours.
  - Between two window marks, the bar shows a hatched estimate at the measured rate and the ETA counts down. "measuring" replaces "warming up" until the second mark.
  - The card and the prefill tile count the same total, including the harness's hidden tokens, on the same clock.
  - The 5-minute charts lose the holes the 1.007 s sampler tick left, and say "none in 5 min" when nothing ran.
  - A decode that stands still reads as "stalled behind a prefill" instead of a bare 0.
  - The Parallel view counts lanes held for memory as waiting and uses the legend's words in the In flight tile.
  - The Now line reads "4.9 of 17.2 tok/s" when several requests decode.
- The prefill's progress line is said only at a window's last chunk. Inside a window, a 47 s prefill read "about 4 min left".

## 0.6.1, 2026-10-10

The small models now give memory back when the KV pool runs short, and the dashboard's memory numbers count what is really in use. The text does not change: with the small models loaded, unloaded and loaded again, Qwen's 128 tokens, 26 blocks and prefill logits matched bit for bit.

- When the pool runs short, the order is: caches, then the shadow reader, then the narrator, then idle side conversations, then slot 0's idle conversation. Only after that does a request wait. An unloaded model is held out, so nothing loads it back on demand. It comes back through the residency planner once free memory has stayed above the floor plus its size plus 4 GiB for 60 s with nothing waiting. Laya stays loaded by default, because it decides routing and its fallback could change the text; `QSE_ROLE_UNLOAD_LAYA=on` puts it last. `QSE_ROLES_DYNAMIC=off` turns the whole feature off.
- In a live test, free memory went down to 24.9 GiB and a 31,687-token request arrived. The shadow reader went (1.82 GiB), then the narrator (3.81 GiB), then one idle side conversation. The request waited 11.5 s and finished, and both models came back 162 s and 238 s after the memory was released. Free memory never went below 21.7 GiB.
- The memory split counts the KV pool's committed pages, not the reserved address range of each slot. Before, it showed 16 GiB of KV and 10 GiB of drafter KV with 12.75 GiB in use. The bar now adds up to MemTotal minus MemAvailable.

## 0.6.0, 2026-10-10

One shared KV pool. Before this release, every slot reserved its whole window at load, so 4 slots fit only with 32,768-token side windows, and the narrator and Laya were refused. Now each slot reserves only addresses, up to 262,144 tokens, and memory pages are mapped as a conversation grows (`QSE_KV_POOL=on`). The text does not change: on 8k, 32k and 128k prompts the logits, every KV row and the GDN state match the static buffers bit for bit, and a greedy decode with the served drafters gives the same 258 tokens in the same 56 blocks.

Measured on :8000 (EXL3 4.5, 2026-10-10 night): 4 slots × 262,144, with Laya and the narrator loaded again. MemAvailable after warm-up is 58-63 GiB, against 26 GiB with the old 32k side windows. On the same 4-request load test, the aggregate went from 28.4-31.5 tok/s on 2 slots to 34.2-35.6 tok/s on 4, and the lowest MemAvailable from 23.7 to 48.5 GB. Three chats of 22k and one of 87k ran on four slots at once.

### KV memory

- `engine/kvpool.py` reserves each slot's engine KV and both drafters' context KV as CUDA virtual memory, with the old buffers' exact shape. It maps 2 MiB pages just before rows are written: every forward pass, restore, pin, park, stash, disk tier, NVMe spill and side-slot carry. No attention kernel changed, and CUDA graphs keep their pointers.
- Pages past what a slot keeps go back when its request ends.
- Under pressure, caches give memory back first, then idle side conversations, then slot 0's idle conversation (to the NVMe). A 53.7k conversation came back from the NVMe in 1.2 s.
- Admission counts the pages a request could still commit, minus what it already holds.

### Waiting instead of refusing

- A request that does not fit waits. Its stream says "waiting while memory is almost full… 1st in line" every 15 s and carries `X-Tandem-Wait: memory`, and the dashboard has a `waiting_memory` lane. A 95k-token request waited 111 s and then ran, with nothing refused. After the queue timeout, a non-streamed request gets a 503 `memory_wait_timeout`.

### Parallel decoding

- Chats decoding on side slots no longer stall while another slot prefills a long prompt (`QSE_BARRIER_IDLE_OWNER`, on by default). In a same-hour A/B they went from 4.5 to 10.7-14.3 tok/s. The long prompt's first token came 18 % later (154.8 to 182 s), because the chats now get their share of the GPU.

## 0.5.1, 2026-10-10

Two dashboard numbers were wrong, and :8000 now runs four requests at once. The text does not change.

- The cache hit counts only the client's own prompt tokens that came from a cache. Rows the conductor adds are reported apart as `hidden_tokens`. The Parallel view had shown 117.2 % (112K cached of 95.3K prompt tokens).
- The live prefill rate counts only the rows the engine computed, so reused and restored rows no longer raise it. It had shown 17,892 tok/s on a prompt that ran at about 800.
- Four parallel requests on :8000 (`QSE_PARALLEL=4`): slot 0 keeps its 262,144-token window, and the three side slots get 32,768 tokens each. With 4 slots the memory guard leaves the narrator unloaded, and about 29 GB stays free after warm-up. A load test of 2 against 4 slots is still to come.

## 0.5.0, 2026-10-09

Weight profiles. The engine serves either our NVFP4 set or an EXL3 quant of Qwen3.8-27B, from 2.5 to 6.0 bits a weight, one at a time. `ops/use-profile.sh <name>` switches between them, and the model is still `TandemLLM`. The `nvfp4` profile gives the same greedy text as 0.4.8 on the three prompts checked. An `exl3-*` profile serves other weights, so its text differs from NVFP4's. Either way, speculative decoding stays exact against whichever weights run.

Against BF16 on 8 held-out rows (16,376 positions), in this engine: NVFP4 has a KL of 0.0582 and agrees on the top token 93.35 % of the time. EXL3 4.5 has 0.0217 and 95.78 %, and reads 14.70 GB a decode step against NVFP4's 15.01.

Speed on EXL3 4.5, fast-run prompts, store off, same hour on 2026-10-09: greedy prose 41.3, chat 52.5, code 84.5 tok/s. The 50-prompt row runs 51.3 tok/s greedy and 50.9 sampled. TTFT with caches off is 8.8 s at 8k and 36.4 s at 32k.

### Weights

- EXL3 linear layers behind `QWEN38_EXL3`: one GEMM kernel per bit width from 2 to 8, for 1 to 32 verify rows. The trellis decode matches exllamav3 bit for bit. With the flag off, the engine is the 0.4.8 engine.
- Both drafters run in EXL3 at 3 bits (`QWEN38_DRAFT_EXL3`), with a 4-bit EXL3 draft head (`QWEN38_DRAFT_HEAD_EXL3`). On the 50-prompt row they move EXL3 4.5 from 49.2 to 51.3 tok/s greedy.
- Profiles live in `ops/profiles/*.env`. `ops/use-profile.sh` fetches missing weights from the private Hugging Face repo after a disk check. A smoke request follows the start; if it fails, the old profile comes back. The crons start the active profile, and `/health` and the dashboard name it.

### Prompt processing (prefill)

- Layer-major prefill windows decode each EXL3 weight slab once a window instead of once a 1,024-row chunk. With caches on, 32k goes from 52.2 to 42.2 s.
- A prefill MLP bridge feeds the prefill MLP's products straight into the down projection: 8k from 9.7 to 8.8 s, 32k from 39.1 to 36.3 s, caches off. Both are bit-identical.

### Sampling

- A sampled round costs what a greedy one does: top-p reads each row's top 1,024 logits and the draws stay on the device, 97.4 to 89.1 ms a round.
- `QWEN38_SAMPLE_NUCLEUS` (on by default) draws inside each row's nucleus. The kept set is bit-identical, and the sampled-distribution gate passes.

### Attention

- Verify attention runs three pipeline stages: 24 rows at 64k drop from 118.9 to 107.9 ms, bit-identical.

### Tools

- `tools/exl3`: the Hugging Face Jobs pipeline that built the six EXL3 sizes.
- Also new: the lattice oracle, the sampled-tree replay and the drafter ranking-loss options. The ranking fine-tune (RND-37) gave no gain, and its tools stay for reuse.

## 0.4.8, 2026-10-08

Two Open WebUI chats beside each other, after a user report of 2026-10-08 (two chats that took turns on slot 0 with the side slot idle, and a chat read again cold, 60,814 tokens in 91 s, after its retrieval block moved). The text does not change: every resume here is held to the end anchor's gate.

Speed guard short gate on the 0.4.8-test engine code (2026-10-08 14:31, store off, one run a side, same hour): release 0.3.0 49.75, 0.4.8-test 50.64 tok/s mean (+1.8 %), 93.52 and 93.75 ms a round.

### The router's notes

- A note stays live when the client changed the prompt before its message: besides the prefix hash it remembers the user message it closes (its ordinal) and the last 32 client tokens before it, and moves to that message's new end when the hash breaks (`QWEN38_NOTE_ANCHOR`). Open WebUI's retrieval block leaving an earlier message had dropped every note of the session and put the whole class note in again on every new message (5.8k tokens a message).
- A warm-up prefill of 2,600 tokens at start on slot 0 and on every side slot (`QWEN38_WARM_PREFILL_TOKENS`), so the first requests after a restart do not pay for the prefill kernels' first shapes.
- A new chat of at most 16,384 rendered tokens beside a conversation a side slot could never hold waits up to `QWEN38_SIDE_NEW_WAIT_S` (20 s) for a busy side slot before it takes slot 0 and sends that conversation to the NVMe: the eviction costs the long chat's next turn, the wait costs the new chat's first token only.

### Parallel requests

- A side slot takes a request whose window leaves it at least 16,384 rows of output, with `max_tokens` cut to the room (`QWEN38_SIDE_MIN_ROOM`). 0.4.7 compared the window with the prompt plus the whole served limit of 32,768, so a chat past about 24,000 tokens could never take the 65,536-token side slot.
- A side slot has a resident prefix of its own (`QWEN38_SIDE_RESIDENT_GB`, `QWEN38_SIDE_STASH_GB`): the next turn of the conversation it holds resumes at the end anchor there (`home`), beside slot 0's conversation, which stays where it is; the router's question in between leaves it in place through the stash. The carry into slot 0 stays the fallback when that slot is busy for `QWEN38_SIDE_HOME_WAIT_S` or the prompt outgrew the window.
- A new conversation beside one a side slot could never hold takes an idle side slot before slot 0 (`QWEN38_SIDE_NEW_FIRST`), so the long conversation is not evicted for it.

### Caches

- The end alignment's third pass: a block the client put into an earlier user message and moved to its last one (Open WebUI's retrieval block, on every request in the last user message) is served from the rows where the model saw it, token-aligned on the bare bytes, only when the same bytes are in the last message; a message the user edited is served as sent (`QWEN38_END_ALIGN_MOVED`). Without it the copy parted from the rows at the first message and the chat was read again cold on every new message.
- A long prompt the end anchor does not serve says why in the log and the journal (`[cache] ... re-read ahead`, `extra.reread`: the position and message the copy parts at, what the alignment refused) (`QWEN38_REREAD_SAY_TOKENS`).

## 0.4.7, 2026-10-08

The release after the 0.4.0 tree. It is 0.3.51-test (the 0.4.0 candidate) plus everything in 0.4.1-test to 0.4.7-test below, the manual, and the proxy documentation of the in-process DeepSeek relay. The 0.4.0 tree was never published; 0.4.7 replaces it. The text changes on purpose in three places: a regenerate under TandemLLM samples, Continue Response continues the partial answer, and the package documents change what the router attaches.

Speed guard short gate on the same engine code (0.4.7-test, 2026-10-08, store off, one run a side, same hour): release 0.3.0 50.38, 0.4.7 49.93 tok/s mean (-0.9 %), 93.73 and 93.74 ms a round.

### Caches

- A long Open WebUI chat comes back from the NVMe after other chats ran: the restore offer asks the end alignment too, and a restore never evicts the entry it reads next. A 48k-token chat came back in 1.0 s with a TTFT of 2.3 s; a cold read takes about 70 s (0.4.2-test).
- The session spill is compressed losslessly: byte planes plus zstd level 1, 1.71x on the rows of a real 48,853-token entry, checked bit for bit. The spill budget is 64 GB, the disk tier 16 GB, and the NVMe gets a daily write budget of 200 GB (`/health` `cache.disk_writes`) (0.4.3-test).
- A conversation that ran on a side slot is carried into slot 0 with its rows and end state. A non-streamed answer keeps its end anchor. The park writes a conversation it gives up to the NVMe first (0.4.1-test).
- A deploy that only registers a knob keeps the disk's heads and conversations. The fingerprint reads `engine/settings.py` by the defaults of the knobs the engine reads, and it now reads the `tools/` modules the engine imports. The first start adopts the old formula's files once (`fp-equal.json`). 0.4.6-test had swept 13 heads (12.4 GB) and 13 spilled conversations (29.6 GB) at its start (0.4.7-test).
- Open WebUI chats own their NVMe entries (`X-OpenWebUI-Chat-Id`), so one chat no longer takes another chat's entry: back in a chat after two others in 1.9 s, 6.9 s before (0.4.7-test).

### Packages

- The first packages (the system set `tandem-core`, `render-tools`, `eval-judge`, and `creative-coding`, `charts`, `voxel-worlds`, `explainer-video`) and the everyday library: 34 tool-free packages plus `everyday-core` and `reply-format` (0.4.4-test to 0.4.7-test).
- Every prose class offers the whole everyday set; the router asks for a package once per class (`package_sticky: class`) and on an idle side slot, not on every new message and never over slot 0's conversation (0.4.6-test, 0.4.7-test).
- The everyday packages were measured against no package: 91 pairs, mean +1.19 of 5, judged by the served model, indicative only. Five ship off (`schema.EVERYDAY_OFF`). Everyday answers draft first, with a placeholder where only the user knows the fact, and never stop on a form (0.4.7-test).
- The testing package deletes only the scratch folder its own run made (`.tandem/<session token>`), and files-care never deletes what the conversation did not create (0.4.7-test).

### Requests and answers

- Regenerate gives a different answer: it samples at temperature 0.7, top-p 0.95, top-k 20 with a fresh seed, and every other answer stays greedy (ledger schema 9, `sampling`) (0.4.4-test).
- Open WebUI's Continue Response continues the partial answer instead of writing a new one from the title (0.4.7-test).
- A memory note the store refuses is never shown as text, and a project note without a working directory lands at user scope (0.4.5-test).
- Laya stays out of the plan and the lines between tool calls; a refused Laya request says what was wrong and exits 2, a network failure still exits 3 (0.4.1-test, 0.4.5-test).

### Dashboard, settings, tests

- The usage filter lists come from two new ledger indexes: the 365-day query is 845 ms cold and 110 ms warm (1,096 and 341 ms before). Seven server knobs are in the settings registry, and the CPU suite is green (0.4.6-test).
- The Deciders screen says why a model is not loaded (0.4.1-test).

### Manual and documentation

- `manual/`: the TandemLLM manual as a LaTeX book, with the HTTP reference (`manual/tools/http_ref.py`) and the reference tables (`manual/tools/gen_reference.py`) generated from the code. `.github/workflows/manual.yml` builds the PDF only for a pushed `v*` tag and attaches it to that release.
- `docs/proxy.md`: the in-process relay's first live run and the `serve.env` lines. The proxy's start line names the config database's schema version.

## 0.4.7-test, 2026-10-08

0.4.6-test (b7be6e8) with the fixes for UX3's first regressions (FX15) and PKG3's measured package documents (v25-v27, router v21, below). The package texts go in as the box's packages v28 (`tools/packages_migrate.py --put`, edit 34, and the everyday skill copies), the router as v22 (`package_sticky: class` on the five prose classes). `~/rollback-0.4.7.sh` restores packages v27, router v21 and the skill copies and returns the box to 0.4.6-test. Speed guard short gate (2026-10-08, store off, one run a side, same hour): release 0.3.0 50.38 -> 0.4.7-test 49.93 tok/s mean (-0.9 %), 93.73 -> 93.74 ms a round; no noise estimate by design.

### A deploy that only registers a knob keeps the disk's heads and conversations (FX15)

- 0.4.6-test changed nothing under `engine/` but `engine/settings.py`, where FX14 registered seven server knobs. The disk tier's fingerprint hashed every engine module's bytes, so that alone swept the 13 shared heads (12.4 GB) and the session spill's 13 conversations (29.6 GB) at its start: UX3's first Open WebUI chat read its 6.7k-token head cold (TTFT 14.3 s, 0.3.49 2.7 s), and the big chats kept on the NVMe went with it.
- The fingerprint now reads `engine/settings.py` by the defaults of the knobs the engine and the kernels read (a server knob's registration changes nothing), and it reads the `tools/` modules the engine imports, which it never did (a kernel change kept rows another kernel wrote). The first start under the new formula adopts the files of the old one computed on the same tree and records that in `fp-equal.json`; later builds read them only under the same fingerprint. `tests/test_fp_equivalents.py`.

### The package question once per class, on a side slot (FX15)

- Router v21 offers 34 everyday options on every prose class, and the package question (about 2,360 tokens) ran on every new user message: W02's "make it shorter" asked again and got the package the first note already held. The class policy's `package_sticky: class`, set on the five prose classes (router v22): a follow-up the class question keeps in the session's class takes the package picked for it (`how: sticky`); a class change or an answer of none asks again. The coding classes keep `message` (the old rule, also the default without a value; `classifier.package_sticky` sets the default): a coding session's next message is often another task with another skill (`tests/test_note_dedup.py`). `tests/test_package_sticky.py`.
- The router's questions take an idle side slot whenever slot 0 holds a conversation: the side-slot rule (`_guest_of_slot0`) no longer bounds a guest by a quarter of the conversation's length, a bound that belongs to a guest ON slot 0 (its stash). The package question over an 8.1k Open WebUI chat (limit 2,028) ran on slot 0, displaced the chat's end anchor (the next turn resumed at 0.96-0.98 and read 250-670 tokens again) and cost 3.3 s when it missed its own head there. `tests/test_resident_guard.py`.
- A side slot taken by the router's own question (or a side-lane job) notes no end to carry: the package question is longer than two chunks, and on build 1 its end was noted as a conversation, the next package question (same options) was carried into slot 0 over the chat, which was parked, and the note kept the next guests off the side slot for 10 minutes (live W01/W02).

### Everyday answers draft first; no form, no stop to ask (FX15)

- W04: "Help me write a short cover letter ..." picked cv-cover-letter, whose step 1 said to ask for the experience "if the whole document depends on it", and everyday-core said "ask that one question and stop there". The model opened Open WebUI's blocking `ask_user` form; the message never finished and the user's next two messages queued in the client. everyday-core now says to take the likely value, state it in one line, put a [placeholder] where only the user knows the fact and give the whole result; never ask through a tool or a form, never stop a draft to ask. Eleven packages lose their "ask the one question" lines the same way (cv-cover-letter, checklist-builder, budget-plan, difficult-conversation, homework-help, tech-troubleshoot, translate, decision-helper, compare-options, weekly-schedule, parenting-help); the quiz turn and the practice conversation keep their question, which is the task. cv-cover-letter's `max_tokens` 950 -> 1050, everyday-core's 550 -> 650. `tests/test_everyday_draft_first.py`.

### The testing package deletes only the scratch its own run made (FX15)

- PKG3's A01 run (opencode in a user's existing project) ran `rm -rf /home/user/pago/.tandem`, a folder with the user's own test kit, by the rule "a {tandem_scratch} left by an earlier run ... delete it before you start". The scratch is now the conversation's own folder (`.tandem/<session token>`, `.tandem/session` without one); the run marks it when it makes it and deletes it before "done" only with the mark; a leftover is reused and nothing is deleted at the start; files-care: never delete a file or folder this conversation did not create. `tests/test_scratch_owner.py` runs the commands themselves next to a user's `.tandem`.

### Continue Response continues; Open WebUI chats own their NVMe entries (FX15; W17, SRV-285)

- W17: Open WebUI's "Continue Response" after Stop sends the conversation with the partial answer last. Every prompt was rendered with a generation prompt, so the partial was closed and a new answer started from the title (chatcmpl-9ea66357: 77 reasoning tokens, then 1,613 tokens; the saved answer held the story twice). A last assistant message with text and no tool calls is now continued (`app.continues_final`: the template's `continue_final_message`, the turn left open after its closed think block, no new reasoning); the body's `continue_final_message` or `add_generation_prompt` decide when given. The head is the earlier prompt's to the user turn's end, the note stays there, and a Continue is still not a regenerate. `tests/test_continue_final.py`.
- SRV-285: the caches' owner key read the body's ids and opencode's `x-session-id`, never `X-OpenWebUI-Chat-Id`, so every Open WebUI spill entry had no owner and a chat that shared a pasted document with another took the other's entry (F57: back in 6.9 s against 1.8 s on 0.4.1). The owner is now `c:<chat id>` when the body names none; an owned save never takes another owner's entry and an owner-less one never takes an owned one. `tests/test_session_spill.py`.

### Earlier on main (PKG3, packages v25-v27 and router v21, documents only)

Live on the box (2026-10-08 00:26, 41a5b3d, about 4.5 min down; serve.env, router v19 and the DeepSeek relay kept): a dedicated test user in an Open WebUI-shaped chat asked for a project note, and it landed at user scope (`rescoped: project`) with no markup in the answer; W05 PASS (no_leak, follow-ups 1.00 at the end anchor, TTFT 1.4-2.0 s); O03 PASS with 0 of 13 visible text parts naming Laya (7 on 0.4.1-test), while the model wrote the new helper and used Laya twice; the helper against the live route: an empty text exit 2 "LAYA not asked", a duplicate label exit 2 with "choices: a label is listed twice (field: choices)" (0.4.4-test: exit 3 "LAYA unavailable (HTTP Error 422)"); W18 PASS (overlap 6.5 s on slots 0/1); DeepSeek flash 200.

### A memory note the store refuses is never shown (SRV-277; QA SRV-278)

- In an Open WebUI chat (0.4.3-test, W05) the model wrote a `<tandem_memory scope="project">` block. The chat has no working directory, so the store refused it (`no_project`), and the stream filter sent the refused block to the user as text, by design ("a block that is not taken goes out as the text it was").
- Now every closed block is hidden from the client, written or not: one over 2,000 characters, the fifth of an answer, one the schema or the store refused. The reason goes to the journal (`memory_notes`/`write`, the row's `extra.memory.failed`) and one log line, and the block's tokens are a hidden span like a written block's, so the next turn still resumes at the end anchor. Only text that is not a closed block goes out as written (an unclosed block, one still open after 4,000 characters, `<tandem_memoryx`).
- A project-scoped note in a conversation without a working directory (every Open WebUI chat, a script) lands at user scope (`rescoped: project`), since every client is the one user and a note is meant to be read back in the next conversation (SRV-173).

### Laya stays out of the progress lines too (SRV-259; QA SRV-260)

- 0.4.1-test took Laya out of opencode's closing message, but 7 lines between tool calls in O03 still named it ("3. Ask Laya about the diff evidence", "Now the Laya verdicts on the key outputs"). The texts said only that the final message keeps Laya out.
- Packages edits 30-31: the texts that keep Laya out of the final message (test-lib, test-web, test-cli, test-api, test-data, testing, coding, tandem-harness, laya-testing) now say the plan and every line between tool calls reach the user too, and a check is named by what it checks. Guidance only; nothing filters the output.

### A refused Laya request says what was wrong (SRV-279; QA SRV-280)

- In O03 the model piped its evidence into a heredoc script (`tail ... | python3 - <<'EOF'`), so the text was empty and the route answered 422. The helper caught every HTTP error as a network failure ("LAYA unavailable ... your code is not the cause"), and the model told the user "Laya is unavailable on this machine (transport error)".
- Packages edits 32-33: the helper sends no empty text ("LAYA not asked: the evidence text is empty ...", exit 2), and a 4xx other than 429 prints the route's message and field ("LAYA refused this request (HTTP 422): choices: a label is listed twice (field: choices). The request is wrong, not the network: fix it and ask again", exit 2). A refused connection, TLS, a timeout, 429 or 5xx is still "unavailable" (exit 3). laya-testing says a refused request is the model's to fix. The route's empty-text message says what to send; its `param` is unchanged.

## 0.4.3-test, 2026-10-07

0.4.2-test (6fee8d3) with the spill compressed, the disk budgets of SRV-271's option A and a daily NVMe write budget, deployed on the box as 0.4.3-test. `~/rollback-0.4.3.sh` returns the box to 0.4.2-test. The text is the same: every cache restores exact state, and the codec is lossless.

### The spill entries compressed losslessly (SRV-275; QA SRV-276)

- A spill entry is the model's computed state, not text: 104 KiB a token (the target's 16 attention layers' K and V, 64 KiB, and the two drafters' K and V, 40 KiB, all BF16) and 0.77 GB of recurrent-state anchors an entry. The 182,000-row Open WebUI chat of 2026-10-07 was a 20.16 GB entry.
- New blocks are written as byte planes compressed with zstd level 1 (`engine/spill.py`, `--session-spill-codec`, `SESSION_SPILL_CODEC`, on): the planes are cut and joined on the device, the host compresses 8 MiB frames on 8 threads, one block while the one before it is written. On a real 48,853-token entry the rows go 5.20 -> 3.04 GB (1.71x; target 1.45x, drafters 2.39x), the entry 5.97 -> 3.81 GB; compress 4.5 GB/s, decompress 10.8 GB/s; the read of the compressed blocks plus their decompression took 0.93 s against 0.97 s for the raw O_DIRECT read. `tools/spill_codec_check.py` ran every block of two real entries through the codec: bit for bit. The block sums are checked on the device after every read, as before.
- Entries on the disk are read either way; a 0.4.2 entry written again keeps its unchanged blocks and compresses the new ones. The fingerprint skips the spill's files, so the deploy keeps every entry.
- Measured and not taken: plain zstd (1.27x target), zstd level 3, the fp32 recurrent state (1.17x), 2 anchors instead of 4. Lossy storage (FP8 KV, BF16 recurrent state) is reported in docs/caches.md and not implemented.
- To verify live: a long chat evicted and read back: the save line shows `codec=zs1` and about 0.6x bytes, the restore line, cached 0.95 or more, TTFT within 1.5x of 0.4.2's restore.

### The disk budgets: spill 64 GB, head cache 16 GB (SRV-271 option A)

- The session spill's budget 40 -> 64 GB (`--session-spill-gb`, now passed by `ops/start.sh` from `SESSION_SPILL_GB`, and `settings.memory.session_spill.budget_gb` live); the disk tier's 50 -> 16 GB (code and schema default; the box's settings document was set live before this deploy). The 50 GB free-space floor stays. Compressed, a 182k chat is about 12.1 GB: 64 GB holds about five.

### A daily NVMe write budget (SRV-273; QA SRV-274)

- SMART on the box's 1 TB drive: 11.6 TB written, 1 % used. The disk tier and the spill wrote 137 to 282 GB a day (10-04 to 10-07). `engine/disk_cache.py::WriteGuard` counts both per local day (kept across restarts in `writes.json`); past `--disk-write-budget-gb` (200, `DISK_WRITE_BUDGET_GB`, `settings.memory.disk_writes.budget_gb` live) the tier writes nothing and the spill only a drain and evictions of 32,768 tokens or more; past 1.5x only the drain. Skips are logged (`[disk-guard] skip`) and counted; `/health` `cache.disk_writes` shows the day's GB, the level and 14 days.

## 0.4.2-test, 2026-10-07

0.4.1-test (585856d) and one fix, deployed on the box as 0.4.2-test. `~/rollback-0.4.2.sh` returns the box to 0.4.1-test.

### A long Open WebUI chat comes back from the NVMe after other chats ran (SRV-269; QA SRV-270)

- Live on 0.4.1-test: back in a 130,381-token Open WebUI chat after two other chats, the engine read the whole chat again cold (about 4 minutes at ~510 tokens a second) while it sat on the NVMe (182,053 rows with the reasoning, 20 GB, `end=True`). The restore's offer (`Entry.offer`) accepted the end anchor only through the hidden spans; Open WebUI's copy leaves every earlier answer's reasoning out, which only the end alignment (SRV-239) serves, so no entry was offered.
- The offer now asks the end alignment too, on the entry's own tokens, end anchor and saved regions (`EndAlign.offers`, `SessionSpill.offer_align`, wired in `server/diskcache.py` `wire_end_align`). A copy that differs in more than whitespace and the reasoning is offered a grid anchor at most, as before. The end anchor of a replayed or aligned copy is bounded by the prompt it is served as (the rows up to the end and the copy's tail), not by the copy's own length: the copy is shorter than the rows by what its client left out (130,381 tokens against an end at 182,053), and the first build of this fix (6bb9028) still stopped at a grid anchor there (live round trip: line 104,448 of 105,734).
- At a full disk budget, the restore's save of the resident conversation (before it reads the entry asked for) could evict that very entry, least recently used, and the read then failed into a cold prefill. No sweep evicts the entry a restore reads next; the resident conversation is then not written (`refused.room`).
- To verify live: a long Open WebUI-shaped chat, three other chats, back: `[spill] restore` in the log, cached 0.95 or more, TTFT under 15 s.

Under the store's 1 GiB entry cap (about 7,400 tokens) it cloned a snapshot, which settles the block's pending commit, then declined it as ahead of its key; the end anchor could no longer be cut back (5 of 45 non-streamed first turns on 0.3.50-test). A save now reuses an entry only when it matches it to within its last 4 chunks; another chat gets its own entry.

### Open WebUI's "Thought for" is the thinking (SRV-237, SRV-249)

- Open WebUI 0.11.4 times a reasoning block from its first `reasoning_content` delta to its first content delta. The reading and waiting lines went out as reasoning, so a summary with thinking off that read 12,874 tokens showed "Thought for 14 seconds" (its block held only the two reading lines) and a one-line answer that waited 35.8 s showed "Thought for 34 seconds".
- For the client kinds in `QWEN38_STATUS_CLIENTS` (default `open-webui`; empty restores the profile's channel) every line said before the model's first generated token goes out as an Open WebUI `status` event (`{"choices": [], "event": {"type": "status", ...}}`), the line under the model's name that its tools use; at the first token one `done` event says what the wait was ("Read 12,874 tokens in 14 s", "Waited 31 s, then read ..."). The reasoning opens with the model's own first piece; a turn that does not think shows no "Thought for". A refusal after a wait closes the status line first.
- The waiting line's estimate reads the holder's own work (`queue_wait.Live`): the prefill it still has to read at its live rate, plus the 75th percentile of what earlier requests of its kind (thinking or not) wrote past the tokens it has written, at its own decode rate, capped by its `max_tokens`. Replayed over the box's ledger (3,716 client requests, the waiter arriving at 10 to 90 % of each hold): for waits of 10 to 60 s the old estimate was a median 0.52 of the real wait (78 % too low), the new one 1.06 (42 %); over a minute 0.17 against 0.59. Waits under 10 s now read about twice their length. Without a view of the holder the hold-time median stays.

### The dashboard on a phone, and the speed check (VIS-66, VIS-68)

- An editor's save bar no longer floats over the conductor's cards when nothing is unsaved (Deciders at 390 px hid "a load now: refused"; Monitor too, also at 768 px, Chromium and WebKit): idle bars sit in the page's flow; unsaved edits keep Save above the tab bar. e2e "an idle save bar covers nothing" (6 screens, 390 and 768 px).
- The speed guard is no warning banner on the Conductor view any more. System → Engine and the Dev tab's model card carry one neutral "speed check" line ("passed for <build> · <date>", "not run for this build"); a one-run short gate whose mean and p50 dropped no more than 5 % reads as passed; Compare keeps the numbers in a muted line. A release tree ships its report as `release/speed-guard.json` (`tools/speed_guard.py ship`), listed by `GET /v1/conductor/evals`.

## 0.3.50-test, 2026-10-07

0.3.49-test (e6970f5) with seven fixes from the normal-user scenario run and FX7's measurements (SRV-243, SRV-239, SRV-245 with SRV-219, SRV-247, SRV-233, SRV-250, SRV-235; QA SRV-244, SRV-240, SRV-246, SRV-220, SRV-248, SRV-234, SRV-236). Under a conductor profile an API client that names no `reasoning_format` now gets `reasoning_content` (a changed default), and the follow-up of an answer that thought is served with that answer's reasoning.

### A chat gets the packages its tools can carry out (SRV-243)

- A plain Open WebUI chat (its tools: search_web, fetch_url) asking for a landing page got the testing and Laya packages, which tell the model to run a shell and write files. It called `terminal` and `write_file` ('Tool not found'), fetched the library's address with fetch_url, wrote the page into a failed call and printed it again: 518 s on 0.3.48-test; a snake game 423 s, a 3D garden 522 s.
- The router reads what the request's tools can do off their schemas (a shell: a `command` argument; a file write: a path and a content argument). A package names what its steps need in `requires_tools` (absent: a shell when its text calls TandemLLM through `{tandem_url}`); one the tools cannot carry out stays out or gives way to its `fallback` (`coding` to the new `coding-answer`; on the reference box `web-design` to `web-design-answer`, packages v18), and the note says which tools the chat has and to deliver the files in the answer. The harness, library and memory routes need a shell too. Decision rows: `extra.tools`. `QWEN38_TOOL_FIT=off` keeps every package.
- Live on 0.3.50-test (n = 1 each): W10 one request, no tool call, 294 s (315 s with `web-design-answer`); W11 195 s and its fix turn 116 s; W12 248 s; notes of 404 to 2,321 tokens instead of 4,562 to 7,590. What is left is the model's own work: 7,000 to 10,000 reasoning tokens and an 8,000 to 9,000-token page.

### The follow-up of an answer that thought resumes at its end (SRV-239)

- Open WebUI sends an answer back without its reasoning; the Qwen3.8 template renders it as an empty `<think>` block, so the client's copy parted from the engine's rows right after `<think>` and the turn resumed at the grid line below. Six of six Open WebUI chats whose first answer thought re-read it on the first follow-up (0.71 to 0.89, TTFT 2.5 to 5.0 s), and a long chat resumed at the grid on every turn after one that thought (W05: 0.985 falling to 0.947).
- The end alignment remembers where each generation's reasoning ends and, when the copy does not align as the rows are, aligns it with the reasoning taken out; the prompt is served with the rows' tokens to the end anchor (the reasoning the engine wrote included, as the template renders it for a client that sends it) and resumes there. `QWEN38_END_ALIGN_REASONING=off` is the old rule.
- A/B on 0.3.49-test, one build, the follow-up without the reasoning against with it as `reasoning_content` (n = 2 each): 0 tokens reused against 309 and 319. On 0.3.50-test with an Open WebUI-sized head: without the reasoning 6,324 to 6,340 client tokens reused at the end anchor, TTFT 112 to 131 ms, like the copy with it. Live first follow-ups: W02 7,300 of 7,315 (TTFT 0.17 s; 0.83 and 3.96 s on 0.3.48), W03 6,880 of 6,897, W04 7,018 of 7,044, W15 6,774 of 6,990, W16 7,095 of 7,116, W17 after Stop and Continue 8,276 of 8,306 (TTFT 1.0 s; 5.0 s before).

### API clients get a clean answer (SRV-245, SRV-219, SRV-247)

- Every client kind but the Hermes agent gets `reasoning_content` when it names no format (`QWEN38_CLIENT_REASONING=*=reasoning_content,hermes=tags`): an OpenAI SDK printed the thinking as its answer, and opencode with the installer's config showed literal `<think>` text. `reasoning_format: tags` keeps the tags. The answer starts with its first character.
- `stop` strings apply to the answer only: `stop: ["\n\n"]` ended a response inside the thinking with no answer; now it returns the first paragraph (P04). State lines never go into a plain client's `content`.
- A request that offered no tools never gets `tool_calls`; a call in the answer is dropped (`extra.calls_refused`), and a request without a shell gets the memory index without its routes. P08: "What is my UX1 pet?" answers "I don't have any note about a UX1 pet", finish `stop` (0.3.48-test: a call to a tool named `tool`, finish `tool_calls`).

### A trivial instruction stays cheap (SRV-235)

- "Reply with just: OK. Do not use any tools." in a new opencode session went to code_edit (0.80) at xhigh with the 4.9k-token coding package: 9.3 s to "OK". Unquoted, the class question put chat first at 0.41, under the 0.45 accept, so a first message fell back to the profile's default class (code_edit); quoted, as the scenario sent it, Qwen said code_edit 0.80.
- The chat class now covers an instruction about the reply itself (answer in one word, say OK, confirm, stop) that asks for no work on code, files, commands or git (router v17 on the box, the shipped router). On the labelled sets (308 prompts) and 20 short opencode messages (`tests/fixtures/conductor/short_prompts.jsonl`, 10 about the reply, 10 coding) the live class question went from 286 to 297 of 328 right (the prose set 18 to 27, the task set 198 to 200, long 51 to 51, short 19 to 19); two answers got worse ("Commit the changes with a short message" is chat, "What does ASAP stand for?" code_edit). Live in opencode: the OK message is chat at 0.999, no note, TTFT 2.3 s; "fix the failing test in textstats.py" stays debug at 0.999 with the coding package.

### cached_tokens counts the client's tokens (SRV-233)

- The hidden rows inside the cached span counted as client tokens: an opencode turn that re-read 3,827 of its 24,706 client tokens reported 24,706 cached. The server now tracks where the hidden tokens sit and reports the client's tokens below the resume point (20,879 for that turn). Ledger schema 8 adds `engine_cached`, `forwarded_tokens` and `wait_mem_ms`.

### The parallel admission sizes a request by what it needs (SRV-250)

- A request counted the workspace floor plus a whole state-store entry (2.1 GiB for 576 tokens) against 6.4 to 8.4 GiB of cache budgets: at the box's idle MemAvailable a 576-token title request waited 63 and 83 s beside a 9,000-token one, booked as prefill. Now its need is its own prefill workspace, and the caches' growth, the requests in flight and its own together are capped by the engine's room to `--mem-peak-gib` (every cache asks the memory policy before it grows and every prefill passes its gate); the wait is queue time (`wait_mem_ms`) with a waiting line, and the alone path says so.

## 0.3.49-test, 2026-10-07

0.3.48-test (c16b27c) with four fixes from the normal-user scenario run (SRV-223, SRV-225, SRV-227, SRV-231; QA SRV-224, SRV-226, SRV-228, SRV-232). Raw and bench text are unchanged.

### A second chat no longer waits for the first

- The cause (SRV-223): with `--parallel 2` a request "continued" slot 0's conversation when it shared all of its rows but the last chunk. Open WebUI's system prompt and tool block (about 6,700 tokens) are the same for every chat, so beside a conversation shorter than that head plus one chunk every new chat of the same client counted as its next turn and waited for slot 0. W18 on 0.3.48-test: '17 x 23' in a second tab shared 6,675 of slot 0's 7,096 rows and waited 35.8 s while slot 1 was idle.
- Both continuation tests (the client view and the resident rows) now also require the shared part to reach past the end of the request's first user message (`_conv_start`, the chat template's `<|im_start|>user ... <|im_end|>` marks). `QWEN38_SIDE_CONV=off` is the old rule; the `[parallel]` line says `new conversation (shared head N)`.
- Live on 0.3.49-test (W18, n = 1): the second tab ran on slot 1 inside the first tab's 67 s essay, queue 1.29 s (the side slot was finishing the router's 412-token question), TTFT 2.6 s, 6,144 of its 6,695 tokens from the disk tier, answer 391; Open WebUI showed "Thought for less than a second".

### A side slot reads the disk tier (SRV-231)

- A side slot had no disk tier, so a new chat there prefilled its client's whole head (0.3.48-test: Open WebUI 6,687 tokens, 9.0 s TTFT; an opencode first turn 19.1 s on slot 1 against 10.7 s on slot 0). It now reads slot 0's tier through a read-only view (server/diskcache.py `SideReader`): find and restore into the side engine's own buffers; no line counted, no write, no fence of slot 0's write-behind jobs. `/health` `parallel.side_disk`; `QWEN38_SIDE_DISK=off` is the old slot. A/B on 0.3.49-test with the tier's mode switched (W18 tab B, a new Open WebUI chat on slot 1, n = 2 each): TTFT 9.6/9.8 s off, 1.9/1.9 s on. Across builds (O03's opencode first turn on slot 1, n = 1): 19.1 s with 12,570 tokens forwarded on 0.3.48-test, 10.5 s with 5,603 on 0.3.49-test (what is left is mostly the router's 5,310-token note, which no cache holds on a side slot). `tests/test_disk_cache.py`: a restore into an engine with a shorter window equals its cold prefill bit for bit.

### One conductor session per Open WebUI chat (SRV-225)

- Open WebUI sends no chat id by default, and the session key fell back to a hash of the head up to the first user message: every chat that opened with the same sentence was one session (A01: a new chat's first row counted 27 turns and 21,216 session tokens of earlier chats and replayed their 4 notes).
- The engine reads `X-OpenWebUI-Chat-Id` as a conversation id. On the reference box Open WebUI's TandemLLM connection sends it as a connection header (`{"X-OpenWebUI-Chat-Id": "{{CHAT_ID}}"}`), not through `ENABLE_FORWARD_USER_INFO_HEADERS`, which would send the user's name and email to every connection (docs/operations.md, Open WebUI).
- Without an id, a head holds a list of conversations: a conversation's first turn starts its own session (`h:<hash>#n`) when the newest one of that head has had a turn; a later turn finds its own by a hash of its whole first turn as the client sends it back. Decision rows carry `extra.session` (`id`, `new`, `continued`, `alias`). `QWEN38_SESSION_GENERATIONS=off` is the old rule.

### A new folder never replaces the user's files (SRV-227)

- "Create a new folder and create there a pagoda garden" ran `mkdir -p pagoda-garden` on an existing folder and wrote index.html over the user's page without reading it or saying so. The tools run in the client, so the fix is what the model is told: the general package `files-care` (a new folder or file gets a free name, a file is read before it changes, a replaced file is copied first, the answer says so) on every class that writes files (code_edit, debug, design_ui, drawing, three_d); packages v16 and router v16 on the box.
