## 0.3.47-test, 2026-10-06

0.3.46-test (6f985a4) with the fix for a new user message that read a long conversation again (SRV-207, SRV-209; QA SRV-208, SRV-210). Raw and bench text are unchanged.

### A short request no longer costs the conversation slot 0 holds

- The cause (SRV-207, one build, replayed on the live engine, n = 1 each): with `--parallel 2` the first request's residency document set the memory ceiling and peak back to their configured 70 and 77 GiB, so the 7.65 GiB the side slot took at the load came out of the caches' room. Every cache was then refused (one evening on 0.3.46-test: 131 anchors, 2 guest stashes, a park, a pin), and the router's own questions before a new user message (its class and its package, 410 and 169 tokens), which run as guests of the conversation, cut its rows at their start when their stash was refused. A 32,875-token conversation and two new user messages: 0 % of the prompt from the cache at the 70 GiB ceiling (67.5 s and 70.7 s), 99.9 % and 99.3 % at 78 GiB (6.4 s and 9.4 s). In the box's logs of that day, the two processes started with one sequence (0.3.42-test) kept every guest's stash (318 guests, none cut); the cut appears only in processes with a side slot.
- The side slots' bytes are kept apart in the memory policy (`Budget.fixed`, `/health` `cache.memory.fixed`) and added to every value the ceiling and peak get, from the flags or a residency document.
- With parallel requests, a guest of slot 0's conversation (short, sharing less than one chunk with it, while slot 0 holds two chunks or more) takes an idle side slot first and leaves slot 0's rows alone (`QWEN38_SIDE_GUESTS`, default `on`; `off` is 0.3.46-test's slot 0 with the stash). The router's questions and a client's title, tags and follow-up tasks are such requests.
- A guest's stash holds the rows the guest can write (its prompt, its `max_tokens`, 2,048 rows for the monitor's hidden tokens, two 512-row margins), not every row its 1 GiB budget holds: a 410-token question asked the memory policy for 1 GiB.

### A new task skill no longer brings the whole note again (third build, SRV-211)

- Live on the second build (17fcb69), Open WebUI agent chat: every user message of the coding class whose task skill differed from the last one's (`test-lib`, none, `test-cli`) brought the router's whole note again, the five general packages included (about 4,800 tokens each time); the dedup key covered the whole block. The third copy pushed the replayed notes over `injection.max_replay_tokens` (16,000), the oldest note went, the prompt changed at its position (12,292) and the turn read 35,442 tokens again (49 s) while the client's own tokens had not changed.
- A class's note now carries only the parts (the effort sentence, each package, the rules) that no live note of the session holds with the same text; every part live, no note (`QWEN38_NOTE_DEDUP`, `parts`; `block` is the old rule). The proxy's harness follows the same rule.
- Replayed with one conversation shape on the live engine (n = 1 each; a 20,000-token document in the second message, then four code messages that pick four task skills): on the second build the fifth message read everything again (cached share 0.000, 60.7 s) and messages three to six took 115.6 s; on the third build (c2af3fe) every one of them read from the cache (cached share 1.000) and they took 17.3 s, the replayed notes 6,040 tokens instead of 15,406.

### Open WebUI's working directory

- Open WebUI appends the terminal's live working directory to `run_command`'s description, in the system prompt's tool block (SRV-209). The first `cd` of an agent changed the prompt about 4,800 tokens in, and the next user message read the conversation again (live: 41,749 tokens, 56 s, of which the cache could have served about 4,800). Under a conductor plan that is on, the sentence moves into a router note at the turn where the directory changed and replays there (`QWEN38_CLIENT_CWD`, default `note`; `off`: the tools as sent).

- `laya_drive.py page URL --step ...`, the kit's one-command check of a page (SRV-195): its own headless Chrome, real clicks and keys, values read back, screenshots at 1280 and 390 px, console errors, uncaught exceptions and failed loads, Laya's verdict, Chrome closed on every path, about 5 s. opencode had found no node, npx or Chrome on its PATH, only Firefox, and spent seven minutes on a Marionette driver of its own after the page was written.

## 0.3.44-test, 2026-10-06

0.3.43-test (a3bf8a5) with parallel requests made workable beside the small models, and no in-flight limit from the proxy on other backends (OPS-69, QA OPS-70). A design decision: parallel requests at 4 or 2, with Laya and the narrator (the describer) always loaded, so three models. With `--parallel 1` (the shipped default) a request is served as before, and the text is unchanged.

### Parallel requests

- `--side-graphs off` (`QSE_SIDE_GRAPHS`): a side slot verifies eager when it decodes alone and holds no CUDA graph pool. A joint pass of two decoding slots is eager either way, so the slot loses its graphs only for the stretches it decodes alone, and it costs its window plus about 1.5 GiB instead of 7.5. The build's estimate follows the switch; `QSE_SIDE_SLOT_CONST_GB` overrides it. `/health`'s `parallel.slots[].graphs` says which slots hold graphs. The default stays `on`.
- docs/parallel-requests.md "Beside the small models": the memory plan of a 128 GB box with Laya, the narrator and two sequences, why the side window is 65,536 and not 8,192 (the conductor's margin and the clients' `max_tokens`), the planner's claims, and what Laya and the narrator do while two requests run.
- The reference box serves two requests at once from this version (its serve.env, not the shipped one).

### The proxy

- No in-flight limit from us: a relayed backend (another TandemLLM, vLLM, SGLang, an OpenAI-compatible server, a cloud API) takes as many requests at once as clients send, unless its `max_inflight` is set (1 to 4,096; the form's field empty, `null`, or `TANDEM_BACKEND_<ID>_MAX_INFLIGHT=none` is no limit). Until now every backend got 64 without asking and a 65th request got a 503. The config file moves to schema 2, which turns a stored 64 into none and keeps any other number.
- The Backends screen shows the field empty with "no limit", the card without "/64", and a line for this engine's own settings: how many requests it decodes at once, its decision models and its narrator. The parallel setting is the engine's, not a backend's.

The UT2 essay went to code_edit at 0.57 (chat 0.29 behind it); on the labelled sets plus 32 prose prompts the guard changed two essays and nothing else.

### Restarts

- The status responder answers `GET /v1/models` (and `/v1/models/{id}`) with 200 and the engine's last model list, kept in the status file by `set up` (OPS-67): Open WebUI dropped TandemLLM from its list on the 503 and a chat said only "Model not found". Chat requests keep the 503 with the engine's own sentence. The reference box's Pi model-list merger asks the responder when the engine lists nothing.

### The dashboard and the ledger

- TandemLLM's own calls to itself (the router's question to the engine) are client kind `internal` (VIS-60): left out of Usage, the summary, the counters, the filters and Recent requests unless "show internal" is on, each naming the request it served. Ledger schema 6: `parent_request`; the migration relabels the router's earlier rows once (`meta.relabel_internal`). Contract: `internal` in the client kinds, `parent_request` on a request row, `filters.internal`.
- The Live panel's cached tokens are never above the client's prompt; TandemLLM's notes show as their own figure, `+N hidden` (VIS-58, `hidden_tokens` in the live rows).

## 0.3.42-test, 2026-10-06

0.3.41-test (a0a943a) with the dashboard's password prompts removed (VIS-56, QA VIS-57). A user report: the memories should be visible with no password prompt anywhere in the UI; when a password applies is decided later. The engine, the API and the text are unchanged.

### Access

- The admin password is the admin token, `QSE_ADMIN_TOKEN` (`TANDEM_ADMIN_TOKEN` for the standalone proxy), and it is the one switch. With none set, every admin route answers anyone who reaches the port: the conductor's writes, every memory route (notes, transcripts, the disk tier), the decision models, `/v1/config` writes, both cache routes and the full `/health`. Until now they answered 404 with no token (fail closed), and with a token the dashboard asked for it. `/metrics` keeps the metrics token when `QSE_METRICS_TOKEN` is set, for Prometheus. With a password set, the rule is the one before, unchanged (server/auth.py `Auth.password_set`; docs/server.md "The admin rule").
- `GET /v1/dashboard/session` says `password_set`; with no password it answers `login: false` whatever `--dashboard-login` says (contract session 1.1, additive). The startup line says "admin password: not set ... keep this server on a trusted network". A conductor version written from the network with no password has the author `open <address>`.
- `ops/make-secrets.sh` writes only the metrics token unless `--admin` asks for the password, so making a Prometheus token no longer locks the dashboard.

### The dashboard

- No password prompt anywhere: the sign-in screen, the sign-out button, the token dialog ("Admin token needed", "Unlock editing"), the Memory view's sign-in state and the token kept in the browser are gone, and no request carries a token. A token an older build stored is deleted on load. Conductor > Memory shows its transcripts, notes and disk tier at once, and a note is edited and saved straight away. With a password set on the server, a 401 shows a text banner and the views show the error; the sign-in for that comes later.
- The box: `QSE_ADMIN_TOKEN` is out of `secrets.env` (the old file kept as a backup); the metrics token stays for the Pi's scrape.

## 0.3.41-test, 2026-10-06

0.3.40-test (0c48e92) with the eleven fixes from a user-level self-test the same morning (UT1: 23 scenarios as an ordinary user would run them, raw API, opencode, the dashboard at 1440 and 390 px), and one test-helper race. A request without these shapes is served as before, and the raw path is untouched; the text of the shipped testing packages changed (below).

### Requests and usage

- A malformed request is a 400 that names its field: empty or missing `messages`, an unknown role, a system prompt alone or only tool results (no user message), a system message after the conversation began, `max_tokens` or `max_completion_tokens` below 1, an empty completion `prompt`, a body that is not a JSON object, and a prompt that renders to no token. They used to be `500 internal_error` with the chat template's exception text, which OpenAI clients retry, and `max_tokens: -5` was served as a one-token answer. OpenAI's `developer` role is the system prompt, and a system plus a developer message become one system prompt (SRV-167; `tests/test_compat.py`).
- `usage.prompt_tokens` is what the client sent. The router's notes (this turn's and the session's replayed ones) and the closed think block of a turn it turned thinking off were counted: a "hi" reported 238 prompt tokens under the chat profile, 11 raw. They are `usage.prompt_tokens_details.hidden_tokens` now (absent when there are none), `cached_tokens` stays within the client's count, and the Playground shows a "hidden" figure (SRV-165; `tests/test_conductor_e2e.py` checks the count against a server without the conductor, turn after turn).
- A JSON answer (`response_format` `json_object` or `json_schema`) whose client names no `reasoning_format` gets the thinking in `reasoning_content`, so `json.loads(message.content)` works; it also gets the answer reserve, so the thinking cannot spend `max_tokens` and cut the JSON, and it carries no state lines. A client that asks for `tags` keeps them (SRV-169).

### The conductor

- The bare compaction shape (no tools, no system text, one user message of 2,000 characters or more) is a compaction only when the client is opencode. A pasted document with "summarize" from any other client had that shape and was journaled as a compaction, thinking off, with the line "the conversation was compacted" (SRV-175).
- One user (a design decision, 2026-10-06): every client is the engine's one user, `owner`, so a curl "remember that ..." is a note in that user's store, as it should be. A request keeps out with `X-Tandem-Memory: off` (no card, no read, no write, journaled `why: header`) or `read` (the reads, and a block the model writes anyway is hidden and dropped). Live checks and tests send `off` (SRV-173; docs/memory.md).
- The waiting line said "waiting while the shadow model reads the conversation, 1st in line, about 10 s left" every time: the shadow job yields at its next chunk, so it counted as 0 s, and the rounding made every estimate "10 s". The ledger's waits behind it were 0.1 to 3 s. The line is in plain words now ("TandemLLM finishes its background work first"), there is none for a wait under 2 s, the estimate behind such work is the median of the waits measured behind it, and below 10 s it reads in seconds. Each request's time behind TandemLLM's own work is the ledger's `wait_own_ms` (schema version 5, added in place) (SRV-177).

### The testing packages

- They named the provider by a literal LAN address (`https://ai-api.example.lan`) where the token belongs (the box's saved packages, versions 3 to 7). On the Spark, whose trust store lacks the LAN's private root CA, every Laya call failed TLS, and the dupfinder session spent 94 s of 222 s (42 %) debugging certificates. The texts use `{tandem_url}` only, and a package that calls `/v1/laya`, `/v1/library` or `/v1/memory` at a literal address is refused at save. `QWEN38_TANDEM_URL` sets the address the notes give instead of the request's own. The Laya helper exits 3 with one line when the call fails ("the call failed on this machine, your code is not the cause"), and laya-testing tells the model to go on without the verdict (SRV-163).
- Scratch files (the logs, the Laya helper, the playtest kit and its log, pid files) go to `{tandem_scratch}`, `.tandem` in the project by default, which the model adds to `.git/info/exclude` when it creates it and deletes as its last step before "done"; `QWEN38_TANDEM_SCRATCH` names another place (`/tmp/tandem-{token}` for a client without a directory sandbox: opencode asks before any path outside the project, and its `run` mode rejects it). In all three opencode sessions of the self-test the user's project ended with `.tandem/` in it. A state hook (`tandem_state`, `/__state`, `--dump-state`) is scaffolding the model wraps in `tandem-test-hook` comments and removes before "done" unless the user asked for one, and the model never downloads a runtime or an executable (the todo session fetched `bun` from GitHub) (SRV-171).
- `tools/packages_migrate.py` applies these edits to the shipped texts, a box's saved `packages` document (a new version, the old ones kept) and its skill copies; a second run changes nothing (`tests/test_package_texts.py`).

### Operations and the dashboard

- While the engine is away, the service says so. `ops/start.sh`, `stop.sh` and `hold.sh` write `logs/engine-status.json` (the state, since when, a hold's reason and budget, the last five start times), and `ops/engine_status.py`'s responder (`QSE_STATUS_PORT`, 127.0.0.1) answers the reverse proxy's fallback: a page for `/dashboard/` that says what is going on and opens the dashboard when `/health` answers, and an OpenAI-shaped 503 with `Retry-After` for the API. The proxy's old fallback said "vLLM cold start takes ~5 min" for a 22-minute hold. An open dashboard shows the same facts in its offline banner (OPS-65; docs/operations.md has the nginx snippet).
- The admin-token dialog closes on Escape and on a route change, gives the focus back, and is one dialog for calls that need it at once; a read says "Admin token needed" for its view instead of "Unlock editing", and after Cancel the Memory view shows a sign-in state. It used to stay over the next page and block the sidebar (VIS-52).
- `/v1/dashboard/system` says `proxy.mode: off` on an engine without `--backends`, and the Backends view reads it first: it no longer asks `/v1/config` (a 404 in the console on every visit and poll) (VIS-54).

### Tests

- New: `tests/test_package_texts.py`, `tests/test_engine_status.py`, `dashboard/tests/away.test.ts`; added to: `test_compat.py`, `test_usage.py`, `test_conductor_e2e.py`, `test_conductor_router.py`, `test_compaction_turns.py`, `test_memory_router.py`, `test_queue_wait.py`, `test_fake_engine.py`, `test_laya_drive_kit.py` (the kit runs from a scratch copy), the Playwright specs `memory` and `backends`.
- `tests/proxy_util.py`: `rows()` waits until every completion request the test sent was accounted. The relay accounts after the client has read the answer, so under the box suite's parallel load `test_proxy_relay.py` sometimes read the ledger first.

## 0.3.40-test, 2026-10-06

0.3.39-test (ab89d54) with parallel requests merged (0.3.38-test, below; `--parallel N`, off by default) and four fixes from an Open WebUI agent chat on 2026-10-06 at 06:11 (five requests, one session): the client turned thinking off and the router said it was on, a stopped looping call sent back five times byte for byte, the loop guard's latency, and the client's no-repeat mask on code. With the flag off and none of these shapes the request and the stream are the release's.

### Thinking off is the client's, and says so

- Open WebUI's agent model sent `reasoning_effort: "none"`. The template closed the thinking block (the ceiling rule: none is off), but the router's row read `thinking: on` at the class's xhigh, and its note told the model "Reasoning effort is set to xhigh. Please think carefully ..." in a turn that could not think.
- An explicit off in any form is now the row's `thinking: off_client`, no budget, and `extra.client_thinking` ("client turned thinking off", the field, the level that did not run); the dashboard reads "thinking off (client)". The effort sentence is left out of such a turn (`effort_note_skipped:client_off`); a package's and the class's rules stay. The 10-03 ruling stands: the client's word is a ceiling and none is off, under every profile.

### The retry storm after a stopped call

- The A1 guard stopped the `write_file` call at 6,400 tokens (a 405-character unit, 7.3 copies). Open WebUI answered the never-closed call with a tool error and sent the conversation again with its 6,400 tokens of arguments in the history; the model copied them, 5 times (about 55 s each, the prompt 17,692 to 46,419 tokens). The note at the prompt's tail changed nothing.
- `server/argloop.py` `collapse_history`: an assistant call whose arguments do not parse (or a value of opencode's `invalid` stand-in) whose tail is periodic keeps its first 1,500 characters and one marker; a call that parses is never touched. The incident's arguments: 15,444 characters, 1,756 kept. Done before the router, the monitor or the template read the messages; `--argloop off|log` leaves the history alone.
- The retry streak is read from the markers after the last user message. The retry's note names the tool and the piece and says when the same loop came again; the router thinks one level up (at least medium) on it unless the client turned thinking off (`extra.argloop_retry`).
- After two identical stops in a row (or three of one tool) the next request is not generated: A1's `GIVE_UP` (`tool_arg_loop_retries(n)`), one sentence, finish `stop`, no call, so the client's tool loop ends. Served like a cached answer, nothing remembered.
- `tests/test_argloop.py` 8 and 9: Open WebUI's loop on the fake engine, five attempts become two generations and the sentence; the real template's prompt carries the marker, not the loop.

### The loop guard at three copies of a long unit

- A unit of 256 characters or more fires at 3 copies over 384 tokens; shorter units keep 6 copies over 1,024 tokens. The incident's call, replayed (`tools/argloop_fp.py --replay`): stopped at token 5,760, 448 tokens after the loop began, against 6,336 and 1,024. Synthetic loops of 405 to 4,000 characters stop at about half the tokens (714 against 1,418 at 405).
- False positives (`tools/argloop_fp.py`, the served tokenizer): opencode's 4,780 legit writes and edits, 0 fire before and after; 9 synthetic legit shapes that repeat on purpose (sprites, identical frames, tile maps, tables), 1 fires before and after (600 zeros written out, 38 identical lines). Three identical frames in a row do not fire; a fourth would. The numbers are in docs/server.md.
- `tools/argloop_fp.py`: the tiers' worst legit stretches, `--synthetic`, `--replay`.

### The client's no-repeat mask on code

- The same requests carried `no_repeat_ngram_size: 4`: 4 nats off every token that would repeat a 4-gram of the conversation, which in code (indentation, pixel rows, `", "`) is the text itself. Under the conductor a client's `no_repeat_ngram_size` is now dropped on the code classes' turns and on every turn that offers tools (`extra.penalty_dropped`, a `[penalty]` log line); the server's default stays and raw requests keep it. No A/B was run, so nothing here says the mask caused that chat's degeneration.

### Parallel requests in 0.4.0

- `parallel-a` (66a76a9) merged; conflicts only in VERSION and this file. [docs/parallel-requests.md](docs/parallel-requests.md) (new): switching it on, the flags, the memory, the numbers, the text.

### Tests

- `tests/test_argloop.py` 7 to 10 (new, 11), `tests/test_client_budgets.py` (the client-off row, no effort sentence, the penalty rule), the dashboard's `didWhat`.
- The box's CPU suite (205 files) on the fixes: 205 of 205. On the merge alone 204 of 205: `test_proxy_relay.py` failed under the suite's four-way load and passed alone. The dashboard's vitest: 403 of 403.

### Measured on the box, and live (single runs, needs verification)

- Identity gate against 0.3.39-test (ab89d54), flags off: PASS. One request at a time (the atlas row, store off, `--no-learn-cost`): 0.3.39-test 49.96 mean tok/s (93.4 ms a block, p90 62.04), this release with `--parallel` off 50.39 (93.5, p90 62.09).
- Parallel requests after the merge (`--parallel 4 --side-max-len 8192`, the four bench prompts, one pass): one at a time 48.35 (median), two at once 65.83 in total (1.36x), four 67.00 (1.39x); every two- and four-request window showed that many slots decoding at once (59 and 80 two-way rounds, 45 four-way), no timeouts. PAR1's numbers were 48.8, 67.4 and 69.2.
- Live on :8000 after the deploy: smoke 27/27 raw, on and coding; ledger rows kept. A tool-call request with `reasoning_effort: none`: the row reads `thinking: off_client` (`extra.client_thinking`: `reasoning_effort`, level xhigh), the effort part was not injected, 0 reasoning tokens, the call made. The same request without an effort word: xhigh, thinking on, the effort part injected, 98 reasoning tokens before the call.
- `tools/argloop_live.py --owui` (the incident's shape: Open WebUI's agent loop, a 412-character frame the prompt asks to write out 40 times by hand): with `reasoning_effort: none` the first call stopped at 1,024 tokens (4 copies, the long rule at its first check), the retry's prompt grew by 198 tokens instead of the call's length (the history cut, 1,837 characters to a 50-character head and the marker), the model looped again on the explicit instruction, and the third request got the give-up sentence in 0.0 s with no call: three attempts, 23.5 s, where the incident ran five of about 55 s. ## 0.3.39-test, 2026-10-05

0.3.37-test (2186a22) with memory recall in a new session fixed, and three release leftovers. The request and the stream are the release's with memory off (identity gate against 2186a22); with memory on, the matching notes' note reads differently.

### Recall in a new session

- The report (CLIP1's demo, live 0.3.37-test, coding profile, memory on, 21:35): a new session asked "Which node version does the build of this project need?", the ratified note "build requires node 20" showed `uses 1` and `body_notes 0`, and the model searched the files and answered from them.
- The body was attached. The journal row of that request has `bodies: [6ac3fbaed97d]` (BM25 11.8), and the prompt carried the card (227 tokens), the index (180) and the body (113) at its tail. Two things were wrong:
  - `body_notes` counted nothing on a first turn: `mark_injected` added the index's and the bodies' ids to `index_notes` whenever the index went in. Each is now counted as itself.
  - The note asked the model not to use it. Every hidden note is framed by the router's wrapper, "Follow it and do not mention it", and the bodies' head only said they match. The model never named the note and went to the files. The bodies now have their own frame: the notes are the user's, the model may tell the user what one says; the head asks it to answer from a note that answers the message, to say it comes from its notes (a ratified note is confirmed by the user), and to tell the user both when the files disagree. The other notes keep the wrapper. Still a tail note, within the same caps.
- The model can no longer archive a ratified note. In the recall check before this deploy (live 0.3.37-test, 22:33), a fresh session read the note, found no Node build in the demo's Python project, and archived the user's ratified note ("› forgot: build requires node 20"). Ratify, pin and delete are the user's: the model's archive of a ratified note now makes it provisional again, with its reason in the note's changelog, and the client gets no `forgot` line. Its own provisional notes it still archives. `tests/test_memory_notes.py` `test_model_archive_of_a_ratified_note` (new).
- `tests/test_memory_router.py` `test_fresh_session_recall` (new): CLIP1's case on the fake engine (the ratified project note, opencode's title request, the question in a new session): the body goes in on the first turn after the index, in its own frame, and the counts read one index note and one body.

### Release leftovers

- `--no-learn-cost`'s help no longer says a block's choice stops depending on timings: it takes out what earlier requests taught the router, and timings inside the request still size its blocks (docs/exactness.md). `--relax-tau` and `--relax-rank` say what 1 means instead of "lossless": only the target's own token is accepted, and greedy output agrees with plain greedy decoding up to a near tie.
- `tools/lane_check.py` compares tokens, not texts: B and A2 must be A1's tokens up to the first fork, and the fork a near tie (each run took the other's runner-up, the top-2 gap within `--tie-nats`, 0.125 nats, in both rows). It prints the fork and both gaps. Before, a byte compare of the texts failed at a near tie with no bug behind it. `tests/test_lane_check.py` (new, 5).

## 0.3.38-test, 2026-10-05

0.3.37-test (2186a22) with parallel requests, phase A, behind `--parallel N` (`QSE_PARALLEL`), off by default: with the flag off (the service's setting) the engine is the release's (identity gate against 2186a22: PASS) and so are the 13 plain requests of `tools/api_text_check.py` with the routers' learned costs frozen (`--no-learn-cost`, both passes byte-identical, also with `--parallel 2` and one request at a time).

### Parallel requests (docs/server.md, "Parallel requests")

- `--parallel N` builds N - 1 side slots beside the engine (`server/slots.py`): each a full sequence (KV, recurrent state, verify graphs, drafter stack) over the one copy of the weights, `--side-max-len` tokens long (65,536); slot 0 keeps the 262,144 window and every cache. A request that finds slot 0 busy takes a free side slot when it fits, has no images and does not continue slot 0's resident conversation.
- The GPU turn: every slot's GPU work runs in its turns, offered back between blocks and prefill chunks (virtual time); whoever holds the engine lock holds the turn as slot 0.
- Lockstep rounds: two or more decoding slots verify their trees in one pass (`engine/model.py` `forward_tree_multi`, every projection once over all the slots' rows), each tree cut to its share so the pass stays at or under 32 rows (16 a slot at two, 10 at three, 8 at four). A chain-shaped block verifies alone; a slot alone keeps its graphed verify.
- Admission by bytes: a request's worst case (its prefill's workspace and one state-store entry) is reserved; with others in flight it waits while MemAvailable less the caches' growth and every reservation would fall under `--parallel-floor-gb` (15). A side slot is built only under the same floor: 104 KiB a token of window plus 7.5 GiB (measured 6.9 to 7.5 GiB for an 8,192-token slot, most of it its 121 verify graphs' pools).
- `/health`, the System page and the Parallel view carry the slots, the turn, the rounds by size and the admission (only with side slots, so a single-sequence server's documents are unchanged); the Parallel view shows each engine lane's slot and the engine's slots.
- The packed draft (`--parallel-draft on`): the decoding slots' draft calls in one pass over the drafter, from CUDA graphs per set of drafters (`engine/drafters/draft_graph.py` `packed_draft`, from branch `par`).
- `--parallel-cut joint` (off by default): the round cuts every slot's whole tree to the pass's rows, best nodes first across the slots, instead of fixed shares. In one same-hour pair it left two requests where they were (64.2 against 64.4 tok/s) and took four from 69.2 to 76.5, with more texts moved at near ties (two requests: 0 of 4 identical to alone, gaps up to 0.116 nats), so the fixed shares stay the default.
- Tools: `tools/parallel_bench.py` (c1/c2/c4 totals, each request against its alone text, the concurrency proof and the round's parts from `/health`, `--prompt-set wide` for 30 prompts), `tools/parallel_verify_check.py` (the joint pass against each slot's own verify on the real model), `tools/packed_draft_check.py`.

### Measured on the box (single runs, needs verification)

Single runs on the box, store off unless noted, thinking off, greedy; "needs verification" until repeated.

- One request at a time (the atlas row, `--no-learn-cost`, A/B/A/B in the same hours): 0.3.37-test 50.42, 49.12, 50.35 mean tok/s (93.4 to 93.5 ms a block); this release with `--parallel 2` 50.12, 50.82, 51.14 (93.6 to 93.8 ms a block). In one later hour: 0.3.37-test 49.29 and 49.75 (95.1 and 94.4 ms a block), this release with the flag off 49.54 (94.7), with `--parallel 2` 50.59 (94.6). With the clean store: 49.93 against 49.81. The 13 plain requests: byte-identical to 0.3.37-test.
- Four long-answer prompts, 384 tokens each, `--parallel 4 --side-max-len 8192`, packed draft on: each alone 47.8, 68.7, 36.3 and 49.8 tok/s (median 48.8); two at once 76.5 and 58.2 tok/s in total for the two pairs (38 a request); all four at once 69.2 in total (19 a request). Every two- and four-request window showed that many slots decoding and joint passes of that many blocks (59 to 80 two-way passes a pair, 45 four-way passes); none queued.
- A joint pass of two blocks takes 94 to 98 ms on the GPU, of four 114 to 119 ms; a slot's round at two requests 125 to 145 ms, at four 226 ms. The packed draft took 9 to 13 ms off the two-request round.
- Beside other requests a request's text equals its alone text up to a near tie: on 30 prompts (prose, code and chat, 256 tokens) 17 of 30 identical at two requests and 15 of 30 at four, every first difference at a top-2 logprob gap of 0.0019 to 0.118 nats. The packed draft proposes bit for bit what each slot's own draft does. The joint pass's logits equal each slot's own (eager) verify bit for bit (40 of 40 rounds, `tools/parallel_verify_check.py`).
- A side slot of 8,192 tokens takes 6.9 to 7.5 GiB beyond its window, most of it its verify graphs' pools.

### Tests

- `tests/test_slots.py` (new, 15), `tests/test_parallel_verify.py` (new, 6: the joint pass equals each engine's own verify bit for bit on the CPU; two and three requests in lockstep write the tokens each writes alone), `tests/test_parallel_app.py` (new, 4: the fake engine over HTTP, three streams at once, a fourth waits, the admission holds a request, flag off one at a time), `tests/test_packed_draft.py` (new, 3); the dashboard's vitest and a Playwright spec for the slots.

## 0.3.37-test, 2026-10-05

0.3.36-test (5b04bbc) with a crash fixed: :8000 died after three hours of metrics scrapes ("Fatal Python error: bool_dealloc", 2026-10-05 13:12, the first time). The request and the stream are the release's (identity gate against 5b04bbc).

### The crash

- torch 2.13.0's `torch._C._cuda_memorySnapshot` gives back one reference too many on every item of the tuple it is handed. Each `MemPool.snapshot()` took one reference off `True` and one off each of the pool's id ints, which are shared singletons on Python 3.11. `Placement.pool_bytes` called it for the narrator's and the shadow reader's pools on every `Budget.memory()`, and since 0.3.34-test's `role_exclude` every one of the 30 `/metrics` collectors reaches that through `cache_stats()`: 30 to 60 references a scrape. After 732 scrapes `True` reached 0 and the process died in whatever line let go of the next reference (a disk-cache gauge's lambda). Measured on the box's CPU: 1000 calls take 1000 references off `True` and off each id int; the call handed `None` takes none.
- The pools are now read from that call (every segment), filtered by `segment_pool_id`; one snapshot serves the calls of 0.25 s (one scrape's 30).
- `server/refwatch.py`: every 30 s the reference counts of `True`, `False`, `None`, `0` and `1`; a count under half its high is logged with its fall rate and the time to 0. `/health`'s `memory` part carries the counts (`python_refs`). Python 3.11 only: from 3.12 these objects are immortal.
- `tests/test_pool_snapshot_refcount.py` (new, 6): the upstream leak as measured; `pool_bytes` 2000 times keeps every reference (before: -2000 on `True`, on `0` and on the id int); the pool's segments from the full snapshot, never a tuple; the watch; the `/health` counts.

## 0.3.36-test, 2026-10-05

0.3.35-test (c718bbd) with the image path's packages in the lock and its backend pinned, the writer's switches on the Backends screen, two steadier checks, and the proxy's writer checked against real engines. The request and the stream are the release's (identity gate against c718bbd).

### The image path's packages (a user report)

- A user installed TandemLLM in a plain PyTorch container and had to add Pillow and torchvision by hand. `server/images.py` decodes with Pillow, and transformers 5.12 builds Qwen3.8's image processor on torchvision (`Qwen2VLImageProcessor`, torchvision.transforms.v2) when torchvision 0.27 or later is installed, else on Pillow (`Qwen2VLImageProcessorPil`). Neither was in install.sh's lock.
- The lock now has `pillow==11.3.0` and `torchvision==0.28.0+cu130` (from the CUDA 13.0 index, the build that matches torch 2.13.0+cu130), and the README's requirements name both, with the pip line for an existing PyTorch container. install.sh's check after the install imports both and prints the image processor class it resolved.
- The backend is pinned: `--image-backend torchvision` (the default; `QSE_IMAGE_BACKEND`). The two backends are not the same numbers: after a resize a patch value differs by up to two 8-bit levels (measured on the box: 0.4 % of the bf16 values of a 1000x333 image, none for an image that is not resized), so the digest the caches key on and the tower's input depended on what was installed. Every served measurement ran torchvision. A backend that does not resolve stops the start with the package to install, never a silent fallback; `--image-backend pil` is the explicit choice without torchvision, and `--vision off` serves text only.
- No `engine` extra in pyproject: torch and torchvision must be the matched CUDA 13.0 pair from the PyTorch index, which an extra cannot say, and an extra resolving torchvision from PyPI could replace a container's torch. install.sh's lock stays the one list.
- `tests/test_engine_deps.py` (new, 8): the lock has both packages and a torchvision build that matches torch; the README and the install check name them; every import of `server/images.py` is the standard library, the repo or the lock; a fresh interpreter that decodes a PNG and runs Qwen3.8's processor on the pinned backend loads no package outside the lock that the image packages require, and the processor's own module imports torchvision unconditionally; `load_processor` refuses transformers' silent fallback. Taking pillow or torchvision out of the lock fails three of them.

### The background writer on the Backends screen

- A backend's form has the writer's four switches: mode (auto, off, shadow, on), the spend cap a day with a no-cap box, runs a day, and the prompt cap. Only the fields that changed are sent (a default stays unset); a field a `TANDEM_BACKEND_<ID>_WRITER*` variable sets is locked and names it. The mode's hint says what auto resolves to for this kind and, in shadow, where the would-be blocks go. Phone width: one column.
- A backend's page shows the day's runs and spend against the caps, each model's resolved mode and why (auto, a paid cloud model, the backend's switch, lowered by the settings), and in shadow the log's place. Its card says `writer <mode>`.
- The Backends API adds `writer.settings_mode` and `writer.shadow_log`.

### Steadier checks (NP1's issues 4 and 6)

- `tools/proxy_gate.py`: the decode check is relative. The median request within 2 % of the engine's rate, each request within 5 % on its best of 3 tries; the token counts, the status and the TTFT order hold on every try. The proxy times frames as they arrive, so over a LAN one late last frame moved a 96-token request by a few percent (1 and 4 of 20 failed a per-request 2 % from the Mac; 20 of 20 passed over loopback). The report says whether the engine was on loopback. `tests/test_proxy_gate.py` (new, 3): a fake engine whose last frame arrives late fails the old gate and passes the new one on its retry; a request late on every try still fails.
- `e2e/performance.spec.ts`: the two dot specs pick an engine-measured dot and select it with the keyboard. Every seventh mock row is relayed through the proxy and draws no timing bar, and which dot came first depended on the rows earlier specs had added, so the spec failed alone and passed in a run. The scatter's dots carry `data-measured`.

### The proxy's writer against real engines

- `tools/proxy_writer_live.py` (new): the standalone proxy in front of a real vLLM, SGLang or cloud API with the writer on: a session with a fact written at its end, shadow (nothing stored, the log written), busy (a client request in flight: the look starts nothing), yield (a client request while the writer streams). On a cloud API the exact cost of every request from the ledger.
- `tools/memory_replay.py` (new): a real session's transcript replayed into an engine with memory on, so the writer writes from a real session (OPS-55).
- Measured on the box on 2026-10-05 (Qwen3.5-0.8B, vLLM v0.30.0 and SGLang v0.5.21 with the `qwen3_coder` tool parser, n = 1 each): `busy` held on both (no writer request while a client request is in flight); on SGLang a client request 1.1 s into the writer's stream closed it and the session stayed due. Without a prefill the 0.8B model wrote a block the schema refused (vLLM) or 400 tokens of text (SGLang); with the prefill `Facts worth keeping (blocks, or NONE):` it wrote 2 notes on vLLM (2,720 of 3,153 prompt tokens from vLLM's prefix cache) and 1 on SGLang. Without a tool parser vLLM refuses a request with tools (400), and SGLang does not hold the model to `tool_choice: "none"` (the writer's invented calls were cut to NONE). DeepSeek (`deepseek-flash`, writer on, one run): 1 note; the whole test spent 1,273 micro-USD at the list price (7 requests), the writer's request 287.

## 0.3.35-test, 2026-10-05

0.3.34-test (5b6fb5d) with the proxy's background memory writer and the writer's own NONE. The request and the stream are the release's (identity gate against 5b6fb5d); what changes is the writer's hidden turn on the engine, and a request the proxy may ask of a backend in its idle time.

### The background writer behind the proxy (MEM2's open item)

- For a backend behind the proxy (vLLM, SGLang, any OpenAI-compatible server, a cloud API) the session-end and after-compaction writer is one more request to the backend the session used (`proxy/memwriter.py`): the messages of the session's last request as they were sent (so the backend's prefix cache matches), its answer, and the writer's user turn; thinking off; the session's tools kept with `tool_choice: "none"`. Its answer goes through the engine writer's parser, store and journal; the run says `via: proxy`, `backend`, `model`, `cost_micros`, and the request is a ledger row of the client `harness:writer` (counted under `memory` on the Backends screen).
- In the backend's idle time: one writer request at a time, only while the backend has no client request in flight; on a local backend a client request that arrives closes the writer's stream (the session stays due). A compaction request in the session keeps the turn before it as the record.
- Per backend (`harness` document, `TANDEM_BACKEND_<ID>_WRITER`, `_WRITER_USD_DAY`, `_WRITER_RUNS_DAY`, `_WRITER_PROMPT_TOKENS`): `writer` auto (on; off on a paid cloud model), off, shadow, on; a spend cap a day on a paid model (0.25 USD, checked against an estimate before each run), a run cap a day (48), and the prompt's size (32,000 estimated tokens, the oldest messages dropped first). The effective mode is the lower of the backend's and `settings.memory.notes.writer.mode`; a paid model without a price is refused. The day's figures come back from the ledger after a restart; the Backends API shows the mode per model and the day's runs and spend.

### The writer's own NONE (L2's open item)

- `settings.memory.notes.writer.ban_tool_call` (on): the `<tool_call>` token gets a logit bias of -100 in the writer's turn, so after a compaction Qwen can no longer answer with a `bash` call; the cut of 0.3.34 stays as the backstop. Behind the proxy the same switch sends `tool_choice: "none"`.
- `prefill` (empty): text the writer's answer starts with (the engine: tokens after the generation prompt; the proxy: an assistant start where the backend can continue one).
- Not yet measured on the real engine: `tools/memory_measure.py --ban-tool-call on|off --prefill ... --stop-after compaction` is the night pass's n = 1 check.

### Shadow writes a log

- A writer run in shadow appends the blocks it would have written, after the secret-pattern refusal, to `<user>/shadow/writer-<yyyy-mm-dd>.md` (`0600`), which nothing reads back. The journal keeps counts only, as before.

### Tests

- `tests/test_proxy_memwriter.py` (new, 9): the switches and the env variables, the trim and the request body (tool_choice none, thinking off, the prefill where the backend continues), an idle vLLM session written with the prefix it sent, shadow's log, a paid cloud model (auto off, no price, the spend cap, the run cap, the spend read back from the ledger), NONE and a cut `bash` call, the compaction record, a client request that stops the writer, the Backends API.
- `tests/test_memory_writer.py`: the `<tool_call>` ban (the token the greedy turn chose first without it is never chosen with it), the prefill.
- `tests/fake_backend.py`: the writer's request (`FAKE_WRITER_NONE`, `_BASH`, `_SLOW`).

Its tokens are recorded as hidden spans, so the end anchor's replay keeps the next turn's prefix (a block whose edge shares a token with text is not, and that turn prefills from there).

Dashboard rebuilt. Tests: tests/test_session_tasks.py (the URL from the environment), tests/test_tandem_eval.py (the rewrite), tests/test_defaults.py reads the holder's name from NOTICE.

The shadow keeps the 0.8B; nothing changes in serve.env.

### The plugins inside vLLM and SGLang and the launcher (proxy P6, branch proxy-p6)

On branch proxy-p4 (the harness in front of any backend, on proxy-p23; not released). Usage ledger schema version 4 (four columns added in place at start). Dashboard contract 1.3, additive. New `tandem-dash launch`. Nothing changes for the engine's own model, and a server with `--backends` off loads none of it.

- Two packages in `plugins/` (plugins/README.md): `tandemllm-vllm-plugin`, a stat logger vLLM loads from the `vllm.stat_logger_plugins` entry point, plus an optional `GET /tandem/stats` route (`vllm.endpoint_plugins`); and `tandemllm-sglang-plugin`, a general plugin SGLang loads from `sglang.srt.plugins` in each of its processes, with two hooks (`TokenizerManager.collect_metrics`, `SchedulerMetricsCollector.log_stats`). Per request: queue, prefill and decode time, cached tokens, preemptions (SGLang: retractions), the engine's finish reason, and on SGLang the speculation verify passes and accepted drafts. Once a second: the scheduler's state. They keep 10,000 requests and 300 samples in memory, post once a second to the proxy with a shared token, and never stop the engine (an import failure, a renamed field or a failing hook is a log line and a null). No dependencies; checked against vLLM v0.30.0 and SGLang v0.5.21.
- SGLang v0.5.21 has an entry point group after all (`sglang.srt.plugins`, with a hook registry), so the SGLang plugin needs no launcher and no `ServerArgs.stat_loggers`; the tokenizer collector's per-request call carries no request id in v0.5.21, while `collect_metrics` has the request's state.
- The proxy: `POST /v1/collect/<backend>` (`proxy/collect_api.py`) takes the batches. The relay tags each request to a `vllm` backend with `X-Request-Id: px-<hex>` (vLLM reports `chatcmpl-px-<hex>`, the row's own id) and to an `sglang` backend with the body's `rid`; a client's own id is kept. The row then gets the engine's `queue_ms`, `prompt_ms`, `decode_ms`, `decode_tps`, `prefill_tps` and `cached_tokens`, and the new columns `preemptions`, `engine_finish`, `corrupted` and `l2_join`. An item that comes after its row amends it in place (`Ledger.amend`); one that comes first waits; either waits 10 minutes, then it is dropped and counted. A request the proxy cannot tag is matched by time and token counts when exactly one row fits (`approximate`, one log line). With nothing pushed for 25 s the proxy reads vLLM's `/tandem/stats` instead.
- The collect token: `TANDEM_COLLECT_TOKEN`, else a random one stored in the config database at the first need.
- `tandem-dash launch vllm|sglang --model M --port P [-- engine args]` (`proxy/launch.py`): registers the backend, hands the engine the collect URL and token, adds the flags the dashboard reads, checks that the plugin is installed in the engine's Python, then becomes the engine (the pid it records is the engine's). Without the plugin it starts the engine at L1 and says how to install it.
- Contract 1.3: `engine.plugin` and `engine.layer: L2` on a backend's status row, `l2` on a `requests` row, `plugin_age_s` filled. On `/metrics`: `qse_backend_plugin_age_seconds`, `qse_backend_plugin_joins{backend,join}`.
- The dashboard: "L2 plugin" or "L1 only" on each vLLM and SGLang card, with the plugin and engine versions, and a line with the joined rows, preemptions, KV evictions and vLLM's acceptance per draft position; a relayed request row whose split came from the engine says so.
- Tests: tests/test_proxy_plugins.py 12 (both plugins on stand-ins built from the tagged sources' classes and call shapes: the items, the per-second fold, failures that stay inside, the import failure vLLM's loader catches, the pull route and its token, the poster's batches, heartbeat and back-off, the two packages' shared file and license), tests/test_proxy_collect.py 12 (the route and its token, both join orders, the client's own id, SGLang's rid, the approximate join and its refusal, the waits, the ledger amend, the plugin block against the contract, L1 only after 60 s, the pull, `launch` with a stand-in engine); dashboard: vitest 373, e2e engines.spec.ts (chromium, webkit at 390 px). A smoke on the Mac: the plugin's poster to a standalone proxy in front of a fake vLLM, the row joined exactly.
- Not verified against running engines yet. The night pass (`tools/proxy_e2e.sh --box --engines`, now with `tools/proxy_engines_check.sh --plugins`) installs both wheels into the release images, checks the joins and the plugin's sums against each engine's `/metrics` within 1 %, and measures the plugin's cost on vLLM with `tools/proxy_plugin_ab.py`: decode tok/s without, with and without the plugin, 20 requests each, gate 1 %.

## 0.3.29-test, 2026-10-04

d2d91f3 (0.3.28-test, with the voice fix caed7b8) and the proxy, P1 (branch proxy-p1): the dashboard in front of other engines and cloud APIs. New server flag `--backends PATH|off` (off); `ops/start.sh` passes serve.env's `QSE_BACKENDS` (empty: off). Usage ledger schema version 3 (columns added in place at start). Dashboard contract 1.3, additive. With `--backends` off, as on :8000 after this deploy, the engine loads none of it and serves exactly as before; Qwen's text does not change (identity gate).

- The proxy (`proxy/`, docs/proxy.md). Requests are routed by model id to the backend that serves it: another TandemLLM, vLLM, SGLang, any OpenAI-compatible server, OpenAI (chat, completions, embeddings, and the Responses API relayed as it is) or DeepSeek. The answer's bytes go to the client unchanged; the proxy asks a stream for its usage frame when the client did not and drops that frame. `/v1/models` lists each backend's real model ids with `owned_by` its backend; two backends with one id are listed as `<backend>/<model>`. Routing rules (ordered globs), fallbacks before the first byte (connect error, 429, 502, 503; at most 2 tries again; `Retry-After` honoured up to 30 s), `max_inflight` per backend (64, then 503), timeouts per backend, a client that leaves closes the upstream connection.
- Two entry points: the engine's own server with `--backends` (a relayed request runs on its handler's thread and never touches the engine's lock or queue; `TandemLLM` stays the engine's), and `python -m proxy` with no torch and no GPU (Python 3.11+, the standard library and `cryptography`).
- The config database (`~/.tandemllm/config.sqlite3`): backends, keys as AES-256-GCM ciphertext (the master key from `TANDEM_SECRETS_KEY`, the OS keychain or a 0600 key file), models with public ids, prices and per-model switches, routing rules, users, an audit table. `TANDEM_*` variables overlay it and win field by field; a field a variable sets is locked in the GUI and a save that changes it answers 422 naming the variable; an env key is never written. One schema (`proxy/config.schema.json`) for both ways in.
- Measured, not estimated: tokens from the backend's `usage` (null without it), cached and reasoning tokens from each provider's fields, TTFT at the proxy, decode tok/s by the engine's formula over the token frames (null without `usage`: a frame is not a token), cost at the model's price when the row is written, the proxy's own time. A relayed row has null queue, prefill, blocks, draft counts and cache source. DeepSeek's off-peak half price applies by the request's UTC hour. `proxy/prices.seed.json`: OpenAI's and DeepSeek's list prices as read on 2026-10-04, offered on a model's row, applied only by a click.
- Users and keys: with one user, the OpenAI routes need a key from any other machine (the engine's own model included); trusted-local requests pass, so the conductor's own questions to Qwen keep working. The key's label is the ledger's `user`.
- The dashboard: a Backends tab (cards with health, models, in flight, latency, cost today; add after a test connection, edit, delete; the write-only key with its last 4 characters; env locks; models with prices and switches; routing rules; users with each key shown once) and a Setup screen while no backend exists. Usage filters by backend (`engine` for the engine's own rows) and by user and shows the cost of priced models; Dev and Performance tag relayed rows and say "measured at the proxy" and "not reported by this backend". At 390 px the bottom bar shows short labels (Perf, Play, Cond) so seven tabs fit.
- The proxy's own families on /metrics (`qse_proxy_requests_total{backend,kind,finish_reason}`, `qse_proxy_tokens_total`, `qse_proxy_cost_micros_total`, `qse_upstream_retries_total`, `qse_proxy_overhead_ms`, `qse_proxy_ttft_seconds`, `qse_backend_up`, `qse_backend_inflight`). The engine's families keep their labels and never count a relayed request.
- Measured on the Mac against the fake backend (`tools/proxy_bench.py`, 200 requests): the proxy adds 0.33 ms to the client's TTFT at the median, its own `proxy_ms` 0.17 ms p50 and 0.22 ms p90; 64 streams at once reached the backend all at once and ended in 5.18 s against 5.22 s for one alone. Against the live engine on :8000 from the Mac over the LAN (`tools/proxy_gate.py`, 20 raw requests, greedy, thinking off): token counts equal, decode within 0.8 % of the engine's own `predicted_per_second`, `proxy_ms` 0.37 ms p50, TTFT 11 ms above the engine's at the median.
- Live on :8000 since 19:55 on 2026-10-04 (97a0ef3, `--backends` off: the service serves as 0.3.28 did), through the drain; down 19:46 to 19:55. Gate identity PASS against c58862d; row with `--no-learn-cost` 50.09 tok/s (c58862d 50.08 at 19:21 in the 0.3.28 hold, the same flags); CPU suite 184/184; the ledger migrated to schema 3 with all 11,404 rows; smoke raw 27/27, on 27/27; 0 tracebacks. caed7b8 (the voice's language and gerund fixes) went live with it. Rollback: `bash ~/rollback-0.3.29.sh` on the box (to c58862d; the ledger keeps its added columns). The proxy on :8000: set `QSE_BACKENDS=${HOME}/.tandemllm/config.sqlite3` in ops/serve.env and restart.
- Not verified with a real key: OpenAI and DeepSeek, which are tested on frames written from their documented shapes (tests/fixtures/proxy/frames.json), not on paid calls.
- Tests: tests/test_proxy_config.py 7, test_proxy_adapters.py 7, test_proxy_relay.py 10 (the fake backend, `tests/fake_backend.py`), test_proxy_engine.py 2 (the engine with `--backends`, the fake engine); dashboard: vitest tests/backends.test.ts 7, Playwright e2e/backends.spec.ts on chromium desktop and webkit at 390 px. `tools/proxy_e2e.sh` runs them all together with the bench and the gate.

## 0.3.27-test, 2026-10-04

aca8126 (0.3.26-test) with branch tandem-d8 and 854aae9. New server flags `--side-lane on|decode|off` (on), `--side-lane-prompt-max` (2,048), `--side-lane-new-max` (64); a `lane` column in the usage ledger (added in place at start). Every request the side lane does not serve gets the same text as on 0.3.26; the long request a guest interrupts gets the same text as without it (measured below).

- The side lane (`server/preempt.py`, docs/server.md). On 2026-10-04 between 16:43 and 16:48 one opencode turn thought for minutes, and everything short waited behind it in the single queue. The `anon` requests the ledger shows as `abandoned` after 9.0 s were the router's own package and library questions to Qwen (`server/conductor/classify.py`, raw, 24 tokens under a choice grammar, an 8 s timeout) for a second opencode session's first turn; that session's turns got a 429 after 256 s. Now a short request -- a raw one or a client's side request (a title), thinking off, at most 2,048 prompt and 64 output tokens -- that finds the engine busy is served by the running generation at its next safe point, between two decode blocks or two prefill chunks. The guest is prefilled from position 0 and decoded one token a forward without the drafter, so its answer is plain greedy decoding of its prompt.
- The generation gets the engine back byte for byte (`engine/cache.py` `Borrow`): the KV rows the guest can reach, the recurrent state, the convolution tails, a walked chain state and the pending commit (copied unsettled, so the next verify folds the same record), and the references the next block reads; the drafter is never touched. A job waits for a later safe point when it would push the engine past its memory peak; a disk-tier write that has not copied the guest's rows yet stops where it is; a job nobody takes runs under the lock on its own thread. A client's side request too long for the lane (opencode's summary) is never refused for its wait.
- What it costs and what it gives, on the real engine (`tools/lane_check.py`, the candidate with every cache off and `--no-learn-cost`, a 5,000-token prompt and 768 output tokens with thinking, greedy): with 10 short requests fired into it (opencode's title shape and the router's question shape), the long request's reasoning and answer were byte-identical to two runs alone. 9 of them were served in the lane, 1.2 s at the median and 5.1 s at most (two arrived during a prefill that ran as one chunk on that server, so they waited for its first decode block); the one over the lane's output cap waited 23.7 s in the queue, the rest of the long request. The long request took 7.4 s longer (32.9 s against 25.5 s) for 4.7 s the guests held the engine. Live on :8000 after the deploy, during a 2,094-token opencode-shaped turn: two title requests in 2.6 s (one served between two prefill chunks) and 1.6 s; a second session's first turn had its router questions answered by Qwen in 0.64 to 0.81 s each (`test-lib` at 0.998) where they had timed out at 8 s, and its turn itself waited in the queue as before. Not measured on the GPU: a guest between two prefill chunks against an uninterrupted prefill (the CPU test covers it bit for bit).

The guard reads the open call's arguments every 64 tokens and stops a held call when its last 1,024 tokens are one unit of at most 4,096 characters repeated 6 or more times, or when it passed 32,768 tokens and 3 times the request's longest message with its last 16 KB compressing 16 times or more. The client gets one sentence and `finish_reason: "stop"`, no call; the session's next request with tools carries a hidden note (write it without the repetition, generate repeated rows with code, write a large file in parts). On the incident's text it fires 2,176 tokens into the call, 1,055 after the loop began.

After a burst with more than 2 GiB free in the pool the shadow parks its sessions on the disk and unloads the model, which drops the pool; the gate has a last level, `roles`, that does the same; before a refusal the gate collects and empties once more; a prompt whose workspace fits in the engine allocator's own free reserve is admitted (`stale_admit`); a refusal is an error line in the Dev tab. The abandoned prefill was not the cause: the shadow read ten bursts after it and the refusals began right after them.

## 0.3.25-test, 2026-10-04

ce78689 (0.3.24-test) with branch tandem-sr1: the shadow reader. New serve.env keys `QWEN38_SHADOW_MODEL`, `QWEN38_SHADOW_DIR`, `QWEN38_SHADOW_GB`, `QWEN38_SHADOW_GRID`, `QWEN38_SHADOW_DISK`, `QWEN38_SHADOW_DISK_GB` (empty model: off, nothing imported); a profile's `shadow` block (absent: off). The deploy sets `QWEN38_SHADOW_MODEL=qwen3.5-0.8b` and `QWEN38_SHADOW_DISK=auto` and stores the coding profile with `shadow: {mode: on, router: shadow, router_min_tokens: 8192, narrator: off}`. Qwen's answers do not change.

- The shadow reader (`engine/shadow.py`, `server/conductor/shadow.py`, docs/shadow-reader.md). Qwen3.5-0.8B keeps its own KV and Gated-DeltaNet state of each coding session, keyed by the router's session key, and reads each turn's new tokens: the served prompt and Qwen's output, as Qwen's own token ids (the Qwen3.5 small models share Qwen3.8's vocabulary and merges). It replaces the two closed-form bridges that failed earlier today (B2's soft rows at chance, B3's KV/GDN map at R² 0.5).
- Exact by construction: the state advances in whole 512-row chunks at fixed positions, so it equals a fresh prefill of the same ids on the same grid bit for bit (measured on the GPU on two real conversations of 41,802 and 58,278 tokens: every K and V row, the recurrent and the convolution state). Against a fresh prefill on a 2,048-row grid: 8 of 8 question probes give the same top token, KL at most 4.1e-5. A prompt that differs from what was read goes back to the newest checkpoint at or below the difference (one at each turn's prompt end).
- When it reads: in the idle window (every 0.2 s, behind every waiter and the summary written ahead, under the box lock taken without waiting, at most 2 s, stopping before the next chunk when a request waits: one chunk is 36 to 50 ms), and inside a turn in 2 % of the time since Qwen's first token, between two rounds. The idle window alone is not enough for opencode: the ledger's 41 sessions (1,624 turns) have a median gap of 0.31 s between requests; replayed with the measured rate the shadow is fresh at 41 % of turn starts idle-only and at 84 % with the in-turn share.
- What it costs Qwen (`tools/shadow_ab.py`, a hold, 6 runs an arm, a 16,350-token prompt): decode 36.02 tok/s off, 35.28 on (-2.05 %, gate 3 %); TTFT unchanged (17.46 / 17.40 s). The first build counted the share from the turn's start and lost 5.3 %; fixed before this release.
- Cost and memory (`tools/shadow_measure.py`, 0.8B): 71 to 97 ms per 1,000 tokens read at depths 0 to 41k (2B: 99 to 135 ms); 12 KiB of KV a token plus 19.5 MB of recurrent state: a 58k session is 0.88 GiB. Resident states are capped at 4 GiB; past it the least recently used session goes to `~/.qwen38-spark-engine/cache/shadow` (20 GB, 48 h) and comes back exact; a planned stop writes them all.
- `ask(session, question, choices)` and `POST /v1/conductor/shadow/ask`: a typed decision of the small model over the whole session, one forward (68 ms for the router's 9-class question at the end of a 41k session). The router's class question is asked of the shadow in shadow mode on turns of at least 8,192 tokens and journaled beside the router's class in `<conductor root>/shadow.jsonl` (agreement, how far behind the shadow was when the turn began); nothing of the turn changes. `GET /v1/conductor/shadow/status`.
- The narrator can read its thought summaries from the shadow (`shadow.narrator: on`), whole session instead of the thought's last 1,500 ids; shipped off (its fork decodes eagerly, 12 to 17 ms a token on the 0.8B).
- Live on :8000 since 16:05 on 2026-10-04 (5cd7e95). A 5-turn test session of opencode's shape (`tools/shadow_live.py`, bearer sr1-test, a 12k-token system text, 12,676 to 21,491-token prompts): the shadow followed every turn (3 rollbacks to a prompt-end checkpoint when an answer came back re-rendered, 1,176 ids read again; 24,064 rows in 47 chunks, 1.65 s in all), 83 ids behind at the end, 0.38 GB. The router's question was asked on all 5 turns (77 to 124 ms each) and agreed with the router 0 of 5 times: the 0.8B picked `debug` 4 times and `design_ui` once, at 0.15 to 0.50, where the router said `chat` or `code_edit` at 0.72 to 0.997. ## 0.3.24-test, 2026-10-04

f0e4931 (0.3.23-test) with branch tandem-d6, live on :8000 since 15:17 on 2026-10-04 (ce78689): the end anchor survives an eviction after a restart, a breakdown of every spill save, the narrator's A/B made repeatable, narrator v2 on for opencode, the Laya drive kit closes its browsers, and the summary written ahead gives the box back. One new server flag (`--learn-cost`, on by default, as before). The changed engine files are engine/cache.py and engine/spill.py, which the disk tier's and the spill's fingerprints leave out, so the deploy kept both (26 tier entries, 6 conversations). After the deploy: serve.env `QWEN38_NARRATOR_MODEL=qwen3.5-0.8b` (was minicpm5-2b) and coding v16 (`ui.narrator: thoughts`).

- The end anchor through an eviction. On 0.3.23 (13:34) the conversation read back at the start had its end anchor, and the next eviction wrote it to the NVMe without it (`end=False`, 0 bytes written); its next turn would have re-read the 759 tokens above its last grid anchor. The request that evicted it was served from the disk tier, and `prefill` dropped the end before `begin`, whose eviction then saved the rows without it and deleted the old `end.anc`. The drop now comes after `begin`. A save that finds every block and the tokens unchanged also keeps the end anchor already on the disk when the engine no longer holds one. tests/test_session_spill.py reproduces the live case (fails on 0.3.23, passes now) and the carried end. Live after a restart (`tools/spill_live.py --phase endcheck`): another session's 11,130-token request served from the disk tier (10,240 reused) evicted the 41,803-token conversation with its end anchor (`end=True`, 0.24 GB written in 187 ms), and the conversation's next turn reused 41,803 of 41,822 tokens.
- The slow eviction (7.0 GB in 4.5 s right after the disk tier wrote 17.6 GB) is the NVMe's write cache. `tools/spill_io_probe.py` measures it: 4-5.6 GB/s for the first 16 to 24 GB, then 0.3 to 1.3 GB/s, back to 5.2 GB/s after 300 s of rest. The real save of a 58,278-token conversation from GPU buffers took 1.46 s on a rested drive and 4.9 s after 17.5 GB of tier-shaped files. Pacing the tier's files did not help (8.2 s), so the tier is unchanged. At the slowest rate measured (0.36 GB/s) the save takes about 20 s, about a third of re-reading those tokens (about 57 s). Every save now logs its parts in ms (lock, staging, sums, copy, waits for the writer, anchors, fsync, manifest) and `writer_ms`.
- Repeatable speed runs: `--no-learn-cost` keeps the length router's served price table. With learning on, the same 2,000 greedy tokens took 366, 468 and 504 blocks in 0.3.23's narrator A/B at 93.5 to 94.1 ms a block, because the router learns verify and draft times across requests and then chooses differently; that was the 37 % spread of the off runs. The narrator measure runs its server with the flag, sets a progress mark every 512 thinking tokens on both sides (the 0.3.23 runs never closed their thought, so the narrator did nothing until the turn's end), records blocks, ms a block and the text of each run, and reads its 3 % gate only when the off runs agree within 3 %.
- Narrator v2 on for opencode (coding v16, Qwen3.5-0.8B). The A/B with the model loaded, the router's costs held and a progress mark every 512 thinking tokens (three summaries in a 2,000-token run, more than the default 4,096-token mark gives): on the six runs that wrote the same text in 514 blocks, off 41.69 tok/s (spread 0.19 %), on 40.64 tok/s (spread 0.17 %), -2.5 %, inside the 3 % gate; 95.7 against 93.3 ms a block. Each turn ends about 485 ms later (the summary's end allowance). Live: `Thought 7s: would use a fixed-timestep accumulator loop ...` on an opencode-shaped request at 58 tok/s. The first ask after a start can be refused while the Laya models load (`refused_load_in_progress`); the slot asks again after 60 s and loads in 13 s (1.74 GiB). Undo: `~/c324-narr-off.sh` on the box.
- The Laya drive kit (`server/laya_kit/laya_drive.py`) closes what it starts. 42 Chrome processes of four drives started a day earlier ran on the box with their driver gone; they were killed. Chrome and the game now run in their own process group, ended whole; a page that never comes up closes its Chrome; SIGTERM and SIGHUP run the cleanup; on Linux Chrome gets the parent-death signal, so a driver killed by SIGKILL takes it along. A kit copied into a project's `.tandem/` keeps the old code until it is copied again.
- The summary written ahead gives the box back: it does not start while another program is on the GPU, and stops when a process waits in `flock` for the box lock it holds (/proc/locks, every 0.5 s) or another program comes to the GPU (nvidia-smi, every 5 s). A hold then waits about half a second instead of up to 45 s. `prepared.stats.yielded` counts it.

- Not built (decided): a keep-alive for long non-streamed requests, the 0.3.21-era open item. In 14 days of the ledger no non-streamed request ran over 158 s, 3 over 60 s; opencode and Hermes stream.

## 0.3.23-test, 2026-10-04

83674ea (0.3.22-test) with branch tandem-d5: a client's compaction served from the conversation the engine already holds, a summary written ahead, a session token on the addresses the notes give the model, the session spill's own I/O path, and the skill canon for every location. New flags `--compaction`, `--compaction-prepare`, `--compaction-idle-s`, `--compaction-min-tokens` (serve.env `QSE_COMPACTION*`, absent = continue, prepare on, 30 s, 32,768 tokens). No conductor document changes.

- Compaction as a continuation (`server/compaction.py`, docs/caches.md "Compaction as a continuation"). On 2026-10-03 a manual /compact of a 111,636-token opencode conversation read 63,614 tokens cold and took 189.8 s, and an automatic one at 198,030 tokens read 129,643 tokens and took 270 s, both while the conversation sat resident. opencode sends its compaction agent's prompt and ONE user message holding the history as text, which shares no token with what the engine read. Now the request is served as the session's own conversation (up to the end anchor of its last generation, in RAM or on the NVMe) plus one user turn with the client's system text and instructions: the prefill reads that turn alone. A guard checks the first and last user lines of the client's history against the record. The end anchor after images is kept with its rotary offset, for this continuation alone.
- A summary written ahead. When the engine has been idle 30 s, the resident conversation of an opencode session of at least 32,768 tokens gets its summary written in scratch rows, under the box lock taken without waiting; a waiting request or a drain stops it at the next chunk or block and the conversation's rows, anchors and end anchor stay as they were. A compaction of that session at that end anchor with the same instructions is answered from it without the engine.
- Measured live (2026-10-04, a captured rrr6 request from a user report, 104,313-token turn with 17 images, 57,008-token compaction request): served as sent (cold) 115.5 s (80.8 s of prefill); as a continuation 40.7 s on f0e4931 (prefill 1.04 s, 56,551 of 57,008 reported cached; the rest is writing 1,406 summary tokens); from the summary written ahead 0.07 s (written 75 s after the turn, in 43.9 s). Every summary kept opencode's eight template sections. On 0.3.20 the same compaction had taken 189.8 s.
- Session addresses (`server/session_tokens.py`, docs/server.md "Session addresses"): `{tandem_url}` in a session's notes is the request's address plus `/s/<token>` (12 random characters, kept 48 h, 0600), so a library or Laya call from the model's scripts names its session in the journal row and the session's counts; an unknown token is served, attributed to nobody; other routes under `/s/` are a 404. A client without a session id keeps its session through a compaction the engine wrote (a new head carrying that summary).
- The session spill's own I/O path: its own lock and staging buffers, the disk tier's writer waits between files while a save runs, a block's copy overlaps the previous block's write, one device sync for a block's sums, unchanged anchors not written again. Live, the same case as 0.3.22's (a 41,587-token conversation evicted by another session's 9,162-token request): 5.20 GB written in 1.03 s (0.3.22: 7.23 s), read back in 0.94 s, the next turn's TTFT 2.0 s. A 58,278-token conversation evicted right after the tier had written 17.6 GB took 4.5 s (7.0 GB); why it was slower is not measured.
- The skill canon for every location (`server/skillcanon.py`). Four first requests of fresh sessions captured from two opencode 1.18.34 processes still parted at character 24,970: two skills had their second copy under `~/.claude/skills/.trash/`, which 0.3.22 did not touch. Every entry with a path is canonical by name now. Live: the 2nd to 4th request reused 37,888 of 38,172 tokens (the first read all 38,172 in 54.3 s).
- The disk tier's fingerprint leaves out the files that keep state (engine/cache.py, disk_cache.py, spill.py, capture_lock.py), as the spill's does: 0.3.22's deploy swept 49 GB of heads for a change in cache.py alone. This deploy sweeps once more.
- Narrator v2 stays off. The A/B now runs from a tree without the hold's pause file, so the model really loaded (1.89 GiB, 12.5 s); 0.3.22's -14.6 % was measured with the model refused (`refused_hold`, the hold's own `.watchdog.off` in the served tree) and so was not the narrator's cost. This time, 2,000 tokens a run: off 58.1, 45.6 and 42.2 tok/s, on 45.6, 45.6 and 45.7, with about 480 ms at the end of each turn on (the end allowance), and no thought summary in the on runs (one 2,000-token thought, still open at the cap). The off runs alone spread 37 %, so this A/B cannot show a 3 % difference either way. Summaries alone: 11 of 12 written, p50 395 ms, p90 499 ms; the graph and transformers' greedy agree.
- Fix found live on the first build (1aa4d99): a continuation after images carried the images' key ids into the suffix store, whose packing raised after the summary, and the stream lost its usage chunk. Fixed in f0e4931.

## 0.3.22-test, 2026-10-04

40a043d (0.3.21-test) with the paused work of branch tandem-d3 and the narrator of branch tandem-n2 merged (branch tandem-d4), and four fixes from a day of user reports on the box. New serve.env key `SESSION_SPILL` (absent = on); ops/start.sh passes `--conductor-defaults shipped` to the :8000 service.

- Live conversations on the NVMe (`engine/spill.py`, docs/caches.md "Live conversations on the NVMe"). The 15:35 deploy cost the next turn of a 130,000-token opencode conversation a 158 s re-read: the disk tier keeps only the cold-grid head (25,600 tokens), and everything past the first answer is a session's rows. A planned stop (SIGTERM's drain, after the work in flight) now writes the resident conversation and the parked one, and the next start reads the resident one back before its first request: its rows of every buffer, the end anchor and the newest 4 anchors, its tokens, `taint` and session, the bytes that were in the engine. The next turn resumes at the end anchor.
- A long conversation is no longer evicted by another client's request. At 15:37 a 10,216-token request of another client (over the guest size, 8,192) replaced the resident prompt, the RAM park holds 35,000 rows above the shared head, and the conversation's next turn re-read everything above 32,768: 165 s. Such a request now writes a resident conversation of at least 16,384 tokens to the NVMe first when the park cannot hold it, and a session snapshot that clears the resident prefix does too; the conversation's next turn reads it back (`cache_source: spill`). The RAM cap and the 262,144-token window are unchanged.
- The spill writes and reads by content: blocks of 1,024 rows with two 64-bit sums per buffer computed on the device; a block whose tokens and sums equal the file is not written again, a block in place is not read, every block read is summed again before the engine resumes from it. Its own budget (40 GB), the tier's 50 GB floor, 48 h. Its fingerprint leaves out the files that keep state (engine/cache.py, disk_cache.py, spill.py, capture_lock.py). Flags `--session-spill`, `--session-spill-gb`, `--session-spill-min-tokens`.
- A client's effort word is a ceiling (a design decision, 2026-10-03 12:30): where the router decides the effort, the turn never gets a cap above the word's (medium 8,192); a number still wins outright, the answer reserve stays. Per profile `thinking.client_word`: `ceiling` (the default) or `ignore`; coding and overnight ignore it, because opencode sends `medium` on every turn. The deploy stores the live coding and overnight profiles with `ignore`.
- One location per skill in opencode's skills list (`server/skillcanon.py`). D3 found that every new opencode session re-read 5 to 6 thousand tokens of its head: 11 of the 32 entries of `<available_skills>` sit in two folders the Claude app syncs, and opencode keeps whichever copy its scan meets last, so their location flips between sessions. An opencode request (not raw) now gets each synced entry as the copy first seen for its name; the choice is kept in the conductor's directory.
- From branch tandem-d3 (2026-10-03): the end anchor for a copy whose whitespace is not the rows' (`server/endalign.py`, `END_ALIGN`): within a session some tool turns re-read 2 to 3 thousand tokens because opencode's copy of a tool call's parameter or of the `</think>` line differs from what the engine wrote in whitespace alone; such a copy now resumes at the end anchor. The Hermes agent is a client kind of its own (`hermes`, by its tools, its title call or its identity) and gets the `hermes` profile. The cache source of each request on the Live panel and the Performance screen. The live documents of 2026-10-03 shipped for a new box (schema.py `SHIPPED_*`, the texts under `packages/`), stored as version 1 at the first start by `server/conductor/shipped.py` for each document a box has no version of (on the reference box: the `hermes` and `general` profiles); the built-in version 0 stays the minimal one.
- From N2: the narrator sums up each thought (`ui.narrator: thoughts`, Qwen3.5-0.8B). Shipped off. On the GPU (2026-10-04) it wrote 11 summaries of 12 real thoughts, 442 ms at the median and 712 ms at p90 (a decode step 9.5 ms, the captured graph and transformers' greedy give the same ids); the decode gate did not pass: the candidate server's planner refused to load the model inside the hold (`refused_hold`), and the runs with the narrator profile were 14.6 % slower than without it all the same. Not switched on until a clean A/B with the model loaded passes the 3 % gate.
- Measured on the live box (2026-10-04): a 41,587-token conversation evicted by another session's 9,162-token request was written in 7.2 s (5.2 GB; the disk tier was writing the same conversation's head at the same time) and read back for its next turn in 1.3 s, TTFT 2.5 s where its cold first turn took 56.9 s. A restart through the drain wrote 0.85 GB (40 of 41 blocks unchanged) in 1.2 s, the start read 5.2 GB back in 1.1 s, and the next turn resumed at the end anchor: 41,719 tokens reused, TTFT 635 ms. tools/session_spill_check.py on the served engine: every row, the end anchor and the restored anchors equal bit for bit in the writing process and in a fresh one, the next turn's tokens equal. Row pair: 40a043d 44.48, 0.3.22 50.10 tok/s (one run each).
- Tests (box CPU): tests/test_session_spill.py 9, test_skillcanon 2, test_defaults 4, test_client_kinds 4, test_client_budgets (the ceiling), test_end_align, test_thoughts; the CPU suite; dashboard tsc clean, vitest 344 passed, dist 153.8 KB gzip of 300.
