## 0.3.21-test, 2026-10-03

A hotfix on 50cc1f5 (0.3.20-test, branch tandem-img1): a long conversation is no longer refused for the images it has gathered, and after a compaction the session's class packages come back. No serve.env key, no ops/ file, no engine file and no conductor document changes; a request whose images fit the caps and that is not a compaction or the first user message after one is served byte for byte as by 0.3.20-test.

- The bug (a user's opencode session in ~/rrr6, 2026-10-03): the `design-review` package (packages v6) has the model screenshot every section and read each png, and opencode sends every earlier image again on every turn. The 17th (several were re-reads of one file) took the request over `--max-images` (16): HTTP 400 `17 images; the limit is 16 a request` on `messages[210].content[1].image_url`, not retryable, and every later request carried 17 or more, so the session could never continue.
- `server/images.py`: when a request's images are over `--max-images` or `--max-image-rows` and the excess is in earlier messages, the oldest images are left out instead of a 400. A left-out image is never fetched or decoded; `build_prompt` renders it as the text `[an earlier image was left out: TandemLLM keeps the newest 16 images of a conversation]` (`images.LEFT_OUT`, one text for every left-out image of a server) in place of its placeholder, so the template writes no placeholder for it and the placeholders left match the images kept. The router, the session monitor, the outcomes and the transcripts read the client's messages unchanged; only the prompt changes.
- For the caches: images go in steps of half the cap (8 at the default), counted from the conversation's start (`images.left_out`): at 17 images the oldest 8 go and the next 7 images change nothing before the prompt, so the head the resident prefix, the state store and the disk tier resume stays the same for several turns (leaving out one image a turn would change the prompt near its start on every turn and miss every cache). Over the row cap the newest message's images are read first, then the earlier ones newest first; the first that would go over and everything older are left out, rounded up to a whole step, so a full queue still holds at most the row cap of patches. The choice is a function of the message list (and the rows of the images it keeps), so the same history always renders the same prompt.
- Only the newest message's own images are never left out: over a cap on their own, the request is the 400 it was, now `17 images in the newest message; the limit is 16 a request`, naming the first image over. The refusals of a single message (a broken image, the row cap, the encode budget) are unchanged.
- Each request that leaves images out says so: a log line `[images] <request id>: left out the oldest N of M images (the caps: ...)` with counts only, the response header `X-Tandem-Images-Left-Out: N`, `extra.images_left_out` in the journal's router row, and the counter `qse_images_left_out_total` (server/METRICS.md).
- The package side, live before this build (packages v7, 2026-10-03 14:24): `design-review` looks at at most 2 to 3 images a round (one full-page screenshot per width, or a contact sheet stitched from saved shots), never reads an image twice, about 12 in a session, and takes what needs no eyes (overlaps, overflow, contrast, fonts, empty cards) from its DOM audit text; its `max_tokens` 1600 -> 1800 for the longer text (1,692 tokens on the engine's tokenizer).
- After a compaction the class packages come back (the same session, 14:42 to 14:50): every turn before `/compact` carried the design packages (`conductor_hidden_tokens` 6,502); every turn after it carried none, and the model went looking for the Laya endpoint and the design skills on disk. The router's journal said why: opencode 1.18.34 sends its compaction request with its `compaction` agent's prompt as a system message, which the compaction shape (no system text) ruled out, so the request was routed as `design_ui` (seven packages, high effort, 2,116 reasoning tokens) and the session never knew it had been compacted; the `continue` after it was then a new user message, classified `chat` at 0.998, and chat has no package. The replay was not the cause: a note the history no longer carries is not replayed and the class's block goes in again (tests/test_conductor_router.py had that case). `server/conductor/signals.py` `COMPACTION_SHAPES` / `compaction_shape`: no tools, a system message opening with the agent's fixed instruction, the history as the one user message after it, is the compaction (class `summarize`, structural, thinking off, no package; the monitor's S2 watch reads the same flag). `server/conductor/router.py`: the first user message after a compaction keeps the session's class (`source: sticky`, `kept: after_compaction`), no classifier asked; the block goes in again at the compacted history's insertion point, the next turns replay it, and the next message a person writes is classified as any other.
- Tests (CPU): `tests/test_compaction_turns.py` (4: opencode 1.18.34's compaction request is `summarize`, thinking off, no note, no classifier; after it `continue` keeps `design_ui`, the block goes in again (tokens > 0), the tool turn after replays it, the next new message is classified; the same `continue` without a compaction is classified `chat`; the shape is exact: tools, a third message, another system text or a flipped order are not a compaction, the old shape still is); the first two fail on 50cc1f5 exactly as live (`opencode 1.18.34's compaction request`, `('chat', 'qwen')`).
- Tests (CPU): `tests/test_images.py` 8 new (the count rule; the window moves at 17, 25, 33 ... images and nowhere between; 17 images across user, assistant and tool turns: the oldest 8 left out as text, 9 read, the body untouched, a message without a left-out image the same object, the same history the same messages; a broken left-out image is not read; the newest message over the cap is still a 400, and 16 in it with earlier ones are served; the row cap in steps; the checkpoint's chat template (tests/fixtures): 17 placeholders become 9, 8 notes, the text before the first left-out image unchanged; `build_prompt` with the fake tokenizer: the notes in the prompt, the count path the same length, the body unchanged).

What changes on deploy: the server's code. A conversation over the image caps is served with its oldest images left out; opencode 1.18.34's compaction request is routed as the compaction (summarize, thinking off, no package) and the first user message after a compaction keeps the session's class; every other request is as before.

## 0.3.20-test, 2026-10-03

68a056c (0.3.19-test, G2's Packages and Skills screen, what :8000 serves) merged with branch tandem-x1 (on 70e1864): the state lines in time order in opencode and Laya playing the build (branch tandem-x1g2). No serve.env key and no ops/ file change; every new field is optional and absent means what 0.3.19-test does: the raw path and every request's bytes are 0.3.19-test's until a profile sets `ui.states_channel: inline` or a script sends `session`.

- Why opencode showed every `›` line at the top of the turn (a user report's screenshots of 09:23 and 10:03, opencode 1.18.34, the coding profile's `content` channel): read in opencode's binary, its bundled `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` (the module `createOpenAICompatible` is imported from) opens one text part per response at the first content delta (`text-start`, id `txt-0`) and ends it only with the stream, so every later content delta, lines and answer, lands in the part the first line opened, above the reasoning; a reasoning delta after a content or `tool_calls` delta opens a new reasoning part, and the TUI titles a reasoning part with its first line when that is `**title**` and a blank line. In the 10:03 case (`› deciding: chat, low effort`, 20 s of thinking, an essay) the whole answer sat above "Thought: 20.1s". In the 10:46 case the follow-up request after two web fetches said `› reading 11,426 tokens at ~820 tok/s, about 12 s left` twice during its prefill, and the essay was appended to the text part those lines opened, above its 1.1 s thought.
- `ui.states_channel: inline` (server/conductor/states.py INLINE, server/app.py): on a `reasoning_content` stream each line is an empty `{"tool_calls": []}` delta (the provider ends the open reasoning part on it and starts no tool part) and a reasoning delta `\n**› text**\n\n`, never content: each line opens a reasoning part of its own, titled by it (`+ Thought: › thinking 2 min, 4,096 tokens · 1m 31s`), in time order, and the answer's text part opens after them. The waiting line of a queued request goes the same way. The strip takes the title form out of the reasoning a client sends back (opencode joins its reasoning parts with nothing between them), so Qwen's prompt ids are the ones without the lines. `tags` and `both` (Hermes) get `content`'s stream byte for byte; a non-streamed answer carries the lines at the head of its content. Dashboard: the Profiles screen's "where" has `inline`.
- Proof in opencode's own parser: `tools/opencode_bundle.py` takes the provider module (and its imports) out of an opencode binary, `tools/opencode_parts.mjs` runs a recorded stream through it in node and applies the processor's part rules and the TUI's title. On the box (node 24) with opencode 1.18.32 and with the Mac's 1.18.34: `content` reproduces both screenshots (one text part on top with every line and the answer), `inline` gives the lines as titles in order, the thinking under them and the answer last.
- Laya plays the build (server/laya_api.py DRIVER SESSIONS, `server/laya_kit/`): the intended use, Laya drives the software under test while Qwen writes it. `POST /v1/laya/ask` takes an optional `session`: a driver step, rated per session (`api.drive_rate_per_s`, 10 texts a second; `drive_sessions` 4 at once; `drive_max_texts` 36,000), not against the scripts' 240 a minute; no journal row a call, one `laya_drive` row a session at `POST /v1/laya/drive/end {session, summary?}` or `drive_idle_s` (30 s) after its last call: counts, the labels' counts, p, unsure, ms p50/p95/max, the driver's summary (numbers only), the question as a hash, never a state. `GET /v1/laya/kit/<file>` serves the kit. The server's path is 3.1 ms p50 a step (box CPU, fake model, HTTP); with laya-english's 18.7 to 48.7 ms a text (journal, 2026-10-03) a step is about 25 to 50 ms. The idle rule holds for a playtest (it runs inside a tool call): 14 of the day's 16 `laya_api` calls met an idle engine, 2 arrived in the last ~100 ms of the request that wrote the tool call and waited for it (148.5 and 187.8 ms).
- The kit: `laya_drive.py` (stdlib; `browser` over the DevTools protocol with real keys and clicks in a Chrome it starts or `--cdp` attaches to, `proc` over JSON lines, `cmd` with a state and an action command, a Python `Driver`; deaths, wins, stuck spots, the step budget, Laya's busy answers with a fallback action; `.tandem/drive-log.jsonl`; `report` for Qwen: deaths with place, cause and the decisions before them, stuck spots, the actions, Laya's numbers; `serve-log`) and `laya-drive.js` (the same loop inside the page with synthetic keys, for when only the browser tool reaches it).
- The package `laya-playtest` (texts in ~/tandem-packages/laya-playtest: 294 tokens before its reference, 1,384 with it, on the engine's tokenizer; an inline general library package, so the core goes into the prompt and the recipes are `GET /v1/library/laya-playtest`): when to use it, the state, the actions, three episodes, the report, and that every interactive build is playtested before "done". `laya-testing` and `test-web` get one line pointing at it (335 and 352 tokens). `tools/playtest_install.py` stores the package, attaches it after `laya-testing` on every class that lists it (at most 12), and sets a profile's `ui.states_channel: inline`; dry run by default.
- Tests (CPU): `tests/test_state_inline.py` (10: the strip, opencode's shape with the lines as titles in order, a tool call with its checks, a line then thinking then the answer, a follow-up after a tool result whose prefill says `reading ... left` twice (the report's third case, 10:46: the essay drawn above its thought), the replay with the same prompt ids, Hermes byte for byte the content channel, non-streamed, the waiting line, opencode's own parser in node on both channels), `tests/test_laya_drive_api.py` (9: the card, the session's rate apart from the minute's, sessions at once, the end and its journal row without text, an idle session's row, invalid names, the kit routes, the latency, the status contract), `tests/test_laya_drive_kit.py` (8: the pieces, proc wins, deaths with place and cause, busy fallbacks, stuck and the step budget, a UI flow over cmd, the report's text, headless Chromium with real keys and the in-page kit through the log sink), `tests/test_playtest_install.py` (dry run, apply, again, a core that would be cut). Dashboard: tsc, vitest 323, Playwright mock tier conductor and deciders specs 73 passed (desktop 1440, phone 390); dist rebuilt on the box.

What changes on deploy: nothing until the post-deploy stores the package and sets the coding profile's `ui.states_channel: inline` (a dry run first). The kit routes answer at once.

## 0.3.15-test, 2026-10-03

7954241 (0.3.14-test, what :8000 serves since 22:04 on 2026-10-02) plus the fixes for the two failures of its post-deploy live check (branch tandem-d2). No serve.env key, no ops/ file and no conductor document changes; the release's text is 0.3.14-test's.

- The end anchor never engaged live (2026-10-02 22:07, `~/c314-live.py` (a): raw turn 1 138 -> 1,413 tokens, its follow-up of 1,869 tokens `cache_n` 0, source none, TTFT 3,743 ms). The client's copy was not the cause: in the box's suffix store the follow-up held the generated ids token for token through `<|im_end|>`. The router was: the raw model's name is an alias that plans as TandemLLM, and turn 1 got a 66-token note (effort low) inside its user message at token 65. A conversation with no session id is keyed by a hash, and the hash was of its first two messages: the user's alone on turn 1, the user's and the first answer on every turn after. The follow-up was another session (`h:c1c5...` then `h:4e49...` in the journal), turn 1's note was not replayed, and the prompt parted from the resident rows at token 65 -- below the end anchor, below any grid line. The key is now the conversation's head, its messages up to and including the first user message (server/conductor/signals.py `first_hash`); with a system message that is the same two messages as before. Every system-less chat (the raw name, Hermes, Open WebUI) lost its notes and its resident prefix at turn 2 the same way.
- The hidden close's phrase and the template's newline (the same check, (a2): TandemLLM with a client budget of 400, the phrase hidden at 413 reasoning tokens). The replay puts the phrase back where the rows hold it, but the client's copy is re-rendered by the template, `reasoning|trim + "\n</think>"`, and the phrase ends in its own newline: the copy held one `\n` more than the rows right after it (suffix store: the follow-up parted at the token after `Mod 7`, `\n` before `</think>`), so the replay found no match and the turn re-read the whole answer. `ResidentPrefix.replay` aligns runs of whitespace-only tokens next to a hidden span (`glue`, the tokenizer's single tokens for newlines, spaces and a tab, server/app.py `glue_ids`, set at load); every other token must be the rows', and what is served up to the end anchor is the rows' tokens. `usage.prompt_tokens` is the client's count, net of the alignment. This is the rrr2 case the end anchor was built for (the D2 backstop closes with the same phrase).
- Not fixed, documented (docs/caches.md): (a2)'s turn 1 (459 tokens) came right after the 1,932-token raw conversation and was a guest of it (shorter than a quarter of it), and a guest keeps no end anchor -- its rows are written over the resident prompt's stashed ones, which the next request puts back. A short conversation that starts while a longer one is resident re-reads its first answer at turn 2, as every guest re-reads its whole prompt. `~/c315-live.py` gives (a2) a 9,000-token system text, over `--resident-guest-max`.
- The disk restore's text "mismatch" (2026-10-02 22:08, `tools/disk_cache_live.py`: 15,360 tokens restored, 1.79 GB in 334 ms, `same_text` false) was the check's: it compared the raw stream, and the stream held TandemLLM's step lines (`› reading 16,427 tokens at ~800 tok/s, about 18 s left` twice on the cold run, `› waiting: another request is running, position 1` on the disk run) and the tool calls' ids, which the server draws per request. The model's text and the calls' names and arguments were the same: "Let's start by exploring the project to understand what we're dealing with." and `tool_00`/`tool_01` with `{"path": "."}`, both runs. The check now compares the text without the step lines (states.py `strip_text`) and each call's name and arguments, and prints the server's TTFT (23,106 ms cold, 2,681 ms from the disk on 22:08; the client's first piece is a step line). On the GPU (`tools/disk_restore_check.py`, in a hold, the served flags and drafters, a directory of its own) the restore is bit for bit a cold prefill's: a 10,701-token opencode-shaped prompt, the head written behind the request (10,240 tokens, 4 anchors, 10 chunks, 1.71 GB), read back into clobbered buffers in 226 ms: the recurrent states and convolution tails at line 10,240 equal the cold prefill's own at that line, the prefill resumed from the disk equals the cold prefill in the last row's logits, the states, the tails and all 6 position-indexed buffers (target K and V, both drafters' rows), and the served loop writes the same 48 greedy tokens from the disk as cold. In a second process (a restart, so a fresh Triton autotune) the cold prefill is the first process's bit for bit (logits, states, tails, rows, the state at each of its 10 lines), the first process's files restore to it, and the text from the disk is the first process's cold text (hold of 2026-10-02 22:32, `~/d2-diag/{write,read}.json`).
- `tools/end_anchor_identity.py --on-base`: against a base that has the end anchor (7954241), the candidate's turns with it on must equal the base's on as well.

## 0.3.14-test, 2026-10-02

4f47239 (0.3.13-test: K1 c3ade36, C1 f11c0c6 the disk tier, J1 6df4abf snapshots, outcomes, cards and the judge; the hold of 2026-10-02 at 20:51 deploys it) plus branch tandem-s1 ebeb071 (on 4764ae2: a client's side requests served as what they are, the state lines outside the thinking, progress numbers in them), merged as branch tandem-m2, and one engine change: the resident prefix's end anchor, so the turn after a long generation forwards its new messages instead of re-reading the generation. serve.env gets one key (`END_ANCHOR=on`); ops/start.sh passes it.

- Side requests (`structural.side_requests` in the router document, on; `off` serves them as turns, as before). opencode's title and summary calls and Hermes' title call are known by their shape: no tools, and the client's fixed instruction opening the system message (opencode 1.18.34's `title` and `summary` agents, Hermes 0.21.0's title_generator; `structural.side_shapes` replaces the list). Such a request asks no classifier, gets no package, rules or note, leaves the session's class, turns, notes and size alone, thinks only when the client asked for a number of reasoning tokens, and writes at most its shape's cap (64 tokens for a title, 256 for opencode's summary). Journal: `kind: side`, in the decisions feed beside the turns and out of the Overview's and the sessions' figures. In the queue a side request of at most 8,192 prompt tokens goes ahead of every waiting turn (a few seconds of engine); a longer one waits until no turn does. On 2026-10-02 at 18:08 opencode's title request was classed `code_edit` at xhigh, wrote 5,567 tokens and held the session's turn 54 s.
- The state lines outside the thinking (`ui.states_channel` in a profile: `reasoning`, as before and for every profile stored before it; `content`, the seed profiles' value). In `content` every line is a content delta of its own: before the reasoning, between its parts, after it; in `tags` a line said inside the open block waits for `</think>`. The strip already took the lines out of an assistant's content, so the prompt is unchanged; a non-streamed answer carries them at the head of its content.
- Progress numbers (`ui.progress`, on with the lines; `prefill_every_s` 10, `thinking_every_s` 120, `thinking_every_tokens` 4,096): `waiting: opencode's title request runs first, position 1` (`another request is running`) while a request waits, `reading 35,189 tokens at ~750 tok/s, about 47 s left` every 10 s of a long prefill, `thinking 4 min, 9,800 tokens` every 2 minutes or 4,096 tokens of thinking; templates, never the narrator's. A request that waits opens its stream at its first waiting line; a refusal after that (queue timeout, prompt too long, memory) ends the stream with an `error` (its code) and `[DONE]`, and the ledger keeps the status.
- The end anchor (`--end-anchor on|off`, `END_ANCHOR` in serve.env, on; engine/cache.py `ResidentPrefix.keep_end`, server/app.py `_remember`). The re-read after a long thinking (rrr2: 33,172 tokens, about 44 s) was not the hidden close phrase: every turn of that session, and of the 18:08 one, resumed at the previous prompt's last 1,024 line whether a phrase was hidden or not, because the resident prefix anchors prefill chunks only and a long session's snapshot is over the store's entry cap (S1's `tests/test_reread_after_think.py`). At the end of every generation the resident prefix now keeps one anchor more: the recurrent states and convolution tails at the last position the engine forwarded (147 MiB, two buffers reused turn after turn), the rows in place valid up to there. A generation that stopped inside an accepted block has its pending commit cut back to the committed tokens first (`trim_pending`); one whose state already absorbed them keeps none. The next request that starts with every one of those tokens resumes there and forwards only what is new; it is taken when it starts later than the anchors in place, the pin and the park, and a store entry or the disk only when they start later still. The journal's `cache_source` is `end` (the live and requests contracts list it). A resume there is the session cache's kind of resume, held to the greedy gate, and so is every anchor a prefill from there takes: the resident prefix's `taint` is the lowest such row; the store takes no prefix snapshot of such a prompt, the disk tier writes nothing of it and reads over those rows, and a grid anchor at or below it, or a cold prefill, is bit for bit a cold grid prefill's again. The pin and the park carry their rows' line. The end anchor goes with its rows (a prompt that parts inside the generation resumes at the prompt's last line, as before). Memory: asked of the policy once at the new `end` level, given back after the body anchors and before the guest stash. Not for a request with images.
- The hidden tokens put back. What the session monitor hid in an answer (a hidden close's phrase, a hidden turn: `_force_close` records each span) and SP4's note at the prompt's tail are in the rows, not in the client's copy, which then parts from the end anchor at the first of them. Before the prefill (after the router's notes, before SP4; and for the in-context stage's prompt) the server puts them back where they sit when the prompt then starts with every token up to the end anchor (`ResidentPrefix.replay`), else serves the prompt as sent. They stay hidden: not in `prompt_tokens`, the suffix store or the response cache; the journal row has `extra.end_replayed`; the next end anchor carries them on.
- Whether the client's copy matches: in the box's suffix store (2026-10-02, 4,607 turns that followed another, token ids only) the next prompt held the engine's visible output token for token to its end in 3,844 (83 %); the others parted late (91 tokens before the end at the median) and resume at the prompt's line, as before.
- C1's disk tier, two bugs seen live on 0.3.13-test (2026-10-02 21:09, `tools/disk_cache_live.py` FAIL: no disk hit). (1) The writer's CUDA calls (its side-stream copy and synchronize, the pinned staging buffers) ran while the drafter captured its CUDA graph, the first capture after the restart: the copy failed (`cudaErrorStreamCaptureUnsupported`) after 1 of the head's 15 chunks, and the capture with it (an INTERNAL ASSERT in the caching allocator), so the request ended in an error. A process-wide lock (`engine/capture_lock.py`) is held by every capture (engine/drafters/draft_graph.py, engine/verify_graph.py) and by the writer around its CUDA calls, and by the probe writer's event wait. (2) The head's 4 anchors were on disk without their chunks (`complete: false`), so the next session found nothing to read and prefilled its 17,074 tokens cold (22.5 s server-side, with the RAM caches just emptied); and `plan` counted those anchors as written, so no later request would have written the missing chunks. An anchor now counts only with every chunk below it, and such a head is admitted again. `tools/disk_cache_live.py`'s gates: the head must be complete with no writer error, and both compared requests must finish without an error (on 21:09 `same_text` passed on two errored requests). Tests: `tests/test_capture_lock.py` (every capture site under the lock; the writer copies nothing while it is held; a head whose chunks failed is admitted again and then read bit for bit; both disk tests fail on 4f47239's tier), `tests/test_disk_cache_live.py` (the failed run is a FAIL); `tools/capture_race_check.py`: the real writer against graph captures on the GPU, with the lock and without (the control), a hold step.
- S1 with C1: a client's side request is read by the disk tier and admits nothing (`request_tag`'s `side`); it already wrote no J1 snapshot, outcome or card (it returns from the plan before them).
- Tests (random model, CPU): `tests/test_end_anchor.py` (the served loop with no drafter and wrong and right chains and trees: the turn after a 150-token generation resumes at its end and writes the 24 greedy tokens the same turn writes from the prompt's line; a pending commit cut back is the shorter commit's state bit for bit; the replay, its carry-over, SP4's span, the in-context stage; `taint`, the store, the disk, the pin, the park, a guest, memory, the length router's released arm inherited; through the handler with `usage` the client's); `tools/end_anchor_identity.py`: the end anchor off is the base tree's resident prefix bit for bit (tokens, resume points, state, rows, anchors, pin, park), on differs.
- `tools/stream_identity.py`: two trees' streams on the fake engine, byte for byte, with S1's switches off (or at their defaults, where only the title request may differ).

What changes on deploy: the disk tier stays as the settings say (off since the 21:09 FAIL, settings v1); the post-deploy check turns it on, runs `tools/disk_cache_live.py` and leaves it on only when the head is read from the disk with the same text. Opencode's and Hermes' title requests are served as side requests at once (the stored router has no `side_requests`, so it is on). The coding profile on the box (v8, `ui.states: on`, no channel) keeps its lines in the reasoning and gains the progress lines there (on by default with the lines); its stream now opens while it waits for the engine. Moving coding's lines into the content is a profile version (`ui.states_channel: content`, Profiles › What the user sees). The end anchor is on: a turn that sends back the whole previous answer resumes at its end (`cached_tokens` = the previous prompt plus its generation), 147 MiB more under the 70 GiB ceiling; `END_ANCHOR=off` and a restart is 0.3.13-test's resident prefix. A rollback to 0.3.13-test (4f47239) ignores `END_ANCHOR`, and like one to 0.3.12-test refuses a router version saved with `side_requests` or `side_shapes` and a profile version saved with `states_channel` or `progress`, and serves the newest older version.

## 0.3.13-test, 2026-10-02

c3ade36 (0.3.12-test 4764ae2 plus K1, branch tandem-k1: the claim check E2, general packages, the eval's effort to PASS; what :8000 serves since the hold of 2026-10-02 19:12, its entries are the last part below) plus two branches merged onto it as branch tandem-m1: C1 (branch tandem-c1 f11c0c6), the disk tier the owner asked for on 2026-10-02 -- the ~24-30k-token head every opencode session starts with, the prefixes prefilled more than once and the packages in them, kept on the NVMe under a budget set in the dashboard; and J1 (branch tandem-j1 6df4abf), the turn snapshots, the Tier 0 turn outcomes, the client tool card and the harness card, the evaluation points, Laya as the test judge in shadow and retrieval on low quality (the plan "Laya as the test judge, state snapshots, turn outcomes and the client protocol", steps 1 to 4 and 6 to 8; step 5 is package texts, step 9 not built). The merge keeps both: the router's plan carries C1's `spans` beside J1's snapshot, outcome and extra notes, and the disk tier's spans cover J1's notes too (an entry whose notes are an outcome's note or a card is labelled a prefix on the Disk cache tab, not a package: a card's parts are of kind card). The disk tier is off in the code; serve.env gets one key (`QSE_DISK_CACHE`), which the deploy sets to `~/.qwen38-spark-engine/cache/disk` and `ops/start.sh` passes to the :8000 service only (a row, gate or soak server never has the tier). With the tier off, every prefill runs the code path of c3ade36 (the prefill takes `disk=None`); with it on, a request that starts from the disk computes the same bytes as a cold prefill on the grid, and the served text is the same (tests). Every J1 part is a switch in a profile's new `outcomes` section, off when absent; the router document's optional `outcomes` section holds the settings over the defaults. The engine's decode path is c3ade36's; the served loop gains one call before the prefill (Qwen asked in place on a narrowed case, off unless the router document's `outcomes.evaluate.ask.mode` is shadow) and the monitor's claim check one optional text.

- The disk tier (`engine/disk_cache.py`). Chunk files hold 1,024 tokens of rows of every position-indexed buffer (the attention KV and the drafters'), keyed by the prefix hash, with the token ids inside; anchor files hold the 48 recurrent states and their convolution tails at one line, with the chain of chunk hashes below it. Written with O_DIRECT, to a temp file, fsynced and renamed; crc32 per section; the files are the index. What is written: the longest line a prompt has had prefilled cold `admit_after` (2) times, and the first long request of a session at its last 4 lines below where its user message starts; the chunks below them not on disk yet. An anchor's state is copied to a staging slot as the prefill passes its line; the rows are written behind the request from the engine's buffers until the next prefill fences them (a write that cannot finish in that window is dropped and journaled). The lookup comes after the resident prefix, the pin, the park and the state store, takes the disk only where it starts later and its read costs less than the prefill it saves, reads only the chunks above the rows in place, compares every stored token id with the prompt's before a byte reaches the engine, and makes the restored prompt the resident one with the disk anchor as its anchor. A file that fails its check goes with every longer chunk of its chain, and the request resumes from the rows in place or starts cold. Eviction least valuable first (hits, tokens saved per byte held, halved per day unused), a TTL (7 days), and never under 50 GB free on the NVMe. A file of another fingerprint (weights, engine code, arithmetic flags, grid, library versions) is swept at the start. The staging buffer (2 anchor and 2 chunk slots, 0.5 GB on the served stack) is its host footprint, allocated at the first use and counted in the engine's declared peak until then.
- Settings: `settings.memory.disk_cache` (`mode`, `budget_gb` 50, `ttl_days` 7, `admit_after` 2, `min_free_gb` 50, which the schema holds at 50 or more), versioned like the transcript settings, applied at the next request. The Memory screen's new Disk cache tab: the bytes against the budget, the NVMe's free space, the hit rate, the tokens restored and the last restore's time and rate, the most-hit prefixes (token counts; a preview for opencode heads and packages only), the last events, the settings, a clear button; phone layout as cards. Routes: `GET /v1/conductor/memory/disk`, `POST /v1/conductor/memory/disk/clear`, `POST /v1/cache/clear?tier=disk|all`; `/v1/cache/stats` gains `disk_cache` (counts, no previews). The journal gains `kind` memory, `task` disk_cache rows (hit, write, evict, drop, restore_failed, clear, error); `/metrics` gains `qse_disk_cache_*`. A request restored from the disk has `cache_source` `disk` in the ledger and the live view (contract: additive).
- `tools/disk_cache_bench.py` (CPU only, a temporary directory): on the box, O_DIRECT writes at 4.3 GB/s, reads at 7.35 GB/s, crc32 at 5.6 GB/s. A 30,720-token head is 3.43 GB: 0.47 s at the read rate, about 0.6 s with the checksum, against about 44 s of cold prefill (arithmetic; the board's restore is measured after the deploy). `tools/disk_cache_live.py`: the post-deploy check (a warm-up session writes the head; a fresh opencode-shaped session's first request reads it; TTFT against a cold run of the same prompt; the same text).
- J1: the turn snapshot (`outcomes.snapshots: on`, `server/conductor/outcomes.py`). At the start of every request whose newest message is a tool result the router builds, from the body alone, what the session did since the last one: the calls (8, results clipped to 1,200 characters), the files written (path, size, a hash), the last write and run, each screenshot's hash and size, the console's level counts and error lines, the checker lines and the session's best per gate, exit codes, a test runner's counts, the `tandem_state` dump and its diff, a `.tandem/*.log` tail. The transcript writer stores it as `snapshots/turn-<n>.json` beside block n (0600, at most 32 KB) with the images under `shots/` (the newest 5 a session), one `snapshot:` line in the block's runtime section and `counts.snapshots` in meta.json. 0.023 ms a request (median over the two Mario sessions, box CPU). Pure observation: the plan and the prompt are the same.
- Tier 0 outcomes (`outcomes.mode: shadow | act`). One outcome a tool-result turn, the first label of the router document's `outcomes.order` whose facts matched (no_visible_change, regression, error, low_quality, surprise, stuck, tool_misuse, test_faked, environment, lost_context), `progress`, or `none`. Every fact is structural: an equal hash after a write, a worse number, an exit code, a runner's counts, a console level, an OS error string, a call the client refused, a script that assigns to a member of an object it did not declare. Journaled as `kind: outcome` with its evidence; the route row has `extra.outcome`; `tools/tandem_eval.py` counts them per session (`efforts.outcomes`, schema additive). Act: no visible change and regression set the turn to xhigh, error to high (never below the class's), held for `raise_turns` (2) tool turns or until a progress; the outcomes in `acting` (the three) add their note once per signature (the E-a note with the snapshot's digest, at most 2,100 characters), replayed at the same token position like every router note, counted as an act under the profile's caps (the monitor adopts it); at the cap the effort still changes and the note is dropped.
- The client tool card and the harness card (`outcomes.cards`). For a coding class with tools: the request's own tools (names, required arguments starred, which take a path) with the client kind's pitfalls package (`tools-opencode`, `tools-hermes`), and the `tandem-harness` package, each kept live in the session's notes (in on the first turn and again after a compaction dropped them). A tool-misuse outcome brings the tool card back as its note.
- Evaluation (`outcomes.evaluate`, step 6). E-c: stuck and low quality go to xhigh with the re-plan note and the digest. E-b: the claim check's note carries the turn's digest (act; shadow journals its size). Qwen in place on a narrowed case (a run's output with no exit code and no counts), through the in-context stage's forward before the turn's prefill, journaled beside the twin, shadow only and off by default (`outcomes.evaluate.ask.mode`).
- Laya as the test judge (`outcomes.judge: shadow`, `server/conductor/judge.py`). On the narrowed cases (`failure`: a run's output without an exit code or counts; `build`: a `.tandem` log tail) Laya is asked after the request on the judge's own thread, through the `decider` role, with a 100 ms deadline; each answer, timeout or failure is a `kind: outcome` row (task `judge`) beside the Tier 0 twin. It acts on nothing. `tools/judge_report.py` gives the confident precision and coverage per question and the gate (0.95 and 0.3).
- Retrieval (`outcomes.retrieve`, step 8): a low-quality or stuck outcome asks the router's package question over `retrieve.packages` (the kind skills) and the package that fits is the note, once per signature.
- The secret-pattern refusal covers J1's text as it covers the transcript blocks: every string of a snapshot file, every outcome's evidence line and every digest that goes into a note.
- The Memory screen: a session's line counts its snapshots and each block's runtime section names its snapshot with the turn's outcome (dist rebuilt; the memory schemas' `counts` allow `snapshots`).
- K1 (live as c3ade36): the claim check, E2 (`server/conductor/monitor/claimcheck.py`, ops/supervisor.yaml version 5, shadow). A coding turn (the router's class in `code_edit`, `debug`, `design_ui`, `three_d`, `drawing`) of a session with a write behind it that ends on a non-empty answer with no tool call: Qwen itself answers, in place under the request's engine lock, thinking off, one letter each, whether the message claims the work is done (Q1) and what the tool evidence since the last write says (Q2: supported, no_run_after_last_write, errors_in_evidence, surprise_unexplained, test_faked). An answer other than supported continues the turn hidden with its note; everything else takes the end token as drawn (fail-open). Once a request, two notes a session, under the caps; journaled at tier 1 with both answers, the structural twin and the calls since the write, and an outcome label (fixed, ran_no_fix, no_run) later. The profiles' E2 (shadow in coding and overnight) sets its mode, `claim_at` and `admit_at`; E2 needs no role any more. The two Mario sessions of 2026-10-02 are the replay fixture: it fires on both final messages.
- K1 (live as c3ade36): general packages: a package with `general: true` in the packages document goes in whole on every turn of a class that lists it, before the task skill the router picks among the rest (so three_d and drawing can carry the coding package and their recipe).
- K1 (live as c3ade36): `tools/tandem_eval.py`: tool calls and turns to PASS beside the minutes to PASS, per run and per suite and arm; every comparison and both report tables read the records' `minutes_to_pass`, never the wall minutes; the pass rule decided on 2026-10-02: a run of a suite with a final check passes by its verdict, the stage gates are progress. The report schema's new fields are optional.

What changes on deploy: what TandemLLM and raw answer does not change. C1: the first long request of each opencode session and every prefix prefilled twice are written to `~/.qwen38-spark-engine/cache/disk` (0700) behind the request, up to 50 GB; the next session's first request starts from the disk. Turning it off is `mode: off` on the Disk cache tab (no restart; the files stay) or `QSE_DISK_CACHE=off` and a restart. J1: the deploy stores profile versions of coding and overnight with an `outcomes` section (snapshots on, the outcomes in shadow, the judge off), as `j1-install.py` does; no stored router has an `outcomes` section and the package texts (the tool and harness cards, the kind skills) are installed after the deploy by J1's installer (a packages version and a router version, dry run first), so nothing is injected until then; the Memory screen shows the snapshot count and line where a session has them. K1 is live already (its monitor document version 2 with E2 in shadow stays as stored). A rollback to c3ade36 leaves the disk directory and the snapshot files on the disk (it neither reads nor deletes them), refuses a settings version saved with `memory.disk_cache` (it serves the version before) and restores the coding and overnight profiles to the versions current before the deploy.

## 0.3.12-test, 2026-10-02

0.3.11-test d539719 (tandem-f2) plus ENG-181 (branch tandem-p2, built on 62d9f5a and merged onto d539719; epic VIS-E7, R2 of the roles and harmony design): snapshots of Qwen's own rows at the router's three decision points, the tool that trains the first probes on them, and the router's probe stage, every part off by default. The engine's decode path and `ops/` are 0.3.11-test's; the loop gains a `probe` argument that only a request with the snapshots on passes, and the block drafters a read-only `tapped()`. serve.env gets two keys (`QWEN38_PROBE_SNAPSHOTS=off`, `QWEN38_PROBE_DIR`). With the snapshots off, TandemLLM's output is 0.3.11's and raw is byte-identical; with them on, the output is the same (tests on every verify path: tokens, context, KV and recurrent state equal with and without a capture).

- Probe snapshots (`server/probe.py`, `QWEN38_PROBE_SNAPSHOTS=on`; a design decision of 2026-10-01: box only, 30 days, tool requests only). For a TandemLLM request with tools (raw never, chats without tools never), one row per tapped layer (the five layers the block drafters read, 5, 19, 33, 47, 61) and the post-norm row, fp16, at the last message's last token (class and effort: the row the router's note and the thinking splice do not move, so a probe can read it before the router decides), every 1,024 reasoning tokens as the mean of the rows the crossing block committed (stuck, decided), and at a finish candidate (done; the last one of a turn that ended in calls is dropped). No extra forward: the rows are the ones the drafters already read, copied asynchronously behind the forward into pinned slots allocated once. A ring on the NVMe (`~/.qwen38-spark-engine/probe/snapshots/<day>/`, records and an index line each with the journal row id, the session, the class and effort, the point and the outcome keys; no text), written by its own thread after the request ended, journaled (`kind = probe`), at most 100 MB a day, 30 days, pruned at start and at 04:00, refused inside a repository. Night 2's traffic writes 81.1 MB (1,023 TandemLLM requests with tools, 271 think points, 17 done claims, 61,860 bytes a point with its index line). `X-Tandem-Probe: off` takes a request out (the live A/B of `tools/probe_measure.py`).
- `tools/probe_train.py`: `fit` joins the snapshots to the journal's later rows (the class Qwen decided in its no-think or in-context answer and the 216-prompt fixture's labels; the D1 guard's acts for stuck; the next checker RESULT for done), fits a logistic probe per question held out by session, and reports, beside the class accuracy, the source-confound numbers (arXiv 2606.02907): the accuracy of a probe predicting the source from the same rows, the class from the source alone, the deconfounded accuracy (each source's mean row removed) and leave-one-source-out. Gates: class 90 % on the deconfounded split, stuck precision 0.9 at the guard's act rate over 30 positives. `fixture` sends the 216 prompts through a server with the snapshots on (one output token each, GPU), `growth` reads a night's bytes from the ledger.
- The probe stage (`classifier.probe_stage` in the router document: off, shadow, on; a probe file and `accept` 0.9). Shadow: the request's own prompt snapshot is answered after the request into `extra.probe`. On: where the plan decides under the engine lock (the in-context stage's follow-ups and long prompts), the probe answers first on a prefill of the turn's prompt up to its insertion point, and the question is asked only below `accept` (stage and source `probe`). One answer is 17 us on the box CPU (6 x 5,120 rows, 9 classes). A probe of other weights, width or rows is refused. Contract: the router schema and the decisions schema (stage `probe`, `stage_ms`) are additive.

What changes on deploy: nothing in what TandemLLM answers. serve.env gains `QWEN38_PROBE_SNAPSHOTS` (off unless the deploy runs with `SNAP=on`) and `QWEN38_PROBE_DIR`; the stored router has no `classifier.probe_stage`, so the stage is off. Turning the snapshots on is the serve.env key and a restart; the stage is a router version. A rollback to 0.3.11-test leaves the ring on the disk and refuses a router version saved with `probe_stage` (it serves the version before).

## 0.3.11-test, 2026-10-02

0.3.10-test 468d669 plus P1 of "One engine for all models" (branch tandem-n1): MiniCPM5-2B inside the engine as the narrator that writes the state lines, off by default; and a per-turn-kind effort for tool-result turns (branch tandem-f2), inherit by default. The engine's decode path and `ops/` are 0.3.10-test's; serve.env gets two keys (`QWEN38_NARRATOR_MODEL`, set to `minicpm5-2b` by the deploy, and `QWEN38_NARRATOR_DIR`), and nothing loads at the start. With `ui.narrator` off, which is what every stored profile gets, TandemLLM's output is 0.3.10's and raw is byte-identical.

- A small-model slot in the engine (`engine/generative/`): a generative model with its own tokenizer, weights and KV cache, loaded through the residency planner like the decision models (its own memory pool and stream, the planner's check for its role, never during a hold or beside another load, its measured MemAvailable drop journaled as `loaded`, three failures in a minute unload it), and run inside a time budget: the deadline is checked before every token. The first model is MiniCPM5-2B (`openbmb/MiniCPM5-2B`, a `LlamaForCausalLM`, BF16): the forward is our own plain PyTorch Llama (`engine/generative/llama.py`, eager, greedy, 1,024 cache rows, the longest common prefix of the last prompt reused), no transformers model, no SGLang or vLLM. Its greedy ids equal transformers' on the real checkpoint for 12 of 12 narrator prompts (box CPU, BF16, `tools/narrator_reference.py`), and its logits equal transformers' on a random tiny checkpoint in fp32 (tests).
- The narrator (`server/conductor/narrator.py`, profile `ui.narrator`, off by default). With the state lines on and the narrator on, each line is the narrator's: the step's kind, its meaning and its facts in words go to the model, which answers with one line of at most 14 words and 24 tokens inside the `narrator` role's latency budget (150 ms); a request spends at most four budgets. Anything else -- not loaded yet (the first line starts the load), refused, out of time, at the token cap, too many words, markup, an error -- is the template, journaled with the reason (`extra.states[].summary` and `.narrator`). It runs on the request's thread when the line goes out (before the prefill, between two of Qwen's rounds, after the last token), Qwen waiting, never beside Qwen. A narrated line ends in a WORD JOINER (U+2060) before the frame's blank line, and the strip takes such a line of any text, so Qwen never sees one either. The roles document's `narrator.mode` (`on`, `shadow`: journal only, `off`) and budget apply without a restart. Routes: `GET /v1/conductor/narrator/status`, `POST .../load|unload`, `POST .../try`. The Profiles screen has the switch under "What the user sees".
- The role contract knows a `generative` kind: window `between_rounds` (a generative role only, at most 1,000 ms a call), writes `state_lines` (a generative role only; the honesty rule stands: only the reasoner writes client-visible tokens), contract `generate`. A roles document stored before the narrator gets the built-in `narrator` role (journaled as a default). The residency document claims 6 GiB for it (declared, in the order after the decider); the engine's ceiling leaves its bytes out as it leaves the decision models'. The session monitor's tool-check event carries the calls' tool names and file paths to the state lines (not to the journal). Contract: additive (roles, profiles, seeds).
- The effort of a tool-result turn (F2). The router document's `structural.tool_turn_effort` (`inherit`, `off`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`; a profile's `thinking.tool_turn_effort` over it) gives a turn whose newest message is a tool result, SRV-161's tool media included, that level's thinking switch and cap (low: 1,024 by the hidden close); the first turn and every new user message keep the class's, the note stays the class's (the prompt is the same token for token), a client's own number still wins, a checker FAIL raises the level as before. Journaled as `extra.effort_source: tool_turn` with `extra.class_effort`. `inherit`, the default and what every stored document gets, plans as 0.3.10 (the test session's 18 turns plan and render identically on 62d9f5a and the branch). Routing › Stickiness and structure and Profiles › Thinking edit it. Built to test why spiral reached PASS fastest when its tool turns ran at chat/low by the SRV-161 bug (eval arm f: profile `overnight-f`, `low`). Contract: additive (router, profiles, meta).
- `tools/narrator_measure.py`: the n = 1 live check (night 2's recorded events through the narrator at its budget and with the budget lifted, latency p50/p90, and Qwen's decode rate with and without the narrator writing lines, gate 3 %). `tools/narrator_reference.py`: the forward against transformers.

What changes on deploy: nothing in what TandemLLM answers (no stored router or profile has `tool_turn_effort`, so every tool turn keeps the class's effort). serve.env gains `QWEN38_NARRATOR_MODEL=minicpm5-2b` and `QWEN38_NARRATOR_DIR`; the server then serves the narrator role but loads nothing until a profile with `ui.narrator: on` asks for a line (MiniCPM5-2B is on the box under `~/.qwen38-spark-engine/models/minicpm5-2b`, 5.03 GB). Turning it on is a profile version, no restart. A rollback to 0.3.10-test refuses a roles version saved with the `generative` kind or a router or profile version saved with `ui.narrator` or `tool_turn_effort` (0.3.10's schema does not know them): it serves the newest older version and shows the error in `GET /v1/conductor/config`.

## 0.3.10-test, 2026-10-02

0.3.9-test 94f129b plus two features of branch tandem-g1, both off by default: Qwen decides inside the conversation it already holds (the in-context stage), and TandemLLM's own steps shown to the user as lines in the reasoning (`ui.states`). The engine's decode path and `ops/` are 0.3.9-test's (`engine/cache.py` gains `checkpoint_upto`, which only the stage passes), serve.env gets no new key. With both off, which is what every stored router and profile on the box gets, TandemLLM's output is 0.3.9's; raw (`X-Tandem: raw`) is byte-identical. One thing runs on every TandemLLM request from the deploy: the handler takes framed state lines (`\n› <template text>\n\n`) out of the assistant messages a client sends back, which changes nothing for a request that has none.

- Qwen decides with the conversation it already holds (the in-context stage). A follow-up (a user message after an earlier answer) or a prompt of at least `min_tokens` (8,192) is classified by the engine itself: under the engine lock, right before the turn's own prefill, it prefills the turn's prompt up to its last message (the session's notes replayed) plus a hidden question with one letter per class, thinking off, and takes the class from the last row's logits over the letters (one token each, nothing decoded). Laya keeps short first messages. The turn then resumes at the grid line below its insertion point, so it re-reads at most a grid chunk plus its note and tail; its logits and state equal the turn without the stage bit for bit (tests on the random model, including the drafter's rows and the anchors). The stage takes state-store snapshots only at lines up to where the turn parts from it and no session snapshot; nothing of the question streams, counts in `usage` or reaches the turn. Journaled as stage `qwen_context` (label, confidence, probabilities, ms, its prompt tokens, prefilled and reused) and source `qwen_context`. Below its threshold, failing or not run, the session's class. Switched by the router document's `classifier.context_stage` (`mode` off by default, `min_tokens`, `followups`, `accept`, `question`); off, nothing changes and the prompt is never counted. Images in the conversation go through the stage expanded as the turn's prompt expands them (the same rows, rotary coordinates and cache keys), so opencode's sessions with screenshots are classified in context too, and the turn after the stage is bit-identical (test on the random vision model). `cache.prefill` gains `checkpoint_upto`. Contract: the decisions schema allows the stage and the source (additive).
- TandemLLM's steps shown to the user (`ui.states` in a profile, off by default). Each step the conductor takes is one short line in the reasoning the client already renders, at the moment it happens: `deciding: code_edit, high effort`, `retrieving: skill photo-to-3d`, `compaction seen`, `steering: gate progress`, `thinking closed at the 16,384 cap`, `loop detected, steering`, `empty answer, continuing`, `checking the tool call`, `repairing the tool call`, `asking for the tool call again`, `giving up` (`reading memory: N notes` is defined for later). Templates, no model, no latency; a `summary` field per line for a clerk later. The marker is `›` and a space, framed as `"\n› text\n\n"`; in `reasoning_content` a delta, in `tags` inside `<think>` (a step after the block closed is left out of `tags`); a non-streamed answer carries them in its reasoning. Whenever the conductor is configured, the server strips every framed template line from the reasoning and content a client sends back (opencode returns its reasoning as `reasoning_content`), so the prompt and the cached prefix are what they would be without the feature (tests: the same prompt ids on the checkpoint's template, the same engine prompt and usage through the handler). Not in `usage`, the suffix store or the response cache's key; the journal has `extra.states` and `extra.states_stripped`, the transcript a `### states` block. `ui.kinds` turns a kind off. The Profiles screen has the switch. Only for a profile in mode `on` and `n` = 1; off, raw and shadow stream every byte as before.

What changes on deploy: nothing in what TandemLLM answers. The router document on the box has no `classifier.context_stage` and loads with the stage off; no stored profile has `ui`, so every profile's state lines are off. Turning either on is a config version (Routing › Qwen in the conversation, Profiles › What the user sees), no restart; `~/c310-live.py` turns them on for its checks and restores the versions it found. A rollback to 0.3.9-test refuses a router or profile version saved with the new keys (0.3.9's schema does not know them): it serves the newest older version and shows the error in `GET /v1/conductor/config`, as the 0.3.9 rollback note says for roles.

## 0.3.9-test, 2026-10-02

0.3.8-test plus stage R1 of the roles and harmony design (VIS-E7, branch tandem-r1, built on the night of 2026-10-01 from a17e99f) and the client thinking budgets (branch tandem-budget, 2026-10-02), both merged onto 0.3.8-test 54f5c98. The engine's decode path and `ops/` are 0.3.8-test's, serve.env gets no new key. R1 adds no step to the path that produces TandemLLM's answer (the transcript writer reads the request after it ended, on its own thread); raw (`X-Tandem: raw`) is byte-identical and is never seen by the writer.

- The role contract (SRV-133). A role in the `roles` document declares `kind`, `memory_claim_gib` (renamed from `memory_gb`), `window`, `preemptible`, `latency_budget_ms`, `fallback`, `tokenizer_sha256`, `writes` and `sharing`; a role without a claim or a window, a client-visible writer that is not the reasoner, `in_decode` for a kind other than a decider or a probe, and token sharing without the engine's own tokenizer hash are refused. The live v2 roles document loads with defaults, journaled once per start; a restore of an older version writes it whole. The registry checks each decision model against the same contract (Laya claims 4.4 GiB, the first checkpoint's measured MemAvailable). The Profiles screen edits every field with the reason an option is off; the Deciders screen shows each model's contract. Contract: `memory_gb` is now `memory_claim_gib` (old versions load), the rest additive.
- Session transcripts on the NVMe (SRV-137): one markdown block per TandemLLM request with tools under `~/.qwen38-spark-engine/memory/sessions/<yyyy-mm>/<session>/` (`transcript.md` and `meta.json`), compaction blocks, counters only for chats without tools, the secret-pattern refusal on every block (counts per kind in the journal, never the value), `0600`, 30 days with keep, `settings.memory.transcripts` versioned like the rest. Written by its own thread after the request ended. Only the :8000 service's conductor directory (`~/.qwen38-spark-engine/conductor`) writes there; any other conductor directory keeps its memory inside itself, a memory directory inside a git work tree is refused, and a server without the conductor (every benchmark row) writes none.
- The Conductor view's Memory screen (VIS-48, VIS-49): the sessions list with a keep switch, a transcript viewer (200 blocks a page, hidden notes and acts highlighted with a jump to their journal row, compactions folded), Markdown and JSON export, the transcript settings; `/v1/conductor/memory/*` needs the admin token for reads too. Phone layout: cards and a full-width viewer.
- Client thinking budgets in every request shape, and an answer reserve (`server/thinking.py`). The server read `max_reasoning_tokens` and `thinking_budget` and nothing else, and took `reasoning_effort` as a template word: a client that sent its budget another way got no cap, and a turn whose reasoning ran into `max_tokens` ended inside the block with no answer (the Hermes agent sends `reasoning_effort: medium`; twice it reported "Thinking Budget Exhausted"). Now OpenRouter's `reasoning` object, Anthropic's `thinking` object, the budget numbers in `chat_template_kwargs` and under other servers' names, the effort words as their levels' caps (minimal and low 1,024, medium 8,192, high 16,384, xhigh and max none) and every off form are read into one budget, with the precedence in docs/server.md; a client that asked for one gets its reasoning closed early enough to leave `--answer-reserve` tokens of the output limit for the answer after the closing phrase (`auto`: min(2,048, a quarter of the limit)). The close is the monitor's hidden one where it acts (journal task `client` or `reserve`), ThinkBudget's streamed phrase otherwise. Under TandemLLM's router a client's number wins and its effort word yields to the turn's level. **This changes the output** only for a request that sends one of these fields: a client's own `max_reasoning_tokens` under an acting monitor now closes hidden instead of streaming the phrase, and every client that sends an effort word (Hermes sends `medium` by default, an opencode model with `reasoning_effort` in its options sends it on every turn) gets the reserve and, outside the router, the word's cap. A request with none of them, and raw, are byte-identical.
- The chat template's 500 on effort words (the budgets branch). The template renders only `low`, `medium` and `xhigh` and raised on any other word, so `reasoning_effort` `high`, `none`, `minimal` or `max` (what Hermes sends for its `/reasoning` levels and for thinking off) was a 500. Now `minimal` renders as `low`, `max` as `xhigh`, `high` leaves the template at the server default and is the cap alone, and `none` renders the template's own thinking off (byte-identical to `enable_thinking: false`); an unknown word is a 400 naming the field.

What changes on deploy: the stored roles version (v2) has no contract fields and loads with the defaults (window idle, preemptible, fallback PASS, writes nothing, tokenizer none, sharing text, the budget its timeout, the kind from its name), journaled once per start; nothing is written to the roles document until it is saved. The settings document has no stored version on the box, so the seed applies (transcripts scope `tools`, 30 days, clip 4,000 characters): from the first TandemLLM request with tools after the start, transcripts accumulate under `~/.qwen38-spark-engine/memory/`. R1's gate is one night of transcripts with 0 bytes written outside `~/.qwen38-spark-engine/`. A rollback leaves the memory directory in place (0.3.8-test does not read it). The budgets add the `--answer-reserve` flag (`auto` by default; `QSE_ANSWER_RESERVE`), not a serve.env key: from the deploy, a request that sends a budget field (a number, an effort word, an on or off form) gets the reserve, and on the raw name its effort word's cap.

## 0.3.8-test, 2026-10-02

0.3.7-test plus the tickets of VIS-E7 built on the night of 2026-10-01 (branch tandem-night2: tandem-night-tickets with SRV-157, SRV-153 and OPS-49, then SRV-159 and the eval tooling). The engine (`engine/`) and `ops/` are 0.3.7-test's, serve.env gets no new key. What TandemLLM serves changes in one place on purpose, the effort levels' caps (SRV-159); effort by task size stays in shadow (no stored profile has `thinking.by_size`), the classifier's context line stays off, xhigh stays uncapped, so 0.3.8 measures like 0.3.7 apart from the caps. Raw (`X-Tandem: raw`) is byte-identical.

- Real thinking budgets per effort level (SRV-159). Before, medium, high and xhigh all had budget 0 and differed by their sentence alone. Now low caps reasoning at 1,024 tokens (as before), medium at 8,192, high at 16,384, xhigh has no cap below the D2 backstop (as before), off stays thinking off. **This changes TandemLLM's output** on turns at medium and high: today that is `research` (medium) and `plan`, `design_ui`, `drawing` and `three_d` (high); `code_edit` and `debug` stay xhigh, uncapped (with effort by task size on, a small `code_edit` task thinks at high and gets the 16k cap). The cap closes with the session monitor's hidden close (SP1, as the D2 backstop does): the vendor's phrase goes into the model's context and the client receives `</think>` and the answer; `low`'s close, which streamed the phrase before, is hidden the same way. Without a monitor that acts, or for `n` > 1, ThinkBudget's streamed phrase closes it as before. A profile's `thinking.budgets` overrides a level (Profiles › Thinking); the Routing screen edits the levels; both are versioned. A client's own budget still wins and raw is untouched. The router document on the box has no stored version, so the new caps apply on deploy; restoring them is a router version with the old values.
- A tool's media is a tool-result turn (SRV-161). opencode sends an image a tool returned (a `read` of a PNG, a browser screenshot) as a user message right after the tool results, captioned `Attached media from tool result:`. The router took it for a new user message: Laya was unsure, Qwen said `chat` at 0.96, and the session switched to `chat` at low effort (1,024-token cap) for every tool turn after it. Read from the ledger: in every photo3d TandemLLM session of eval night 2 and round 1, 3 to 5 turns ran as `three_d` and about 90 % as `chat`/low (14 to 21 turns a session at the 1,024 cap); spiral the same after its first `code_edit` turns. Now such a message (after tool results, media parts, no text but the caption) keeps the session's class and asks no model, journaled `kept: tool_media`; a person's message with an image is classified as before. **This changes TandemLLM's output** on the image suites: their turns think at their class's effort (three_d and drawing high, 16,384 cap) instead of chat/low. Whether that changes their pass rate is untested (round 1's photo3d passed with the old routing).
- Effort by task size (SRV-157). The class sets the ceiling and the session's size picks within it: `code_edit` thinks at `high` while its task is small and at `xhigh` once it is medium or large. The size comes from four structural signals (the prompt tokens the session added after its first request, the files its tool calls named, the most gates a checker's RESULT line named, the turns), each with two thresholds in the router document's `effort.size` (first guesses from eval round 1: 20k/60k tokens, 3/8 files, 4/8 gates, 30/100 turns); it never falls within a task, and a compaction starts it over. The profile's `thinking.by_size` (off, shadow, on) says whether it acts; shadow is the seed and what every profile stored before it gets, so a deploy changes no effort until a profile sets it on. The journal keeps the size, its signals, the ceiling and the effort per turn (`extra.size`, `shadow.size`). The Routing screen edits the levels per class and the thresholds, the Profiles screen the mode, the test box shows the size. `tools/tandem_eval.py` reports turns per effort level per run and per suite and arm (the `efforts` and `size_mode` columns; the Compare screen shows them).
- The classifier's digest is sized per stage (SRV-153): the decider's to its own limits, head and tail. Before, the decider cut the 2,000-character digest from the front and never saw a long message's tail; on the new long set Laya's best guess went from 29 to 33 of 60 right (requests at the tail 7 to 14 of 20) and its confident wrong answers from 3 to 0, the short set unchanged. The context line (`prev=code_edit@0.93 tools=read,edit,bash files=.py,.md checker=calccheck:FAIL compaction=no`, at most 120 characters out of the tail's share, never a path or a file's text) is built and switched by the router document's `classifier.context_line`, off: with Laya alone it failed the ship rule (short set 50.0 % to 32.4 % right at 0.80; follow-ups that change the task 10 to 1 of 12, pulled to the previous class). The Qwen stage with the line is not measured yet. `tools/conductor_eval.py` compares digest variants (`--digest today,sized,line`) on several sets (`--set` repeated), reports the router's stickiness as its own stage, and can load the decision models in process on the CPU (`--local-deciders laya-english --device cpu`) without touching a server. New labelled sets: 60 long prompts of 1,600 to 7,200 tokens (five classes, the request at the head, the tail or the middle) and 66 short follow-ups whose class the session decides (`tests/fixtures/conductor/make_sets.py` writes both).
- `tools/idle_gaps.py` (OPS-49, Harmony R0): the idle gaps between a session's requests from a copy of the usage ledger and opencode's steps (names and times only), per tool kind, as a histogram with percentiles, gaps over 5 and 20 s per hour, the idle time per session hour and what fits in the gaps. Read-only; the live ledger is refused.
- `tools/conductor_eval.py` counts one way (night plan A2): per model stage all right (the best guess, threshold ignored), confident right (right and at or above the threshold, over all prompts), coverage and confident precision, with the threshold and the errored answers (NOT A COUNT when any); `--rescore REPORT --at 0.6,0.8` re-counts a kept report. The morning's 63.9 % and the night's 50.0 % for Laya on the 216 prompts were the same answers counted at 0.60 and at 0.80.
- `tools/tandem_eval.py --resume` (OPS-63) continues an interrupted night: only what has no record runs, an errored record is kept aside and run again under a new tag, the store is cleared first, `night.json` keeps the night's build and each resume, and the report says so (`resumed`).
- The box keeps a suite report whose night carries a suffix (`2026-10-01-r2`; 0.3.7-test refused it with a 422), and `GET /v1/conductor/evals` marks a report a later one supersedes (`superseded_by`). The Compare screen shows turns and thinking tokens per suite and arm, labels a superseded report and shows the newest one nothing replaced first.

## 0.3.7-test, 2026-10-01

0.3.6-test plus the engine's memory limits (OPS-47), the narrow drafter arm as a switch (SPD-75), branch tandem-cache-limits, and the eval reader fix with a fresh-text live_check (OPS-63), branch tandem-evalfix. The design decisions of 2026-10-01: a 70 GiB ceiling, a 77 GiB declared peak, capped caches, a parked session; the context window stays 262,144.

- One memory policy for the serving caches (`engine/cache.py` `Budget`). Between requests the engine holds at most `MEM_CEILING_GIB` (70), allocated plus the allocator's reserve; during a prefill at most `MEM_PEAK_GIB` (77). Before a prefill and before the response starts, the free blocks go back to the driver and then the caches, cheapest first (state store, body anchors, guest stash, parked session, pinned head), until the prefill's workspace fits; if it still does not, the request gets a 503 with Retry-After instead of running the box into its out-of-memory wedge. Every cache allocation asks first and may take the room of the cheaper ones. After a request the reserve over `RESERVE_SLACK_GIB` (2) goes back to the driver. Measured in a hold: steady state 67.25 GiB with every cache filled, a 261,611-token prompt peaking at 68.35 GiB allocated, nothing shed.
- The caches' caps: resident anchors 2.5 GiB (17), guest stash 1.0 GiB for guests up to 8,192 tokens, pinned head 4.0 GiB (no longer out of `CACHE_GB`), state store 2 GiB with a 1 GiB entry (room is made before the clone, not after), and the parked session, 4 GiB: when a request of another session (`x-session-id`) replaces the resident prompt, its rows past the shared head are kept, and that session's next turn swaps them back instead of re-reading them (measured: 41,984 of 53,209 tokens reused, 11,225 re-read in 16.4 s). A compaction drops its session's store entries and parked rows. Every limit decides only where a prefill starts; resumes from the park are bit-identical to a cold prefill (tests).
- The residency planner subtracts the engine's growth to its declared peak (77 less what it holds now) before a role's claim, not just today's MemAvailable: at 37.9 GiB free with the engine at 70, a 12 GiB reader is refused (18.9 left) where it was admitted.
- Every limit is a key in `ops/serve.env` (`MEM_CEILING_GIB`, `MEM_PEAK_GIB`, `RESERVE_SLACK_GIB`, `RESIDENT_GB`, `RESIDENT_STASH_GB`, `RESIDENT_GUEST_MAX`, `RESIDENT_PIN_GB`, `RESIDENT_PARK_GB`, `CACHE_GB` 8 to 2, `STORE_ENTRY_GB`, `NARROW_ARM`), passed by `ops/start.sh`. The System view's Memory plan panel shows each with what it holds now, draws the ceiling and the peak over the split bar, keeps the shed log and the last session switch's re-read cost, and edits them as the residency document's `engine` section: live keys apply at the next request, `PREFIX_CHUNK` and `NARROW_ARM` say they need a restart, `MAX_LEN` is locked. Metrics `qse_memory_bytes{part}`, `qse_memory_shed_total{level}`, `qse_requests_refused_total{reason="memory"}`. Contracts: additive.
- `--narrow-arm off` (`NARROW_ARM=0`, SPD-75): the block-16 drafter alone, valid only with `QWEN38_LEN_MODE=wide`, about 8 GiB less. Off by default. A design decision (2026-10-01 20:25): keep the narrow arm, `NARROW_ARM=1` is served; the switch stays an option. The same-hour comparison is in SPD-75.
- `tools/mem_gate.py` (the 262k memory gate for a hold), `tools/verify_spec.py --narrow-arm`, `tools/forced_bench.py` `_nn` configs.

From tandem-evalfix (tools only, nothing the engine serves changes):

- `tools/tandem_eval.py` reads a run right (OPS-63). Round 1 (2026-10-01) published spiral and photo3d as failed on both arms, with 0 tokens, 0 turns and one needed continuation on every run; a separate checker's runs on the final shots passed all four. The causes: `opencode export` was read through a pipe, and opencode 1.18.33 exits before a pipe has taken more than 64 KiB, so every export ended at 65,536 bytes, did not parse and read as nothing (it now goes to a file; an export that cannot be read gives null counts and says why, never 0); the image suites had no check of their own, so with nothing read no gate passed (spiral and photo3d now check the last stage's shot, `final_shot` in the suites file: `s4-animated.png`, and `final.png` or the highest of S7/S6/S5 in any case, never a heatmap, an hourly shot or `s4-mid.png`; the check's metric lines are kept with its verdict); and the continuation count was taken before the final check, so a passed run counted one (now: one each time opencode ended in time with the suite not done).
- `--report DIR --reread` rebuilds a night from its run folders, the sessions and the engine ledger, keeps the night's own build (`--build`, else the night's report.json) instead of the build the server serves by then, names the published report it replaces (`--supersedes`), and keeps the replaced report and run records beside the new ones. The report's markdown gets a per-run table. Schema: optional `reader`, `final_check.shot` and `metrics`, `supersedes`, `superseded_by`.
- `tools/live_check.py` sends new text on every run: four seeded stories with the run's nonce in the prompt and in the answer (`--seed` repeats a run). Its fixed prompts had been learned by the persistent suffix store, so on 0.3.6-test no request decoded long enough for the live decode-rate check.

A test build for the box, not tagged: 0.3.4-test plus the supervisor in the Live view and the residency planner (branch tandem-p2-views).

- The supervisor where the dashboard is watched (VIS-44): the Live view's Now line keeps a line for the running request's last supervisor action ("Supervisor: closed the reasoning at 2,880 tokens (D1, score 0.93)", or what a shadow decision would have done); each request row, live and in the Dev tab, has a badge with its actions (filled) or shadow decisions (outlined) that opens a drawer with every decision from the conductor's journal; the header shows the session monitor's mode; the Conductor view's session gets one wall-clock axis with every turn, the monitor's actions, the router's notes, the compactions and the checker results, and Tier 1's shadow agreement once there is any. Live 1.2 adds `shadow` and the decisions' `score`, `tier` and `at_tokens`; the live engine block and the summary add the monitor's mode; a `requests` row adds `conductor`; `GET /v1/conductor/events?request=`. All additive; a server without the monitor shows none of it.
- Residency planning (OPS-41): the engine reports where its memory goes (`memory.split` in `/v1/dashboard/system`: weights, KV pool, GDN state, the drafters' context caches, vision, the state store, the resident prefix, the rest and the allocator's reserve, and each load stage's share, also printed as a `[memory]` line at start). The residency planner decides what may load beside the engine (floor 15 GiB plus a 6 GiB margin, claims at their peak, one load at a time, never during a hold), journals every decision, and is edited in the dashboard as the conductor's `residency` document; `GET /v1/conductor/residency/plan` and the System view's memory plan show it. `ops/roles.sh` loads roles in that order (none configured today), with vLLM roles held to BF16 and the planner's memory fraction; `hold.sh` stops the roles first and waits a settle time after a stop.
- C2's allowlist (SRV-113): the project-rules check takes `allow_paths`, path patterns no C2 rule applies to (a path covers everything under it; `*`, `?` and `[` make a glob; `~` is home; a relative entry is under the project root). The default is opencode's own scratch, `/tmp/opencode`, which opencode's tool texts send the model to and which the /tmp/ rule flagged; a monitor document saved before the key existed gets the default. It is a field of C2 on the Conductor view's Monitor screen, which shows the default for a document that leaves the key out. The policy file is version 4.
- Changed behaviour: a streamed request with `stop` strings and tools no longer streams a call's arguments while the model writes them; each call goes out whole when its block closes. A stop string can end the generation inside a `<tool_call>` block, and the arguments already sent could not be taken back: the client was left with a call whose JSON never closed (`{"filePath": "src/a.js`), beside the block's text. The release 658b5fb did the same; the harness did not add it. Now such a block is the text it was, as the non-streamed answer already had it, and no call goes out. Requests without stop strings stream as before. A call the token limit cuts still streams half its arguments with the monitor raw (SRV-47); with a tool-call check able to act it gives up as before.
- The speed guard's result for a build (`tools/speed_guard.py`): two row3 reports of the same hour become a `speed_guard` report in the conductor's `evals/` directory, with the build the server serves, the medians, the deltas and the verdict by row3's rule. One run a side gives `no_noise_estimate`: row3's rule reads every one-run difference as resolved, and the report says instead that the noise is unknown and the row decides nothing. The Conductor view's guard line and the Compare screen show the result for the serving build (a note for a one-run short gate, with mean, TTFT and ms a block; a warning for none, a resolved-worse one, or one recorded for other code) instead of "speed guard not run" for every build.

A block the parser cannot read is repaired when the fix is not a guess, else the model writes the calls again after a hidden reminder with the parser's reason (two times a request, then content as before); the same call a third time after two identical results is written again too ("do something different"); risk floors (rm -rf outside the project root, git push, writes outside the root, a download piped into a shell) and AGENTS.md rules (numbered copies, /tmp paths, files over 400 lines) are journaled in shadow; a call the token limit cut gives up rather than going out as half a call. Every pattern, limit and reminder is in the policy file, and each profile turns the four packs on or off. With the shipped policy and a tool-call task able to act, a call arrives whole at the end of the answer instead of streaming its values; with the monitor raw nothing changes.
